author: akesson
body:
Full-discipline completion of the post-refactoring cleanup (PR6 from the approved plan). Extends the 500-line `file-size` rule to the whole workspace with **no expect directives**, and makes **both** `file-size` and `crate-size` measure production code only.

## What changed

**Part A — `file-size` counts production source only.** Hoisted the shipped-source counter out of `crate_size/` to `lints::shipped_source` and added a per-file breakdown for `file-size`. `.rs` files matched by a rule now exclude `#[cfg(test)]` items, `#[test]`/`#[wasm_bindgen_test]` fns, out-of-line `#[cfg(test)] mod x;` files, and `tests`/`benches`/`examples` trees — the same definition `crate-size` uses, so the two budgets agree to the line. Non-Rust globs keep tokei's raw count.

**Latent bug fixed in the shared counter.** The old approach blanked test lines in place before one tokei parse, which severed tokei's stateful string scanner around a `'"'`-style char literal (e.g. `s.trim_matches('"')`) and leaked whole test blocks back into the count — it inflated this repo's own `module_tree.rs` by ~450 lines, and silently affected `crate-size` too. Now the production complement is counted in one self-contained buffer; the source is never modified. Verified identical on all existing unit tests, plus a new regression test.

**Part B — split `resolve/module_tree.rs`** (1900 lines) into a directory module: `occurrences` / `items` / `uses` / `tests`, with `mod.rs` keeping the walk. Pure movement, gated byte-stable by `oracle.rs` + `scip_diff.rs`. The `git mv` is its own commit so the carve shows only line moves.

**Part C — split `resolve/mod.rs`** (1400 lines) into `types` / `model` / `workspace` / `queries` / `tests`, with `mod.rs` a re-export facade. The crate-root public surface is unchanged. The only semantic edit: `Workspace`'s fields are `pub(super)` so the sibling `queries` impl can read them.

**Part D — extend the rule.** `file-size` now covers `crates/*/src/**/*.rs`. Every `src/` file is under 500 shipped lines, no exceptions.

## Consequences worth noting

- Removing messages.rs's now-stale `expect!(file_size)` left `workspace-lint-marker` unused by the binary, so that dependency is dropped (the tool itself flagged it).
- Corrected shipped totals: syn-workspace ~3.7k, workspace-lint ~5.4k. workspace-lint is now the binding crate against the 6000 crate-size budget — worth watching as lints are added.

## Verification

`cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo test --doc`, oracle + scip_diff (byte-stable), `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo doc -D warnings`, `cargo publish --dry-run -p syn-workspace`, and `cargo run -p workspace-lint` (clean on its own repo) all pass.

author: michaelcrosato
body:
## What this does (plain English)

This is a **tooling fix for our own release step** (no product code). When a session finishes a feature, it opens a pull request and then runs a helper that waits for the automated checks to pass before merging. There's a brief moment right after a pull request is created where the checks haven't appeared yet, and the helper used to mistake "checks haven't shown up yet" for "checks failed." A person had to notice and re-run it by hand (it happened twice).

This change makes the helper **wait patiently for the checks to show up first**, then watch them to the finish — and, importantly, if checks *never* show up, it **refuses to merge** rather than guessing. An unchecked change can never slip through as if it passed.

## How to see it

Nothing to click — this is behind-the-scenes release machinery. You'll feel it as **fewer stalled releases** that need a manual nudge.

## What could be risky

- The one thing that must never happen is merging something before its checks pass. This change was reviewed specifically for that and **fails safe**: in every edge case it either waits or refuses — it never merges early. An automated security review confirmed this.
- Two timing settings were added; a typo in either now stops with a clear message instead of hanging.

## Machine checks

- `bash scripts/verify.sh` — **PASS** (typecheck, lint, build, 115 internal safety-net tests incl. 5 new ones for this exact behavior, assertion shield). Evidence: `roadmap/evidence/kaizen-ship-register-wait/verify.log`.
- Security review of the merge-tool change: **APPROVE** (cardinal risk — merging an unchecked change — found unreachable by any input or setting).

author: dip686
body:
Based on Electron GitHub issues analysis (11849, 39959, 40749, 47946):

1. backgroundColor '#00ffffff' instead of '#00000000'
   - Transparent black causes white flash on navigation/reload on Windows
   - Transparent white avoids the DWM rendering artifact

2. app.disableHardwareAcceleration() on Windows only
   - Prevents WM_NCACTIVATE from triggering non-client area (titlebar) rendering via DWM compositing
   - Known Electron bug that has regressed multiple times (PR #40749)
   - Only applied on win32 to avoid affecting macOS

3. 1px position offset on Windows
   - Windows incorrectly detects windows at exact screen edges as "maximized", causing opaque background rendering
   - 1px offset prevents this detection

## Why

The README was strong on the form-field wrapper but **under-sold several shipped, public features** and carried a **stale "experimental" claim**. A follow-up docs audit (reader-tested with fresh-context agents) extended the same pass across the package READMEs and `docs/` guides: broken npm-facing links, the cascade never reaching the npm README, buried when/why guidance, and no distilled best-practices anywhere. These are additive doc edits — no runtime API changes (one `package.json` metadata field).

## What

### Root README (first 3 commits)

- **`### How settings resolve (the cascade)`** — names the precedence chain (`input ?? form context ?? component config ?? app config ?? default`) and the per-key nullish-merge rule. Several later sections now point back to it instead of re-explaining resolution.
- **`## Warnings that don't block submit`** — closes the biggest functional gap. `warningError` + `submitWithWarnings`/`canSubmitWithWarnings`, using the canonical `validate(path, ctx => …)` idiom, plus a helper table.
- **`### Per-component overrides`** — the `…ForComponent` providers (config, presets, renderers) as the cascade's payoff: override one key, inherit the rest.
- **Stability reconciled** in `README.md` and `COMPATIBILITY.md`: Signal Forms is **stable as of Angular 22** (`@publicApi 22.0`). The intentional `<23.0.0` peer ceiling is kept but re-justified on major-version API-risk grounds.
- **demo-primeng surfaced** (table row, FAQ, Resources) and the control-presets pointer sharpened.

### Docs audit follow-up (commits 4–9)

- **npm-facing link fixes** — `../../docs/…` links in the package READMEs break on npmjs.com (`docs/` isn't published); in `form-field/` and `vest/` they were also one level short and broken *on GitHub*. Now absolute GitHub URLs. The npm README gains live-demo + full-docs links up top.
- **`repository.directory` added to `packages/toolkit/package.json`** — without it, npm rewrites relative README links against the repo *root*, breaking every intra-package link (`./form-field/README.md` → top-level path). Root-cause fix for relative links on npmjs.com.
- **Cascade propagated beyond the root README** — the npm README now documents the full precedence chain (it previously described only the `skipSelf` merge semantics); sister guides cross-link each other (`ANGULAR_VS_TOOLKIT` ↔ `WARNINGS_SUPPORT` / `VALIDATION_STRATEGY`; `COMPLEX_NESTED_FORMS` names strategy inheritance as a cascade tier).
- **When/why framing leads the guides** — `ANGULAR_VS_TOOLKIT` gets an explicit "when to reach for / when to skip" list with the side-by-side comparison ahead of directive mechanics; `WARNINGS_SUPPORT` gets "when a warning is the wrong tool" (error vs warning vs hint); `CUSTOM_CONTROLS` gets a pick-in-ten-seconds interface guide and promotes the silent template-local-imports gotcha out of the FAQ; the form-field README gets a which-surface decision matrix and a required-vs-inherited inputs note.
- **`docs/BEST_PRACTICES.md` (new)** — five practices derived from the toolkit's two design commitments (additive + cascade-driven), each with do/don't/why and deep links, plus a review checklist. The root README carries the one-line versions before the FAQ.
- **`PACKAGE_ARCHITECTURE.md` hygiene** — audience note (contributors, not adopters), entry-point table de-duplicated to one maintained copy, and the consumer consequence of the internal `/core` boundary spelled out.

### Public-API audit (commits 10–12)

A barrel-vs-README diff of every entry point against its docs:

- **Two doc-vs-source defects fixed** — the headless notification directive's documented `exportAs` was wrong (`notification` → actual `notificationState`), and the wrapper inputs table omitted the `orientation` input.
- **README↔barrel lockstep restored** — `index.ts` declares the package README as the public-API ledger, but ~25 value exports had no README presence. Added: error-visibility additions (`createErrorVisibility`, `readDirectErrors`), a strategy/context-resolution section, message-resolution functions, a custom error/hint **renderer** section (tokens + providers), control-semantics utilities, an advanced DI-tokens table (all 8 public tokens), and a companion-types ledger note. The headless README now documents its re-exported custom-wrapper ARIA factory suite and field-optionality helpers.
- **Hygiene** — PACKAGE_ARCHITECTURE layout diagram refreshed against the real tree (stale `assistive-row.ts` dropped; six missing files/dirs added), headless most-used list completed, hint `position` input and vest adapter companion types documented.

## Verification

- All referenced exports verified against the public barrels (`packages/toolkit/index.ts`, headless, assistive); `warningError` imports normalized to the canonical root path.
- Reader-tested with fresh-context agents: every new anchor/link verified to resolve; adoption-decision questions answerable from the docs alone; no contradictions found between the README summary and the full best-practices guide.
- Stability status verified against `@angular/forms` v22 `@publicApi 22.0` types.
- oxfmt re-run via lint-staged on every commit.

## Summary

The per-language **test badges** in `README.md` and `docs/index.md` were switched to
GitHub-native `badge.svg` in #546. Those workflows only trigger on `pull_request`
(never on the default branch), so the native badge has **zero runs on `main`** and
renders **"no status"** (looks broken) even though every PR run passes. The
`update_badge` gist for each language — updated on every run — still holds the correct
`passing` / `failing` status.

This restores the gist-endpoint badges and fixes a related path-filter typo so the
gist actually refreshes when the workflow file changes.

## Changes

- **`README.md` / `docs/index.md`** — point all **19 language test badges** back to the
  shields.io gist endpoint (`.../raw/<lang>-test-badge.json&cacheSeconds=0`), the
  pre-#546 form. The gist is updated on every workflow run (`update_badge`, `if: always()`),
  so the badge always reflects the real latest result instead of "no status".
  **Sample-workflow badges keep native `badge.svg`** — they have `schedule` +
  `workflow_dispatch`, so they do run on the default branch and the native badge works.
- **`go` / `nodejs` / `python` / `ruby` / `rust` `_test.yml`** — fix the `paths:` filter
  from the nonexistent `.github/json2vars-setter/<lang>_test.yml` to
  `.github/workflows/<lang>_test.yml`. Without this, editing the workflow itself (e.g. a
  Dependabot setup-action SHA bump) did **not** trigger a run, so a break introduced there
  was never reflected in the badge. The other 13 languages already used the correct path;
  also removed a duplicate path line in `nodejs_test.yml`.

## Notes

- No `schedule` is added (per the chosen direction): the gist endpoint already reflects
  every PR run. Upstream drift between PRs is therefore not auto-detected; a
  `workflow_dispatch` / `schedule` could be added later if desired.

author: joergzeidler
body:
## Summary

Reclassifies every `resize_if_needed` failure as non-fatal, except `FsckRequiresReboot` which still triggers a controlled reboot via Plan A's recovery policy.

**Changes:**
- `OdsStatus` gains `resize_data: Option<ResizeStatus>` (absent on happy path)
- `ResizeOutcome` enum (`skipped_fsck` | `tool_error` | `invalid_layout`) with snake_case serialization
- `InitSetupCtx` gains `ods_status: &mut OdsStatus` (3rd lifetime) so initial_setup steps can record status indicators
- `resize_data::run` absorbs all errors except `FsckRequiresReboot`; records indicator in `ods_status`
- `recovery_class` gets `ResizeData(Filesystem(FsckRequiresReboot)) → RebootToApply` arm before the catch-all
- Guard semantics unchanged; `omnect_resized_data` is only written on full success

## Reason

Previously any resize failure on a release image caused an infinite halt loop (no watchdog → potential brick). This makes resize a true best-effort preflight step: failures are surfaced to ODS for cloud notification instead of stopping boot.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-27-fsck-and-resize-design.md`

## Verification

All feature-combination test runs pass (174 unit + 12 integration tests for grub; 175 + 5 for uboot). `cargo fmt -- --check` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean for `grub,gpt` and `grub,gpt,resize-data,release-image`.

body:
## What

The Authorization Code grant helper was split across two scripts that handed the code off through a `.auth_code` file:

- `oauth_authcode_step1.py` — build the authorize URL, capture the browser redirect, write `.auth_code`
- `oauth_authcode_step2.py` — read `.auth_code`, exchange the code for tokens

This merges them into **`scripts/oauth/oauth_authcode.py`**, passing the code straight to `exchange_code_for_token(code, ...)` instead of round-tripping it through a file.

## Why it's also a testability win

Consolidating pulled the previously-inline logic into pure, testable functions — `build_auth_url`, `extract_code` (with its CSRF state guard), and `exchange_code_for_token`. Added **`tests/test_oauth_authcode.py`** covering:

- code extraction on a valid redirect (happy path)
- state-mismatch rejection (CSRF guard)
- missing-code error
- the authorize-URL parameter contract

These paths had **no** unit tests when the logic lived inline across the two scripts.

## Other changes

- Renamed `oauth_authcode_step3.py` → `oauth_authcode_refresh.py` so the pair reads coherently now that there are no numbered steps.
- Updated `docs/TESTING.md`, `oauth/README.md`, and the `test_audit_live.py` docstring to the new script names.

## Coverage note

The `auth/prelogin` and token-exchange **spec** paths remain covered by the live suite (`tests/test_oauth_integration_live.py` — separate `test_prelogin_happy_path`, `test_authorize_happy_path`, `test_token_auth_code_grant_*` cases). The helper scripts were never the source of that coverage, so collapsing them loses nothing.

Full suite: **431 passed, 134 skipped** (live).

author: aetherlogosprime-architect
body:
## Summary

Closes correction #53 — the PUSH-WRAPPER-FALSE-POSITIVE that fired ~10 times across 2026-06-10 / 2026-06-11 sessions, burning hours of cycles on phantom-success pushes that hadn't actually landed.

## What it does

- `scripts/divineos_push.sh` — drop-in `git push` wrapper:
  - Runs `git push "$@"` without piping (preserves exit code)
  - Verifies post-push via `git ls-remote` (catches silent-divergence)
  - Prints `[divineos-push] result: exit=N (STATE)` as LAST line so even truncated output shows truth
- `tests/test_divineos_push_wrapper.sh` — 4 tests covering exit-code propagation, failure-mode propagation, tail-truncation survival, and ls-remote-step presence.

## Why structural beats discipline

Behavioral fix ("always run git ls-remote after every push") is what I did manually all session and it burned cycles every time. The structural fix means: any push routed through the wrapper carries its own truth in the last line, so the next pass — mine or anyone's — sees the real result without remembering to check.

## Dogfood evidence

This PR's own push was made using the new wrapper. Final-status line on that push: `[divineos-push] result: exit=0 (PUSHED+VERIFIED)`, SHA confirmed against origin in the same call.

## Not changing yet (deferred)

The harness's default git push invocation still ships unchanged; this PR adds the tool. A follow-up will add a hook or convention that prefers the wrapper for in-session pushes.

author: zyrtnin
body:
Finishes the **Tier-1 developer on-ramp** and updates our Radiant-Core baseline to the latest release (**v3.1.1**, 2026-06-10). Also lands a sanitized public `docs/ROADMAP.md` + the Tier-1 sprint plan.

## Context
PR #185 already shipped the on-ramp's S1–S6; verifying the North Star this session surfaced the real remaining gaps. The dev regtest needs a `radiant-core:*-amd64` image, but **no Dockerfile was committed** — the old v2.3.0 image was built ad-hoc, so a fresh `pip install` dev couldn't obtain it (the funnel leak). And we were three releases behind, across v3.1.x's `SCRIPT_SECURITY_UPGRADE` soft fork (active on regtest from genesis), which re-opens the covenant's regtest consensus validation.

## What's here

**A — Committed image + one-command setup**
- `docker/regtest.Dockerfile` wraps the **official** Radiant-Core release daemon (SHA-256-verified against the release checksum file) on `ubuntu:22.04` (chosen to satisfy the binary's Boost 1.74 + GLIBC 2.34 needs — measured via `ldd`/`objdump`).
- `pyrxd regtest setup [--version vX.Y.Z] [--no-cache]` builds it from a Dockerfile **embedded in `pyrxd.devnet`**, so a pip-installed dev with no checkout can build it too. A drift-guard test keeps the embedded copy byte-identical to the committed file. The missing-image error now points at `regtest setup`.

**B — Bump to v3.1.1, measured GREEN (not assumed)**
Built `radiant-core:v3.1.1-amd64` and ran the consensus-sensitive suites against it:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_spv_covenant_differential_regtest.py` (nBits ceiling, bin2num sig-bytes, OP_OUTPUTVALUE arity, sentinel, 20-level branch) | **21 passed — identical** under the soft fork |
| `test_htlc_regtest_e2e.py` + `test_soulbound_covenant_regtest.py` | **6 passed** |
| BTC↔RXD `test_xchain_swap_regtest_e2e.py` | **10 passed** |
| ETH↔RXD `test_xchain_eth_swap_regtest_e2e.py` | **7 passed** (after fixing an orthogonal pre-existing breakage — see below) |
| North Star quickstart mint | **green on v3.1.1** |

The soft fork's per-script stack budget is **64 MB** (v3.1.1 release notes); the covenant uses kilobytes — hence no rejection. Pinned v3.1.1 across `devnet.py`, the regtest suites, and dev-facing docs.

> **Orthogonal fix included:** `test_xchain_eth_swap_regtest_e2e.py` predated #192's MEDIUM-1 guard and never set `accept_estimated_eth_margins=True`, so it had been red since #192 (not in default CI, so it slipped). Fixed with the same explicit opt-in #192 applied to the dust harnesses. **Not** a bump regression.

**C — CI North Star gate**
New `quickstart` job in `ci.yml`: builds the image from the committed Dockerfile, runs `pip → regtest up → mint a Glyph → assert confirmed`, then the RXD covenant consensus suites — so the quickstart **and** covenant validation can't silently rot between releases (closes the sprint's "verified in CI" DoD).

**D — Testnet how-to**
`docs/how-to/use-the-public-testnet.md`: when to graduate from regtest to the public testnet, how to run `radiantd -testnet`, point pyrxd at it, and get coins. Honest about reliability — regtest is the dependable path; the community testnet faucet is best-effort (it returned a gateway error when checked 2026-06-11, while the mainnet faucet was up).

Plus: `quickstart.md` gains a "Step 0 — build the image" and drops the manual image prerequisite; `ROADMAP.md` is sanitized for the public repo (private exploration codenames → generic capability categories).

## Verification
`task ci` green: **4132 passed**, 86 skipped; lint / format / typecheck / private-links all clean (verified independently — the local coverage gate is the known fresh-worktree double-count artifact, not a regression; CI runs on a clean checkout). All regtest measurements above ran locally against `radiant-core:v3.1.1-amd64` built from the committed Dockerfile.

## Bug
Dopo il restyle, nella modalità "per destinazione" il dropdown città si apriva ma **non era possibile selezionare una città**.

## Causa
Il redesign assegna `z-index:2` a `.form-area` (crea uno *stacking context*). Il `.dropdown-backdrop` è `position:fixed; z-index:90`: l'intero blocco form — col pannello città dentro — finiva **sotto** il backdrop, quindi i tap sulle voci colpivano il backdrop, che chiude il menu.

## Fix
Mentre il dropdown è aperto, `.form-area` viene elevata sopra il backdrop (`z-index:95`) e ripristinata alla chiusura. Applicato a `index.html` e `weekend.html`. Nessun'altra modifica.

- `cityDropdownInput` è dentro `.form-card#formDest` → dentro `.form-area`, quindi `closest('.form-area')` risolve correttamente.

- Wires all three boolean preference toggles (push notifications, weekly report, data sharing) to `PUT /users/me/preferences` with optimistic update and revert on failure
- Expands `updatePreferences()` to accept all four preference fields as nullable named params; uses `@EncodeDefault(NEVER)` so only changed fields are sent (backend uses Go pointer semantics — nil = no-op)
- Bootstrap block on sign-in reads all four prefs from backend and seeds any missing fields with a single batched PUT

## Bugs fixed (caught in code review)

- **Invisible snackbar** — toggle-failure errors were queued to `AtmosApp`'s `SnackbarHost`, hidden beneath `ProfileScreen`'s own `Scaffold`; errors now route via an `onError` callback to `ProfileScreen`'s visible snackbar
- **Rapid toggle race** — double-tapping a toggle spawned concurrent PUTs with a broken `prev` chain; each toggle now cancels its previous in-flight job before launching a new one
- **`CancellationException` swallowed by `runCatching`** — cancelling a toggle job triggered a false-positive revert; `updatePreferences` now re-throws `CancellationException` via `.also { }`
- **Bootstrap scope escape** — `else` branches used `scope.launch` (outer composition scope), allowing PUT requests to fire after sign-out against a stale token; replaced with a single batched `launch { }` bound to the `supervisorScope`

## Test plan

- [ ] Toggle Push Notifications on/off — switch persists after app restart; snackbar shows on network failure and toggle reverts
- [ ] Toggle Weekly Report and Data Sharing — same as above
- [ ] Rapid double-tap a toggle — final state matches last tap; no spurious error snackbar
- [ ] Sign in on a fresh account — bootstrap PUT fires once; all four preference fields appear on backend
- [ ] Sign in, immediately sign out before bootstrap completes — no PUT fires against old session token

body:
💡 What: Refactored the `LetterGlitch` canvas rendering loop. Instead of checking a random condition for every cell to decide if it should be updated, it now pre-calculates the required number of updates and selects a cell at random to apply it.
🎯 Why: The original implementation performed an O(N) loop iterating over the grid size (e.g. 14,000 times for 1080p resolution) each frame and triggering `Math.random()`. This causes heavy CPU usage.
📊 Impact: Reduces evaluation time in the tight loop. Benchmark shows a performance difference going from ~2.8s to ~210ms over 10000 iterations (a ~90% decrease in overhead).
🔬 Measurement: Reviewing the benchmark script or observing CPU load reduction when leaving the tab open for an extended period.

body:
## Summary
Model fix **#1** — the big one. A municipality can now require a **different set of steps**, not just different fees. `procedures`, `dependencies` and `rules` carry an optional `municipality_id` (`NULL` = national); the catalog **layers** them — national rows always apply, a municipality's own rows apply only to projects in that municipality (SPEC 3.1).

## Why this is clean
The proven **RuleEngine / ScheduleEngine are unchanged.** The layering is pure data filtering in the catalog, and a municipal `include` rule pulls a municipal procedure into the graph exactly like any other rule — it can also `exclude` a national step or `switch_institution`, per municipality. So the etalon engine logic stays frozen.

## Changes
- **models + migration** — `municipality_id` on `core.procedures` / `dependencies` / `rules` (FK to municipalities, named constraints; the spurious `alembic_version` drop removed).
- **catalog** — `load_catalog(db, municipality_id)` filters the three to `municipality_id IS NULL OR == <project's>`.
- **recalc** — passes `project.municipality_id` (the project is the single source of truth).

## Test plan
Verified locally:
- `smoke_municipal_graph`: a Варна-only procedure (added by a Варна `include` rule, with a Варна dependency) appears for a **Варна project → 14 steps** but **not** for a **national project → 13**; national total stays **420 days**
- engine tests **10/10**; recalc / sections / municipal-fees / schedule-edit smokes green — **etalon untouched** (seed is all national → national catalog → 420 / 39 870 / 11.8%)

## Where this leaves us
With #19 (fee resolution) + this, the model can express the real per-municipality differences in **steps, approvals and costs** — the prerequisite you asked about, for entering real data across all municipalities.

## Next enablers (not in this PR)
- **Admin API + CSV import for procedures/rules/dependencies** — there's no way to *enter* municipal graph data yet (only acts/tariffs admin exists). This is the next thing to build so you can start inputting real data.
- Documents / `procedure_inputs` (the "what documents are needed" dimension, gap #3).
- Richer rules (compound conditions, conditional-add, чл.137 category as a driver — gap #4).

author: swordofmorning
body:
PR Summary by Qodo

Move GFL farm GitHub Actions workflow from Windows to Ubuntu ⚙️ Configuration changes ✨ Enhancement 🕐 10-20 Minutes

Walkthroughs

Description 
• Switch the farm job runner from Windows to Ubuntu for faster, cheaper execution.
• Make the respawn-flag detection step Linux-compatible by replacing PowerShell with bash.
• Harden matrix JSON output formatting to be single-line and space-free for GHA outputs.
Diagram
```mermaid graph TD A["GHA: gfl_farm.yml"] --> B["prepare job"] --> C["matrix JSON output"] --> D["farm job (Ubuntu)"] --> E["Run GFL Agent"] --> F{"respawn.flag exists?"} --> G["Upload respawn artifacts"] --> H["Trigger next workflow (gh)"] F -->|"yes"| G F -->|"no"| G G --> H subgraph Legend direction LR _wf["Workflow/Job"] ~~~ _step["Step"] ~~~ _dec{"Decision"} end ```
High-Level Assessment
The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Keep Windows runner and only fix output formatting - ➕ Avoids Linux shell portability work and runner-specific differences - ➕ Lowest behavioral change risk if the agent is Windows-tuned - ➖ Does not achieve the primary performance/cost goal - ➖ Continues dependence on pwsh scripting patterns
2. Extract respawn logic into a reusable composite action - ➕ Centralizes shell/OS handling and reduces workflow YAML complexity - ➕ Easier to test and reuse across workflows - ➖ More up-front structure for a small amount of logic - ➖ Adds another moving part to version and maintain
**Recommendation:** The current approach (move the farm job to ubuntu-latest and convert the respawn check to bash) is the most direct way to realize the performance goal while keeping workflow structure unchanged. A composite action is worth considering only if the repo has multiple workflows that need identical respawn/flag orchestration.

File Changes

Ensures the generated matrix output JSON is strictly single-line and space-free for GITHUB_OUTPUT, and replaces a PowerShell-based file existence check with an equivalent bash check for respawn flags. Adds clarifying comments around secrets passing and workflow dispatch locking.

author: mildtomato
body:
## What changed

~20 new canvas pattern experiments, all reachable from the page menu:

**Pills** — Features wall (Stripe-Sessions-style feature pills with wipe transitions), Rows Color, Rows Features, Rows Blocks (multi-slot span pills that manifest over uniform dashes), Rows Neon (custom palettes)
**Text art** — Rows (ASCII density shading), Shapes / Intercept / Intercept Grain (large repeated-character forms cutting into the glyph field), Fluid (metaball masses), Geo (SDF primitives — triangle/circle/square/hexagon — with fully randomized attributes, layer toggles, periodic re-render), Liquid (a real Stable Fluids / Navier-Stokes solver driving the glyph grid — stir with the cursor, click to splat)
**Dither** — Grain / Grain Earth / Grain Green (per-pixel stochastic film-grain gradients), Rows Bloom (gradient ramps + glow), Rows Cut (vertical-slice collage)
**Other** — Dot Panels (perforated-sheet mosaic), Orbit Points (3D billboard starburst with orbiting camera)

## Shared infrastructure

`components/PatternControls.tsx` centralizes:
- Per-theme (light/dark) palettes with live color pickers, save/load/delete, copy + paste as JSON, and baked-in presets that survive any localStorage/origin change
- Animation settings: tween / step / slide modes, speed, row drift, ease, steps
- `usePersisted` hook — every page-local control (shape attributes, text size, liquid params, layer visibility, re-render interval) survives reloads
- The dither rows family and pill pages all consume the same store, so palettes follow you across pages; they also now respect the light/dark toggle

## Notes for review

- All rendering is hand-rolled canvas 2D — no new dependencies. Hot paths use sprite caches (pre-rendered glyphs/text/dots) after profiling showed per-frame `fillText` at ~4.5k cells dropped PillGrid to 12fps; it now runs 85–120fps
- The liquid page implements Jos Stam's Stable Fluids (advection, 12-iter pressure projection, vorticity confinement) at 128×72, sampled bilinearly by the glyph grid
- `.claude/launch.json` and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` intentionally left untracked
- Typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) passes; pages verified in the browser preview throughout

author: nvdigitalsolutions
body:
## Summary

Fixes two moderate security vulnerabilities in the transitive `guzzlehttp/psr7` dependency:

| CVE | Title | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-49214 | Host Confusion via Authority Reinterpretation | 2.10.2 |
| GHSA-34xg-wgjx-8xph | CRLF Injection via URI Host Component | 2.10.2 |

## Root Cause

`guzzlehttp/psr7` 2.9.0 (pulled transitively via `symfony/http-client` → `guzzlehttp/guzzle`) did not reject ASCII control characters, whitespace, or DEL in URI host components.

## Fix

Added `"guzzlehttp/psr7": "^2.10.2"` as a direct dependency in `composer.json`. This constrains the transitive dep to a patched version without conflicting with `guzzlehttp/guzzle`'s `^2.8` requirement. `composer update` resolves to `2.11.0` (latest).

## Changes

- `composer.json` — added `guzzlehttp/psr7: ^2.10.2` to `require`
- `composer.lock` — updated lock to reflect resolved version

author: laxels
body:
## Context

Every `ultraclaude-host-2` provision attempt since 2026-06-11 ~18:36 PDT failed at the "Creating M2-L server" step with a Python `JSONDecodeError` traceback in `hostEvents` instead of the real Scaleway API error. Nobody could tell from fleet events whether host-2 creation was failing on quota, auth, or something else.

## Root cause

`scw_api` prints HTTP error bodies to **stderr** and returns 1 with **empty stdout**. Callers piped its stdout straight into `json_get` or inline `python3`, which crashed on empty stdin with a `json.load` traceback. The traceback (~11 lines) flooded the hostagent's 8-line failure tail *and* Convex's 500-char summary cap (`convex/hosts.ts:218`), pushing the actual `ERROR: Scaleway API ...` line out of the `provision_failed` summary entirely.

## Fix (two layers)

1. **`scripts/provision-host.sh`** — capture `scw_api` output into a variable before parsing at all four call sites (never pipe it into a parser). Under `set -e` a failed call now stops the script with the clean ERROR line as the last output. `json_get` additionally fails with one clear `ERROR:` line on empty/invalid input instead of a traceback (defense in depth).
2. **`hostagent/src/hostProvision.ts`** — track the first `ERROR:`-prefixed line of bootstrap output and lead the `provision_failed` summary with it when the tail window has dropped it, so the root cause always survives the 500-char cap.

## Proof

**Failing test first** (TDD): new test reproduces the exact live shape — ERROR line followed by a traceback longer than the tail window. Pre-fix summary was 100% traceback; post-fix it leads with the ERROR line.

**Manual repro, pre-fix script** (bogus creds, read-only GET fails — nothing provisioned; last 15 lines all traceback, real error scrolled away):
```
  File ".../json/decoder.py", line 363, in raw_decode
    raise JSONDecodeError("Expecting value", s, err.value) from None
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

**Same run, fixed script** (exit 1, the clean error is the last line):
```
==> Resolving Scaleway project id
ERROR: Scaleway API GET /iam/v1alpha1/api-keys/SCWBOGUS... -> HTTP 401: {"message":"authentication is denied",...}
```

**`json_get` hardening**: empty stdin → `ERROR: json_get id: not JSON: empty input (upstream command failed?)` exit 1; HTML body → `ERROR: json_get id: not JSON: '<html>502 bad gateway</html>\n'` exit 1; valid JSON unchanged.

**Validation**: `bun run validate` green — typecheck 0, lint 0, 244 tests pass.

## Live failure identified (the original goal)

With visibility restored via host-1's hostagent log (`~/hostagent.log`, which keeps the full bootstrap output), the real error behind every recent attempt — including the latest — is:

```
ERROR: Scaleway API POST /apple-silicon/v1alpha1/zones/fr-par-1/servers -> HTTP 403:
{"details":[{"current":1,"quota":0,"resource":"AsServersType_M2_L"}],
 "message":"quota(s) exceeded for this resource","type":"quotas_exceeded"}
```

**Quota — not auth, not ratelimit.** Confirmed reads are healthy by hand from host-1 with the fleet creds: `GET .../servers` → HTTP 200 (only `ultraclaude-host-1` exists). The quota increase remains blocked on Axel's Scaleway support ticket.

body:
Scheduled tasks sent a static summary email on every run whenever
`notification_subscribers` was set — with no clear on/off, and a risk of two
emails per run when the prompt itself already asks to be emailed.

This makes the summary email an explicit opt-in, and never lets a single run
produce two emails: prompt asks to email/notify → the agent's `send_email`
tool handles it; prompt is silent → a static summary email goes to the creator.

**UI (`ScheduledPromptModal`)**
- Replaces the always-on subscriber box with an "Email a summary after each run"
  checkbox.
- Default is inferred from the prompt text (off when it already asks to
  email/notify, on otherwise) and stays user-overridable once toggled.
- Recipient defaults to the creator; subscriber picker shows only when checked;
  an amber hint appears when the prompt already sends email.
- Edit mode honors the saved setting instead of re-guessing.

**`create_scheduled_task` tool**
- Attaches the static summary email to the creator only when `task_prompt` has
  no email intent (was previously never attached).
- Tool/schema docs clarify email is automatic, and that writing email intent
  into the prompt is for *conditional* notifications handled by `send_email`.

**Shared / misc**
- New `prompt_requests_email()` heuristic (first-person intent, tuned to skip
  false positives like "summarize the emails in the queue") + unit tests.
- `promptSendsEmailHint` i18n key across all locales.

scheduled-task changes.

author: aspulse
body:
Adds temporal motion blur as a `MotionBlur` timeline component: each frame, the child is evaluated at N sub-clocks across a trailing shutter window `[t − shutter, t]` and the resulting frames are averaged on the GPU. A blurred frame is treated as a pure function of the shutter interval — each sample bakes its own state into the child's raster tree, so sub-frames memoize through the existing content-hash cache with no cache-key changes, and a static stretch short-circuits back to a single shared cache entry. The live preview gains a motion-blur toggle, and the demo scene gains a streak comet that showcases the effect. 17 files (+973 / −16) across `tellur-core`, `tellur-renderer`, `tellur-plugin`, and `tellur-live`.

## Motion blur engine (`tellur-core`, `tellur-renderer`)
- `Clock::shifted(dt)` shifts both time axes — the sampling primitive for temporal effects; `MotionBlur { shutter, samples, child }` wraps any `TimelineComponent` and averages its shutter samples.
- Cache coherence falls out of the existing design: animated stretches bake distinct per-sample states (own cache entries, shared across overlapping shutters), while static stretches collapse to one entry via a storage-identity short-circuit (`RasterImage::shares_storage`), costing the same as no blur.
- GPU accumulate/resolve compute kernels average in premultiplied u32 integer space and match the CPU fallback byte-for-byte (covered by a GPU smoke test); missing samples (a child absent for part of the shutter) count as transparent, so clips fade instead of brightening.

## Preview toggle (`tellur-live`)
- `RenderContext::motion_blur_enabled` (default on) is a policy signal like `gpu_preference`; the server threads a `motion_blur` query param through `/api/frame`, `/api/stream`, and `/api/video.mp4`, and the web UI gets an icon-button toggle with a CSS tooltip in the transport bar.
- Media-cache keys include the toggle (`mb1`/`mb0`), so blurred and unblurred segments cache separately and flipping the toggle back reuses existing chunks.
- The `RenderContext` / `GpuRasterBackend` vtables changed, so the plugin entry symbol bumps to `tellur_timeline_collection_v3` (a stale plugin fails to resolve cleanly instead of hitting vtable UB).

## Demo (`tellur-live` examples)
- A new `Streak` layer — a comet that rests, dashes across the lower band, and dashes back — wrapped in `MotionBlur` (1/60 s shutter × 16 samples): the dashes draw a visible trail while the rests collapse into the static cache path.

Verified: workspace tests and the GPU `--ignored` suite pass (including CPU/GPU byte-identity for the new kernels); during a dash, frames differ between blur on/off, while at rest they are md5-identical — the static path produces the same image either way.

body:
### Motivation
- Expose a Machines section in the dashboard and mobile UI so users can view and manage equipment from the app chrome.  
- Centralize machine fetching behind a `MachineService` that supports same-origin proxying or direct API calls with a token to avoid repeated ad-hoc `apiClient` usage.  
- Improve resiliency and diagnosability of machine-related flows by adding clearer error messages and ensuring fetch hooks react to `accessToken` changes.  

### Description
- Added a `Machines` navigation item in `lib/navigation.ts` and wired it into the mobile nav and top bar in `components/ui/mobile-nav.tsx` so the item appears on mobile and provides the correct page title mapping.  
- Introduced/updated `MachineService` in `lib/MachineService.ts` to accept `propertyId` and optional `accessToken`, use same-origin proxy requests in browser (with `credentials: 'include'`) and allow direct API calls with `Authorization` headers for server-side callers.  
- Replaced the previous direct `apiClient` call in `dashboard/machines/page.tsx` with `MachineService.getMachines(...)`, implemented client-side pagination of the returned list, and adjusted total count calculation.  
- Added i18n keys `nav.machines` to both English and Thai dictionaries in `lib/i18n/dictionary.ts` so the new nav label is localizable.  
- Improved error handling in `PreventiveMaintenanceForm.tsx` by including `accessToken` in the effect dependency array and mapping HTTP-related error messages to friendlier user-facing strings.  

### Testing
- Performed a TypeScript type-check via `yarn tsc --noEmit` which completed without type errors.  
- Built the frontend with `yarn build` to validate Next.js compilation and the changes integrated into the app bundle.  
- Ran the existing frontend test suite with `yarn test` and linting with `yarn lint`, and both completed successfully.

author: shorta-01
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the retiree-income profit-harvest doctrine — the bridge between the forecast layer and the suggestion engine.

Once a candidate clears the risk-universe gate (#575) and produces a forecast, the confidence gate asks the question that actually matters:

> *"What probability does the model assign to the gross take-profit target being hit inside the user's horizon?"*

If that probability is at or above `trading_confidence_threshold_pct`, the candidate becomes a suggestion; otherwise it's skipped.

### Math

Fits a lognormal terminal-price distribution to the forecast median (`p50_price`) and annualised volatility, then applies the standard normal CDF (via `math.erf`, no numpy at this leaf) to compute `P(S_T >= K)` where `K` is the gross take-profit price.

The gross target is derived from the user's net target via the existing `profit_harvest.gross_pct_for_net_target_pct`, so Belgian TOB on both legs of the cycle is folded in automatically (4 % net → 4.73 % gross on a standard stock, 6.78 % on an accumulating ETF).

### Locked blocking reasons

- `below_confidence_threshold` — clean refusal, surfaced to the UI
- `invalid_forecast_inputs` — structural problem in the inputs
- `zero_volatility` — flat-history series, target unreachable by definition

### Diagnostics on every result

`p_target_hit_pct`, `required_gross_pct`, and `target_price` are populated even on blocked candidates so the operator UI can render the reason in plain Dutch ("58 % kans op €104,73 binnen 6 maanden — drempel 70 %").

### Conservative choice — documented

Terminal-price probability, not running-maximum. A real take-profit LMT triggers when the target is touched at any point during the horizon, which is mathematically higher than `P(S_T >= K)`. Using the terminal probability keeps the gate conservative — under-suggesting beats over-suggesting for the retiree-income use case.

## Test plan
- [x] 16 new tests pass (`tests/test_confidence_gate.py`)
- [x] Full portfolio suite green (611 / 611)
- [x] `ruff check` clean
- [x] `mypy src` clean
- [x] P scales correctly with median, vol, horizon
- [x] All three blocking paths exercised
- [x] Accumulating-ETF carries higher gross target than standard stock
- [ ] CI green on this PR

## Contexte

Closes #337

La suppression d'une carte grise (`RegistrationCertificateFr`) passait par le comportement par défaut de `SaturneObject::delete()`, dont le 3ᵉ paramètre `$softDelete` vaut `true`. La ligne n'était donc pas réellement supprimée : elle restait en base avec le statut `-1` (Deleted). C'est le cas notamment de la mass-action « Supprimer » de la liste, qui appelle `$object->delete($user)`.

## Correctif

Override de `delete()` dans `class/registrationcertificatefr.class.php` pour basculer la valeur par défaut de `$softDelete` à `false` et déléguer à `parent::delete()` → suppression définitive (hard delete) via `deleteCommon()`.

- Couvre tous les points d'entrée existants (mass-action de la liste) et tout futur bouton « Supprimer » sur la fiche.
- Le paramètre `$softDelete` reste disponible pour les appelants qui souhaiteraient explicitement un soft delete.
- Diff minimal, aucun changement de schéma. La constante `STATUS_DELETED` et son libellé sont conservés pour l'affichage d'éventuelles lignes déjà soft-deletées en base.

## Test

1. Créer une carte grise.
2. La supprimer (mass-action « Supprimer » depuis la liste des cartes grises).
3. Vérifier que la ligne n'apparaît plus **et** qu'elle est bien absente de la table `llx_dolicar_registrationcertificatefr` (plus de ligne en statut `-1`).

author: bitflicker64
body:
## Summary

Fixes #44749. Relative schedules like "in 10 seconds" were broken in two places:

1. **LLM fabricates absolute timestamps.** The system prompt only injects the date (for caching), so models invent something like `12:35` for "now + 10s" and the job never fires.
2. **`parse_duration` rejected seconds.** Even a correct `"10s"` schedule raised `ValueError`.

This PR adds seconds support and makes the built-in ticker actually honor those schedules.

## Changes

**`cron/jobs.py`**
- `parse_duration` accepts `s` / `sec` / `secs` / `second` / `seconds`
- Allows decimal values (`1.5s`, `0.5m`)
- Returns `float` minutes so sub-minute precision is preserved
- `seconds_until_next_job` / `compute_ticker_wait_seconds` for adaptive sleep

**`cron/scheduler_provider.py`**
- Built-in ticker still defaults to a 60s cadence when nothing is due soon
- When a job is due sooner, wait shortens to that job's `next_run_at`
- Rechecks every second so a job created mid-cycle (e.g. "remind me in 10s") still fires on time

**`tools/cronjob_tools.py`**
- Schema examples include `10s` / `30s`
- Explicit warning: do not invent ISO timestamps for relative times; use duration format instead

**Docs**
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/cron.md` documents seconds formats and adaptive wake

## Review follow-up

Earlier feedback correctly pointed out that advertising `10s` while the ticker slept a fixed 60s could not honor the promised resolution. This update keeps the seconds parser and adds the trigger path plus an end-to-end test that a `2s` one-shot fires in under ~6s with `interval=60`.

## Test plan

- [x] `parse_duration("30s") == 0.5`
- [x] `parse_duration("90seconds") == 1.5`
- [x] `parse_schedule("every 30s")` / `"30s"` / `"1.5m"`
- [x] `TestTickerWait` (no jobs, near-term shortens wait, overdue near-zero, paused/disabled ignored)
- [x] `test_inprocess_provider_honors_subminute_schedule` (e2e dispatch path)
- [x] Existing scheduler-provider suite green (61 tests)

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/cron/test_scheduler_provider.py \
  tests/cron/test_jobs.py::TestTickerWait \
  tests/cron/test_jobs.py::TestParseDuration \
  tests/cron/test_jobs.py::TestParseSchedule -q
```

author: fransjorden
body:
@
## Problem (found in post-cutover verification)

Production 301s every no-slash URL to its trailing-slash twin (`/nl/diensten` -> `/nl/diensten/`): Netlify Pretty URLs does this for directory-style output (`page/index.html`). But the canonicals, sitemap and hreflang all declare no-slash URLs (`trailingSlash: "never"`). Net effect: every sitemap URL bounces through a 301 and every served page carries a canonical pointing back through that redirect — a sitewide duplicate-signal problem, worst for Bing.

## Fix

- `astro.config.mjs`: `build: { format: "file" }` — emit `page.html` so Netlify serves `/path` directly with a 200.
- `src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro`: strip the `.html` suffix that `Astro.url.pathname` gains under file format, so canonicals/hreflang/nav paths stay clean and the NL<->EN segment map matches again.

## Verified on the build

- 106 pages, zero `.html` occurrences in canonicals or hreflang
- Canonicals: `https://aiheroes.io/nl/diensten` (clean), homepage `/`
- hreflang pairs resolve correctly again (`ai-consultancy-groningen` <-> `ai-agency-groningen`)
- Sitemap URLs unchanged (clean, no-slash)

## After merge

Re-check production: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://aiheroes.io/nl/diensten` should print 200 (currently 301). Then proceed with the Bing resubmit from the cutover checklist — do it after this lands, not before, so Bing fetches the 200 versions.

body:
## Description

Fixes #3603 (nightly CI OOM in `test_batch_prefill_with_ragged_kv_cache_custom_mask`).

For the failing parametrizations (`batch=128, qo_len=577, heads=32, head_dim=256`) the two fp16 outputs are ~1.1 GiB each, and `torch.testing.assert_close` allocates several full-size temporaries inside `torch.isclose` — on top of the still-live `q`/`k`/`v`, bool custom mask, and 256 MB workspace buffer. That transient spike is what pushes 22–24 GB CI GPUs over the edge.

Two changes:
1. Free everything except the two output tensors before the comparison.
2. Compare via a new shared `assert_close_chunked` helper in `tests/test_helpers/test_helpers.py` (row-chunked `torch.testing.assert_close`; bounds the comparison transient to the chunk size, identical pass/fail semantics, scalar/empty fall-through).

## Validation

Measured on RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB, SM120) running exactly the two failing parametrizations:

| | peak `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated` |
|---|---|
| before | **9.333 GiB** |
| after | **3.694 GiB** |

Both parametrizations pass after the change (`2 passed`). Sensitivity-probed the chunked compare: identical tensors pass, a single corrupted mid-tensor element is caught, scalar/empty guards work.

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed (test-only change)
- [x] All tests are passing (`2 passed` on the failing parametrizations; pre-commit clean)

body:
## 変更の要点

issue #404 のPR分割案のうちPR-2にあたる、`docs/07-terminology.md` のリライト。深刻度「中」とされた節末定型文の機械的反復と、横断課題X-1の「入口」の連鎖を解消する。

- **節末定型文「本章では、〜という定義のみ示します」（15回）の解消**
  - 11節（システムプロンプト／アーティファクト／事前学習／ファインチューニング／RAG／グラウンディング／Embedding／マルチモーダル／ハルシネーション／Web検索／プロンプトインジェクション）で省略
  - 4節（メモリ／Research・Deep Research／ツール呼び出し／サンドボックス）で文形を散らす。「経路の輪郭を共有するところまでにとどめる」「呼称と機能の対応関係を揃える」「土台になる段取りであることを示す」「呼び方と狙いの定義に絞る」のように、節の主題に合わせて言い回しを統一しない
  - 既存の短い項目（コネクタ・MCP・エージェント）が省略している書き方を基準線にした
- **「で扱います」連続の解消**
  - 事前学習節とファインチューニング節の連続する「で扱います」を、それぞれ「[5章]にまとめてあります」「[Appendix: ローカルLLM]に分けてまとめてあります」に振った
  - RAG節のAppendix参照を「に集めてあります」に振り、置換後の語が新たに連鎖しないようにした
- **「入口」の解消（横断課題X-1）**
  - サービスの定義（L22）と用語一覧の参照表（L286）の「入口」を「接点」へ
  - プロバイダ自身が運営するサービスの説明（L42）の「入口」を「提供先」へ
  - PR-1（#405）で確立した「見出し・本文・まとめでの比喩的用法は実体側の語に開く」の方針に沿う。本章は通読・拾い読み両用の辞書章のため「接点」（読者が触れる場所）を採用した

## 確認方法

- `npm run lint`：警告ゼロを確認
- `grep -n "本章では、.*という定義のみ示します" docs/07-terminology.md`：0件
- `grep -n "入口" docs/07-terminology.md`：0件
- 章を通読し、削除・置換で段落が宙に浮いた箇所がないこと、変形語尾が新たに連鎖していないことを確認

## 対応する指摘

issue #404 の以下のテーブル行：

- `docs/07-terminology.md`（中）行67〜275（節末定型文）
- 同 行22／L42／L286（「入口」）
- 横断課題 X-1（「入口」の連鎖）の本章該当分

WRITING_GUIDE.mdへのカテゴリ6への追記は、横断課題の整理と合わせて別PRで扱う前提とした。

## 完了条件への寄与

issue #404 の Definition of Done のうち、深刻度「中」の5ファイル中1つ（07章）を解消した。残りのPR分割案（PR-3以降）は別セッション・別ブランチで進む。

body:
### Changes proposed in this Pull Request Applies the agreed team-wide gXdQoz5sdk2CrUqq0UkaLp-fi-65_2 to the Order edit and new screens (HPOS and legacy CPT). First retrofit of the standard aligned in #woo-design (June 2026). **Sizing (all WPDS tokens, no hardcoded values):** - Primary column: `--wpds-dimension-surface-width-xl` (720px) - Secondary column: `--wpds-dimension-surface-width-sm` (320px) - Gap: `--wpds-dimension-padding-2xl` (24px) - Page width: derived (720 + 24 + 320 = 1064px), applied via `calc()` on `.wrap:has(#poststuff)` so the page-title row aligns with the grid below. **Notes for reviewers:** - **Not behind a feature flag.** This is the agreed team-wide standard, not an experiment, so it ships unconditionally. The existing `order-detail-redesign` flag-gated `max-width: 1200px` rule on `.wrap` is removed — it conflicted with the new derived width. - **`@media` instead of `@container`.** The brief specifies container queries, but the legacy admin CSS pipeline uses `grunt-contrib-cssmin@3.0.0` / `clean-css 4.x`, which strips `@container` at-rules entirely (verified — they don't survive the build). The workaround uses `@media (max-width: 1140px)` (≈ wrap < 960px after WP admin chrome). A `TODO` comment in the SCSS marks this for revisit once cssmin is upgraded. - **Stacked order: sidebar on top.** When stacked on narrow viewports, the **secondary** column sits *above* the primary — opposite of the design-system "primary above secondary" rule. Reason: the primary `Update` CTA currently lives in the Order actions metabox in the sidebar; flipping the stack would hide it below the full order detail. Revisit once #60962 moves the CTA out of the sidebar. - **Postbox drag/reorder preserved.** Manually verified on Studio (HPOS) that moving metaboxes between containers and reordering inside a container still works correctly under the new CSS Grid layout. - **WP core float-layout resets.** WP core's `edit.css` sets several float-era widths/margins on `#post-body.columns-2`, `#postbox-container-{1,2}`, and `#side-sortables`. All four are reset in this PR with inline comments explaining why. Implements DSGWOO-1375. ### Screenshots or screen recordings ### BEFORE Default WP metabox layout ### AFTER 720px primary + 320px secondary + 24px gap, derived 1064px page width, centered. ### How to test the changes in this Pull Request 1. Open an order on the Order edit screen — both URLs should look identical: - HPOS: `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=wc-orders&action=edit&id=` - Legacy CPT: `/wp-admin/post.php?post=&action=edit` 2. Verify the layout: - Primary column (Order details, Items, Downloadable permissions, Custom fields) is **720px wide** on the **left**. - Secondary column (Order actions, Order attribution, Customer history, Order notes) is **320px wide** on the **right**. - Gap between columns is **24px**. - Whole layout is **centered** on the page; the `Edit order` page heading and `Add order` button line up with the grid. 3. Drag a metabox from one column to the other — drag/reorder should still work and persist on reload. 4. Resize the browser narrow (or open Responsive mode). Below ~1140px viewport, the columns should **stack with the sidebar on top** and the order details below. 5. Repeat on the **New Order** screen (`/wp-admin/admin.php?page=wc-orders&action=new`) — same sizing should apply. 6. RTL eyeball: with an RTL locale, primary should flip to the right, secondary to the left (CSS Grid handles this automatically). ### Testing that has already taken place - Manually verified the layout on Studio (HPOS path) at desktop (~1900px viewport) and at narrow viewports (mobile responsive mode in DevTools). - Verified postbox drag/reorder works correctly across both containers. - Verified the compiled CSS via the served `admin.css` to confirm `@container` strip and `@media` survival through the cssmin pipeline. ### Follow-ups (separate PRs) - **Prev/next nav alignment.** The sibling PR adding the prev/next order navigation will need a small follow-up tweak once both this PR and the nav PR land — the nav should align to the right edge of the new 1064px grid. This PR has priority over the nav PR. - **Order details internal layout.** Separate PR to come for the **General / Billing / Shipping** stacking behavior *inside* the Order details metabox. Out of scope here. - **cssmin upgrade.** When the legacy admin CSS pipeline is updated (clean-css 5.x+), swap the `@media` workaround back to `@container (max-width: 960px)`. Not blocking this PR. - **Stacked order revisit.** Once #60962 moves the primary `Update` CTA out of the sidebar, swap the stacked layout back to "primary above secondary" per the design-system standard. ### Milestone - [x] Automatically assign milestone for the **[next WooCommerce version](../blob/trunk/plugins/woocommerce/woocommerce.php#L6)** ### Changelog entry - [ ] Automatically create a changelog entry from the details below. The changelog entry was created manually in this PR (`plugins/woocommerce/changelog/order-detail-new-column-sizing`).
Changelog Entry Details **Significance:** patch **Type:** update **Message:** Apply the agreed 2-column sizing (720 / 24 / 320) to the Order edit and new screens.

## Sprint 6 — Mission Control + Templates

Brings Goal Boards (Mission Control) and reusable Templates to NamWeb.

### Goal Boards (Mission Control)
- **Foundation** — a `missionControlStations` lens (projects matching any of a board's tags, de-duped to the top-most, with done-ratio roll-ups via a shared `projectRollup`) plus `createMissionControl` / `deleteMissionControl` mutations. Pure, tested. Closes #65.

body:
## Summary

- Adds `infra/` directory with OpenTofu configuration managing all active `vbonnet/*` repos and the `dear-labs` org
- Per-repo required CI status checks wired for 7 repos (dear-agent, engram, brain-v2, engram-research, vbonnet.ai, gdoc-sync, ai-conversation-logs)
- `dear-labs` org baseline ruleset in evaluate mode: no force push, no deletion, required PR review (1 approver), empty bypass_actors
- Two-provider setup (default `vbonnet` + aliased `dearlabs`) in a single root module — no sub-modules needed
- `import.sh` for bootstrapping existing repo/branch-protection state on first apply
- Supersedes `vbonnet/infra-iac` standalone repo

## File layout

```
infra/
├── providers.tf              # Two GitHub providers: personal + dear-labs org
├── variables.tf              # personal_owner, org_name (token via GITHUB_TOKEN env only)
├── locals.tf                 # Repo inventory with per-repo required CI check names
├── repos.tf                  # github_repository + dependabot resources
├── branch_protection.tf      # github_branch_protection (vbonnet/* repos)
├── dear_labs.tf              # github_organization_ruleset (dear-labs org)
├── import.sh                 # Import existing state before first apply
├── terraform.tfvars.example
└── .gitignore
```

## To apply

```bash
cd infra/
export GITHUB_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)"
tofu init
./import.sh    # imports existing repos + branch protection (skip if fresh)
tofu plan      # review — expect ~0 changes for existing resources
tofu apply
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `tofu init` succeeds (provider download)
- [ ] `./import.sh` imports all 14 active repos + branch protection without errors
- [ ] `tofu plan` shows no unexpected changes for already-configured repos
- [ ] `tofu plan` shows additions for dear-labs org ruleset (new resource)
- [ ] `tofu apply` succeeds — verify on GitHub that branch protection rules are unchanged
- [ ] Spot-check: dear-agent branch protection now lists "Build & Test (ubuntu-latest)" as required check

body:
💡 What: Replaced manual base64 string manipulation (`.toString('base64').replace(/=/g, '').replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_')`) with Node.js native `.toString('base64url')` in `bot/src/services/urlscanner.ts`.
🎯 Why: Creating a base64url string via regex character replacement creates intermediate string allocations causing excessive garbage collection overhead.
📊 Impact: Expected to speed up base64url string generation for URLs by ~3.5x and significantly reduce garbage collection overhead per URL scanned.
🔬 Measurement: Verify by executing a tight loop testing both approaches for ~1M iterations (measured native implementation to execute ~3.5x faster).

---

author: copilot
body:
`SettingsPageView` was being opened modally and crashing in `OnAppearing()` due to unsafe `AppModel.Instance.MainPage` access during modal lifecycle timing. This update keeps the modal `ContentPage` flow intact and removes the null path in settings initialization/actions.

- **Settings modal context binding**
  - `ShowAsync(Page callerPage)` now passes the concrete caller page into `SettingsPageView`.
  - `SettingsPageView` stores that reference and uses it as the primary navigation/sync context.

- **Null-safe settings initialization**
  - `OnAppearing()` now resolves `mainPage` via caller-bound reference first, then `AppModel.Instance.MainPage` fallback.
  - Sync-upload count uses safe access with a default `0` path instead of direct dereference.

- **Null-safe sync action**
  - `btn_SettingsSyncUploadTapped` now safely invokes sync upload only when a valid `MainPage` reference is available.

```csharp
var mainPage = _mainPage ?? AppModel.Instance.MainPage;

int countAll = mainPage?.GetAllSyncFromUploadCount() ?? 0;
mainPage?.CheckAllSyncFromUpload();
```

author: kevinlourd
body:
## Why

Today the welcome gift amount lives in `local_promo_codes.welcome.amount_cents` (the live value read at redeem time), but there's no write endpoint — so changing it needs a migration + deploy each time. This adds an authed endpoint to read/set it, so the dashboard can re-price the welcome gift (or any admin-managed code) **without a migration or deploy**.

## What

- `GET /internal/promo-codes/:code` → `{ code, amount_cents }`
- `PATCH /internal/promo-codes/:code` `{ amountCents }` → updates the row, returns the new value. `amountCents` validated as a non-negative integer. `404` on unknown code (never creates a row).
- `promos.ts`: `getPromoCode` / `setPromoCodeAmount` helpers.
- Applies to **NEW redemptions only** — orgs that already redeemed keep their `local_promos` grant.

## Security

Service-auth only (`x-api-key`), like every other billing route. The amount is **not** a per-request input on a public signup path (which would let a client self-grant credit) — it's a persistent admin value. **Follow-up (separate repos):** api-service proxy that **gates the PATCH to staff**, then a dashboard admin field. The PATCH must not be exposed to non-staff.

## Tests

8 new integration tests (GET, PATCH persist+reflect, redeem-at-new-amount, accept 0, reject negative/non-integer, 404s). Full suite **153 green**.

## Triage

`feature → staging`. Billing-service only this PR; gateway + dashboard are follow-ups.

body:
### Description

When Dynamic colors is enabled and the system wallpaper/accent color changes, the app's colors don't update until force-stopped. The root cause is that `MainActivity` handles `configChanges` (including `uiMode`) itself, and its theme-change detection only compares the theme resource ID — which stays the same for dynamic color variants.

The fix tracks the resolved `system_accent1_500` color value alongside the theme ID. When the wallpaper changes and the system delivers a configuration change (or the activity resumes), the color mismatch triggers `restartActivity()`, applying the new dynamic colors.

Closes: #7795

author: abecid
body:
## Purpose

Adds a reproducible GenRL HPSv3 + VideoAlign training recipe for Wan 2.1 T2V 1.3B on the modular `fastvideo/train` stack.

This PR makes the GenRL run reproducible without relying on a local Modal launcher or git submodules. Runtime assets are prepared through a public helper script, reward dependencies are pinned, and the vendored HPSv3/VideoAlign runtime code is aligned with the reward implementations used by the previous successful GenRL run.

Fixes: N/A

## Changes

- Added `examples/train/prepare_genrl_assets.py` to prepare:
  - GenRL filtered prompt JSONL files
  - `KwaiVGI/VideoReward` checkpoint under `.cache/VideoReward`
  - optional reward-model preflight via `--check-rewards`
- Added `examples/train/requirements-genrl.txt` with the GenRL reward-stack dependency pins.
- Moved the GenRL Wan config to `examples/train/configs/rl/wan/genrl_hpsv3_videoalign.yaml`.
- Updated `examples/train/README.md` with a non-Modal reproduction path.
- Vendored only the HPSv3 and VideoAlign runtime files needed by the GenRL reward wrappers.
- Aligned vendored reward runtimes with the exact successful-run upstream revisions:
  - HPSv3: `a2eb2ef2c7b5d91a566347a5825cf6d872122149`
  - VideoAlign: `aba26b658fec7d9fd30c295187b548ea673c8769`
- Added reward-head load checks so HPSv3/VideoAlign fail fast instead of scoring with randomly initialized reward heads.
- Added prompt dataset validation for missing files, Git LFS pointer files, malformed JSONL, and non-object JSON entries.
- Kept `modal_train_genrl.py` local-only and ignored; it is not part of this PR.

## Reproduction / Training Command

Install the GenRL reward-stack pins after the editable FastVideo install:

    pip install -r examples/train/requirements-genrl.txt

Prepare prompts and reward checkpoints:

    python examples/train/prepare_genrl_assets.py \
      --prompt-dir .cache/genrl_filtered_prompts \
      --genrl-cache-dir .cache/GenRL \
      --videoalign-dir .cache/VideoReward \
      --check-rewards

Launch the 4xGPU GenRL HPSv3 + VideoAlign training run:

    WANDB_MODE=online \
    WANDB_ENTITY=<your-wandb-entity> \
    NUM_GPUS=4 \
    VIDEOALIGN_CHECKPOINT_PATH=.cache/VideoReward \
    FORCE_QWENVL_VIDEO_READER=opencv \
    PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
    bash examples/train/run.sh \
      examples/train/configs/rl/wan/genrl_hpsv3_videoalign.yaml \
      --training.checkpoint.output_dir outputs/genrl_longcat

For the 41-step reproduction probe:

    WANDB_MODE=online \
    WANDB_ENTITY=<your-wandb-entity> \
    NUM_GPUS=4 \
    VIDEOALIGN_CHECKPOINT_PATH=.cache/VideoReward \
    FORCE_QWENVL_VIDEO_READER=opencv \
    PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
    bash examples/train/run.sh \
      examples/train/configs/rl/wan/genrl_hpsv3_videoalign.yaml \
      --training.loop.max_train_steps 41 \
      --training.checkpoint.training_state_checkpointing_steps 20 \
      --training.checkpoint.output_dir outputs/genrl_longcat_repro_rewardfix_41

## Verification

Reward parity was checked against the previous successful GenRL run source state:

- FastVideo commit: `17aecbe2dd07245333a1c0ea85f89b2b7a4a1f88`
- HPSv3 submodule: `a2eb2ef2c7b5d91a566347a5825cf6d872122149`
- VideoAlign submodule: `aba26b658fec7d9fd30c295187b548ea673c8769`
- VideoReward checkpoint: `checkpoint-11352`

Fixed-video reward parity after syncing the vendored runtime:

    hpsv3_general delta:    ~1e-6
    hpsv3_percentile delta: ~1e-6
    videoalign_mq delta:    small residual runtime drift, about -0.03 to +0.04
    videoalign_ta delta:    small residual runtime drift, about -0.04 to +0.02

Training reproduction run after the reward-runtime fix showed reward curves recovering compared with the earlier bad run.

## Test Plan

    python -m py_compile \
      examples/train/prepare_genrl_assets.py \
      fastvideo/train/methods/rl/utils/data.py \
      fastvideo/train/methods/rl/reward/hpsv3.py \
      fastvideo/train/methods/rl/reward/videoalign.py

    python examples/train/prepare_genrl_assets.py --help

    python -c "import yaml; from pathlib import Path; p=Path('examples/train/configs/rl/wan/genrl_hpsv3_videoalign.yaml'); yaml.safe_load(p.read_text()); print(f'parsed {p}')"

## Test Results

    python -m py_compile ...  # passed
    python examples/train/prepare_genrl_assets.py --help  # passed
    YAML parse check  # passed

body:
## Implementato

Validazione live post-merge di #1918 su `/fr/trouver-emploi-suisse/recherche-inconnus-lausanne/`: FCP 3972ms → **320ms** e slug-map fuori dal critical path, MA il body statico restava **visibile sotto il JobBoard idratato** (duplicazione). Diagnosi: App.tsx imposta correttamente l'inline `display:none`, però `index.css` ha il guard anti-AdSense-side-rail `main:not(.seo-static-content) { display: block !important; }` che in cascade batte un inline style non-important (verificato live: `style.display === 'none'`, computed `block`).

- **`App.tsx`** — hide via `style.setProperty('display','none','important')`: vince su qualunque regola `!important`, presente o futura. Il ramo restore (`removeProperty`) invariato.
- **`index.css`** — le tre regole del side-rail guard (`display:block` + 2 `max-width`) escludono anche `.cluster-seo-prose`, coerente con l'esclusione esistente di `.seo-static-content`. La protezione Auto Ads sul `<main>` SPA resta intatta (nessun gating/disable di Auto Ads).
- **`tests/seo/seo-static-css.test.ts`** — nuova guard per la miss-class: regole broad `main`/`main:not(...)` con `display !important` devono escludere entrambe le classi static-handoff; companion test che App.tsx usa l'hide `!important`. (La guard di #1918 controllava solo selettori contenenti i nomi classe — questa regola non li nomina, per questo è sfuggita.)

Vitest mirato: `tests/seo/seo-static-css.test.ts` 6/6 verdi.

## Non implementato (ancora)

- **Verifica live post-deploy della scomparsa duplicazione** — non validabile pre-merge (serve deploy); la rifaccio a deploy avvenuto con Playwright (computed display:none su `main.cluster-seo-prose` + un solo `<main>` visibile). Revert-trigger: se post-deploy la duplicazione persiste o Auto Ads side-rail risulta rotto sulle pagine SPA, revert.
- **Audit altri inline-style vs regole `!important` nel codebase** — fuori scope; nessun altro caso noto con lo stesso conflitto.

author: vigneshnarayanaswamy
body:
## Problem

Connectors deriving lifecycle status from sources couldn't propagate it to the model registry. `Ledger.add()` called `register()` without a status (defaulting to `active`), and `register()` early-returns cached/existing refs unchanged — `add()` then only bumped `last_seen` before `update_model()`. So a connector that derives `status='deprecated'` for an entity deleted at the source saw it land in snapshot payloads only; the model row's status stayed `active` forever.

## Fix

`Ledger.add()` now reads `node.metadata['status']` — the same contract `add()` already uses for `owner` / `model_type` / `tier` / `purpose` / `model_origin`, and what the SQL connector's unmapped-columns path already populates (no `DataNode` / `ModelRef` API change):

- **New models:** the discovered status is passed to `register()`.
- **Existing models:** `ref.status` is reassigned when the discovered status differs, *before* the content-hash dedup check — so the row self-corrects even when the snapshot write is skipped as unchanged.
- **Guard:** values are validated against `ModelStatus` (case-insensitive) and normalized; an absent or unrecognized status leaves the stored status untouched, so an explicit status is never regressed to the default.

Both Snowflake flush MERGE paths already `SET STATUS` on match, so existing rows self-correct on the next sync — no migration needed.

## Tests

- SDK-level `add()` coverage: new-model-with-status, existing-model flip, default, absent/unknown no-op, case normalization, flip-records-snapshot, dedup-skip self-correction (`tests/test_graph/test_ledger_graph.py`)
- Snowflake MERGE-path tests driving `Ledger.add()` end-to-end, plus in-memory ↔ Snowflake-SQL parity on the same discovery sequence (`tests/test_backends/test_snowflake_ledger.py`; the mock session now captures `PURPOSE`/`STATUS` from the MERGE source instead of hardcoding them)
- Hypothesis property: a model's status equals the last *valid* discovered status, with absent/unknown values never regressing it (`tests/test_invariants.py`)

750 passed locally; ruff, mypy, and the coverage gate are clean.

### Motivation
- Add safe admin deletion flows for teams, matches and rounds while protecting historical results, bets and markets.
- Surface tour team membership and round metadata to public Bet Punto and matches endpoints so UI can display team rosters, round sessions and tee times.
- Improve admin round planning, Bet Punto quick-market builders and general robustness of the admin UI.
- Rebrand the Results page to a Golf experience with richer tee-time, teams and results views.

### Description
- Added new serverless endpoints `admin-delete-team` and `admin-delete-match` and hardened `admin-delete-round` and `admin-delete-tour` to reject deletes when protected data (completed matches, player results, protected bet markets, bets, historical stats or protected years) exist, and to provide clear admin-safe error messages.
- Extended public data bundle in `_publicData.ts` to include `tour_team_members` and to return rounds for Bet Punto responses, and updated public API types in `src/lib/publicApi.ts` to include `TourTeamMember` and `rounds` for bet markets.
- Updated admin client API in `src/lib/adminApi.ts` with `deleteTeam` and `deleteMatch` helpers and integrated those actions into the admin UI in `src/pages/Admin.tsx`, including: round session handling (`[Session: ...]` in notes), `combineRoundNotes`/`splitRoundNotes`, safer round planner (max 8 rounds), protection checks for surplus-round deletion, quick Bet Punto market builders (`applyStablefordWinnerOptions`, `applyRoundTeamScoreOptions`), and delete flows for teams/matches/rounds with confirmation and error display.
- Reworked public UI: renamed Results to Golf (navigation icon `golf`), added `BottomNav` golf icon, updated `BetMarketCard` to accept and display `round` info, passed round to `Betting` page, enhanced `Matches` page into a multi-section Golf view with tee-times, results, teams and info components, and added CSS rules for golf UI and team colour palette updates.

author: claude[bot]
body:
## Sentry issue

https://canopy-ey.sentry.io/issues/126913798/

**Error:** `ProgrammingError: column "processing_attempts" does not exist`
**Culprit:** `services.job_queue in claim`
**Count:** 61 occurrences between 2026-06-10 20:53 and 20:56 UTC

## Root cause

PR #140 ("Offload model inference to Modal serverless functions", merged 2026-06-10 20:47) introduced the `processing_attempts` column to `camera_trap_image` and `audio_recording`, along with the Alembic migration `m8e9f0a1b2c3_add_processing_attempts.py`.

However, the app had no mechanism to apply migrations at deploy time — the Dockerfile simply starts `uvicorn`, and `alembic upgrade head` must be run manually via `make migrate-prod`. The job dispatcher started up immediately after deploy and crashed on the first `claim()` call because the column didn't yet exist in production.

A prior diagnosis PR (#141) was closed without a fix.

## What changed

`app/backend/main.py` — the `lifespan` context manager now runs `alembic upgrade head` before starting the job dispatcher. This:

- Applies any pending migrations on every deploy automatically, so code and schema are always in sync.
- Is a no-op if the database is already up-to-date (Alembic checks `alembic_version` first).
- Runs synchronously before the app accepts requests or starts background workers, so there is no window where new code runs against an old schema.

## Caveats

- **Multi-replica deploys:** Alembic does not hold an advisory lock across replicas. If two replicas start simultaneously on a fresh migration both will attempt the DDL; PostgreSQL's own DDL locking means one will win and the other will get an error on startup. For the current single-replica Railway deployment this is not a concern, but worth noting if horizontal scaling is added later.
- The fix does not retroactively un-crash the jobs that failed; any rows left stuck in `processing` will be swept back to `pending` by `sweep_stale()` once the app is running again.

author: jonahgabriel
body:
## Summary

Fixes **OMN-13038** — FIFTH defect on `node_context_roi_runner` (sibling to the OMN-13003 → OMN-13005 → OMN-13010 → OMN-13012 ladder) and the P5 pre-battery blocker from the 2026-06-11 night plan.

`node_generation_consumer._emit_benchmark` routes `contract_passed=False` benchmarks to `onex.evt.omnimarket.node-generation-failed.v1`, but the runner's contract declared only the completed topic and `_run_trial` opened a single two-phase terminal session on it. Failed terminals — emitted with full telemetry (`attempt_count`, tokens, model/provider, `contract_passed=False`) — were never delivered: the runner blocked the full per-arm timeout (120s) and recorded `failure_stage=GENERATION / attempt_count=0`, indistinguishable from "generation never ran". OFF-arm failures are the context-ROI experiment's signal, so every such row was corrupted.

## Fix (consume-side only — smaller contract-compliant change)

The emitter and its contract are **untouched**: `failed.v1` has zero other subscribers, and the P5 probe4 abort diagnostics rely on the failed.v1 high-watermark as a topic-level failure signal, so unifying the emit onto one topic was rejected as the larger, semantics-changing migration.

- `node_context_roi_runner/contract.yaml`: declares `generation_pipeline.terminal_failed_event_topic: onex.evt.omnimarket.node-generation-failed.v1` (already contract-declared on the emitter's publish side; no topic literals in code; handler fails fast at construction if it is missing).
- `handler_context_roi_runner.py`: opens one two-phase session per terminal topic BEFORE publishing (subscribe-before-publish discipline from OMN-13012 preserved for BOTH topics), then races the correlated waits across both topics within the single per-arm timeout. First correlated terminal wins; all sessions are closed on the way out (publish-failure path included). Legacy single-call consumers are raced per-topic the same way. `_extract_row` already maps `contract_passed=False` → `failure_stage=VALIDATION` with the real `attempt_count` — no row-extraction change needed.

## TDD (real entry points, RED first)

`tests/nodes/node_context_roi_runner/test_failed_terminal_routing.py` written before the fix: **10 tests RED on dev tip `dcd3ead5`** (core: failed terminal must yield `failure_stage=VALIDATION, attempt_count=2`, not the GENERATION/0 timeout signature; both sessions opened pre-publish; winner+loser closed; legacy fallback races both topics; `handle_async` dispatch entry covered; genuine-timeout signature preserved; command payload shape unchanged; topics never hardcoded). All GREEN after the fix. `test_handle_async_non_blocking.py` fakes updated to per-topic sessions.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/nodes/node_context_roi_runner/ -v` → 84 passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/` (no filters) → 33 failed / 7200 passed; failure set diffed against a clean dev-tip (`dcd3ead5`) stash run of the same suite: **byte-identical** (`diff` → no output). All 33 are pre-existing env-dependent failures (tests reaching live Kafka `192.168.86.201:19092`, unreachable from this lane; they pass in isolation). This branch adds +14 passing, 0 new failures.
- `uv run mypy src/omnimarket/ --strict` → Success, no issues in 2331 files.
- `uv run ruff format` + `ruff check --fix` → clean. `pre-commit run --all-files` → all hooks pass.

## Deploy posture

deploy_pending — rides the P5 dev rehearsal → stability rebuild batch (per OMN-13038 / night plan P5). No batteries until this fix is merged AND probe4 is non-degenerate.
