author: msft-tkendrick
body:
## What & why

Implements an **agentic SDLC** workflow that takes a [SpecKit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) feature spec from *ambiguous* to *implemented-with-evidence*, wiring together the four building blocks from the request:

| Block | Role here |
| --- | --- |
| **GitHub SpecKit** | Source of truth (`specs/NNN-slug/`). |
| **Copilot SDK sdk-style squads** | Squad members are Copilot custom agents, dispatched as a parallel **fleet**. |
| **ASSERT framework** | NL specs → executable `eval_config.yaml` that *generate* and *police* the squad. |
| **Copilot SDK inference** | Crafts each member's grounded prompt (deterministic offline fallback). |

## The loop
interview → micro-spec facets + ADRs → ASSERT evals → **provably grounded** squad → fleet dispatch → BDD features → TDD red/green/refactor → evidence (coverage, screenshots, video, Playwright).

## "Provably grounded"
`sdlc ground`/`run` emits a grounding proof that **blocks implementation** unless:
1. coverage = 100% (every requirement owned),
2. no ungrounded members, and
3. no dangling requirement references.

## What's here
- **`sdlc/`** — `@tokenizer/sdlc` toolkit: SpecKit parser, ambiguity detector, facet/ADR managers, squad role derivation + forge + grounding proof, Copilot SDK inference + fleet dispatch, ASSERT eval gen, BDD gen, guarded TDD loop, evidence collector, CLI + pipeline. **53 vitest tests, 94.5% stmt coverage, fully offline-deterministic.**
- **`.github/agents/`** — `sdlc` orchestrator + `spec-interviewer`, `facet-curator`, `evidence-auditor`, and generated grounded squad members under `squad/`.
- **`specs/001-model-cost-comparison/`** — a real SpecKit spec for the tokenizer app (spec/plan/tasks).
- **`docs/sdlc/`** — methodology doc + the generated worked-example bundle (interview, grounding 13/13, 6 ASSERT evals, 5 features / 13 scenarios, TDD loop, 5 evidence manifests) + `ADR-001` and resolved `MSF-001`.
- **`sdlc_assert_targets.py`** — ASSERT callable adapter so the generated evals' `callable:` refs resolve.

## Verification
- `sdlc`: 53 tests green, 94.5% statement coverage.
- Example pipeline: `sdlc run specs/001-model-cost-comparison` → squad **13/13 grounded (100%)**.
- **No app regressions:** root `npm run typecheck` clean; root `npm run test` 12/12 green (`sdlc/**` excluded from app vitest).

## Try it
```bash
npm run sdlc:build
node sdlc/bin/sdlc.mjs interview specs/001-model-cost-comparison
node sdlc/bin/sdlc.mjs ground    specs/001-model-cost-comparison
node sdlc/bin/sdlc.mjs run       specs/001-model-cost-comparison --repo .
```

author: notacop38
body:
Works through every finding in `docs/reviews/2026-06-09-codebase-review.md` (P1 bugs → P2 architecture → P3 product/UX), one coherent commit per finding group. The review doc gains a dated status addendum mapping each finding to its resolution.

## Reliability (P1)
- **`make ci` now passes on a fresh machine.** Every gate tool runs as `$(PY) -m <tool>`; bare names could resolve to shims bound to a different interpreter (reproduced: a uv-tool mypy fails where the project env's mypy passes). `make test` gains the Python-version guard; `types-PyYAML` is pinned so the strict YAML loaders genuinely type-check.
- `make demo-gif` probes per-platform font paths instead of hardcoding the Debian DejaVu location (regenerated GIF verified **byte-identical** to the committed asset).

## Architecture (P2) — behavior-identical, verified
- One shared synthetic-TCP PCAP scaffold (`substation/emit/_tcp.py`, parameterized by `payload_for`); the three emitters keep only PDU builders. A fourth protocol's emitter is now PDU builders plus one line.
- Shared protocol helpers (`substation/protocols/_common.py`: zeek uid, IPv4 check, ephemeral ports, param validators with per-protocol error types) and one strict YAML loader (`substation/_yaml.py`). ~400 duplicated lines removed.
- **All 19 bundled scenarios emit byte-identical `.pcap`/`.jsonl` before vs. after the refactors** (verified against the pre-refactor commit in a separate worktree; an independent fresh-context review re-verified this).
- Sigma rules parse once per process; the demo loads the registry once per run.

## Product (P3)
- **CLI front door:** `substation --version` · `list` · `validate` · `coverage` · multi-file `demo --scenario` · `demo --strict` (exits non-zero unless every scenario's `exercises` contract holds — including on typo'd/unknown detection ids). Default demo output is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Tighter Detection Contract:** every validated Tier-1 fire case pins its exact hit indices (catches a rule that over-matches yet still passes fire/quiet), with a completeness check; Sigma rule UUIDs must be unique; scenario names must be globally unique (they're artifact basenames) — the one DNP3 straggler is renamed `dnp3-anomalous-x1-new-function`.
- **Honeypot:** probe log rotates at `log_max_bytes` (default 50 MiB, `--log-max-bytes`) so a noisy scanner can't grow it unboundedly.
- Single coverage snapshot (`docs/coverage/` only); ICSNPP load expectations documented in the S3/X1 Zeek rules; guard thread-safety documented; README/CHANGELOG/contributor guides aligned.

## Verification
- `make ci` fully green end to end (format, lint, strict mypy, **322 passed / 20 skipped**, schema, coverage drift check, bandit, scoped dep audit, secret scan, SBOM, files-only invariant).
- Demo output diffed against the committed transcript: unchanged.
- Independent fresh-context review of the full diff: **no blockers**; its findings (strict-mode unknown-id gap, uncaught `S7Error`, stale checklist paths, probe-log newline portability) are fixed in the final commit.

A deliberate non-change: a `zeek --parse-only` CI gate (review P3.11) was rejected with rationale — the S3/X1 rules can't parse on stock Zeek without the icsnpp-s7comm plugin, and `make verify` already executes all four Zeek rules in the ICSNPP container.

author: rasros
body:
## What changed

- **`BenchCache`** — content-addressed cache of solve results, keyed by `sha256(model bytes + datafile bytes) · time-settings · solver+settings`. `SolveMetric` looks the key up first: a hit replays the stored `SolverInvocation.Result` (no subprocess), a miss invokes and stores. Reference baselines stay frozen across runs; klause's key also folds in the klause-cli binary mtime, so rebuilding klause invalidates only klause's entries. Under `build/bench-cache/`; disable with `-Dklause.bench.cache=false`.
- **`parity-runs/compare.sh`** — offline, direction-aware comparison of two saved `solve` reports across the instances they share. "better" = higher for maximize / lower for minimize, equal-value tiebroken on time-to-best; flags `UNSOUND` (beating a proven optimum) and reports the "solve 100% of B's" superset. Supersedes `analyze.sh` (which assumed minimization).
- `ResolvedProblem.maximize` (set by MiniZincRunner from the solve directive) flows to `SolveRow.maximize` so the comparison knows the objective's direction. `SolverInvocation.Result` is now `@Serializable` (for the cache).

## Why

The redesign saves one result per (instance, settings, solver). Caching that makes reruns instant and lets reference baselines be frozen while klause iterates — the "known record" the campaign needs. The compare script is the offline diff that replaces in-session comparison, and being max/min-aware it scores maximize instances correctly (the other half of the #388 fix).

## Testing

`:klause-bench:detektMain`, `:klause-bench:test` green. End-to-end: `bench solve name=mario,cargo engine=cp` then a second identical run replays from cache (identical `@ms`, solve skipped); `compare.sh solve-klause-cp-x20.json solve-choco-x20.json` correctly scores mario (both 628, choco proved+faster → loss, not unsound) and cargo (choco 3358 < klause 27368 → loss).

- **`parseJsonlLines` warn rate-limiting** (`performance-reader.ts`): module-level `warnRateLimiter` Map keyed by full source path; at most one warn per source per `WARN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` (60s). - **`classifyTaskComplexity` reuses the long-lived reader** (`main-agent.ts:452-455`): the old per-call `new PerfR(...)` had an empty cache and bypassed the mtime score cache entirely; now reuses the registry-wired instance via a new `getPerformanceReader()` accessor on `AgentRegistry`. author: akaryl
body:
## Summary

Nuevo endpoint `POST /api/uploads/proxy-images-bulk` que recibe lista de URLs (max 100 por request) y descarga las imagenes desde Spaces en paralelo server-side (sin el limite de 6 conexiones por host del browser), devolviendo los buffers como base64.

Cada fetch upstream tiene timeout de 20s con `AbortController` para que un Spaces lento no detenga al lote entero — devuelve `{ url, error }` solo para esa URL y sigue con las demas.

## Por que

La descarga del Versionario Artes embebe cientos de miniaturas (cat 10 de prod ~792). Hoy el front hace 1 GET por imagen al `/proxy-image` existente, en pools de 8 (limitado por el browser). Con muchas miniaturas se traduce a ~30s solo en la fase de prefetch.

Con el endpoint bulk, el front pasa a 3-10 requests totales y el backend hace el fan-out paralelo a Spaces (que aguanta cientos de conexiones sin sudar). Reduce el prefetch de ~30s a ~5s.

## Acompaña a

PR de `front-qeb` que consume el endpoint en `uploadsService.proxyImagesBulk`. Si este PR no se mergea, el front cae al endpoint individual existente y todo sigue funcionando (degradado).

## Test plan

- [ ] `POST /api/uploads/proxy-images-bulk` con `{ urls: [validUrl1, validUrl2] }` → 200 con array de `{ url, buffer, contentType }`.
- [ ] Con `{ urls: [invalidUrl] }` (no Spaces) → 200 con `{ url, error: 'URL no permitida' }` para esa.
- [ ] Con 100 URLs → 200, todas procesadas.
- [ ] Con 101 URLs → 400.
- [ ] Con `{}` (sin urls) → 400.
- [ ] Sin Bearer token → 401.

author: grdsdev
body:
## Summary

- `handleClose` in `ConnectionManager` was transitioning to `.disconnected` but never calling `initiateReconnect`, so any server-initiated WebSocket close (deploy restart, load-balancer timeout, etc.) left the SDK permanently disconnected.
- Fix: added `initiateReconnect(reason: closeReason)` inside the `.connected` guard in `handleClose`, mirroring the existing behavior in `handleError`.
- SDK-initiated disconnects are unaffected — `disconnect()` transitions away from `.connected` before the close event arrives, so the guard fails safely and no reconnect is triggered.

## Test Plan

- [x] Added `testHandleCloseInitiatesReconnectAndEventuallyReconnects` — verifies that a remote close transitions through `.reconnecting` and completes a second transport call.
- [x] Existing `testHandleCloseUpdatesStateWithoutSendingAnotherCloseFrame` continues to pass (no spurious extra close frame).
- [x] All `ConnectionManagerTests` pass (8/8).

## Related

Companion to #1003.

author: bashandbone
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `std::path::Component` loop in the `typescript` extractor's path normalization carelessly popped elements without checking stack bounds or root prefixes. When `..` `ParentDir` components were encountered without a previous valid element on the stack (i.e. standard relative path syntax like `../../file.ts`), it effectively ignored the `..` elements, altering the path destination or enabling directory traversal escape vulnerabilities. It also falsely popped root/prefix elements.
🎯 Impact: This caused faulty module resolution and enabled path traversal outside of bounded analysis directories, presenting a serious security traversal risk.
🔧 Fix: Explicitly prevented popping bounded constants (`RootDir`/`Prefix`). Updated logic to push the `ParentDir` instead of ignoring it when the stack is empty or its preceding element is also a `ParentDir` (to natively preserve consecutive `../../`).
✅ Verification: Ran `cargo +nightly fmt`, `cargo clippy`, the workspace tests to verify no regressions existed (`cargo test --workspace -- --skip incremental_postgres_tests --skip incremental_integration_tests`), and targeted tests (`cargo test -p thread-flow --test extractor_typescript_tests`) indicating normal functional parity was maintained securely. Also formatted and included learnings in `.jules/sentinel.md`.

---
*PR created automatically by Jules for task [9407032769846878330](https://jules.google.com/task/9407032769846878330) started by @bashandbone*

## Summary by Sourcery

Fix insecure path normalization in the TypeScript dependency extractor and apply minor cleanups and documentation updates.

Bug Fixes:
- Harden TypeScript extractor path normalization to correctly handle parent directory components without escaping root or altering intended relative paths.

Enhancements:
- Simplify function signatures and locking logic in the rule engine and tree-sitter integration for improved clarity and consistency.

Documentation:
- Add sentinel documentation describing the path normalization vulnerability, its root cause, and prevention guidelines.

author: gustavovalverde
body: OAuth Provider gains one extension contract so a companion plugin can implement an OAuth RFC (token exchange, CIBA, OIDC4VCI, ...) in its own package, instead of the provider growing a bespoke option per protocol. A plugin calls `extendOAuthProvider(ctx, extension)` from `init()` to contribute grants, assertion-based client authentication, discovery metadata, claims, and client-id discovery. `@better-auth/cimd` is the first consumer. Because other protocol plugins will copy this shape, the guarantees matter more than the surface: - Contributions are validated as a set: grant types, auth methods, and assertion types must be disjoint across extensions, so a collision fails at setup instead of silently shadowing one. Metadata and claims are additive and cannot override authorization-server core. - Extension claims run through the same access-token claim authority as built-in claims, so a JWT mint and an opaque-token introspection cannot disagree and reserved names stay server-owned. - `consumeClientAssertion` is exported so a custom client-auth method enforces the RFC 7523 audience, lifetime, and replay checks the built-in `private_key_jwt` runs, instead of re-deriving them. A contributed grant reaches the shared issuer, so it inherits scope validation, resource policy, JWT or opaque access tokens, refresh, ID tokens, and the response envelope unchanged. Motivating example: the CIBA work in #8485. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an extension surface to `@better-auth/oauth-provider` so plugins can add grants, client auth, discovery, and claims without changing core. Also adds token confirmation (RFC 7800) and a provider API for grants and plugin endpoints. - **New Features** - `extendOAuthProvider(ctx, extension)` registers grants, client auth (`token_endpoint_auth_method`/`client_assertion_type`), additive discovery metadata, additive access-token/ID-token/UserInfo claims, and client-id discovery. - Token confirmation: `issueTokens` accepts `confirmation` and stamps `cnf`; sets `token_type` to "DPoP" for a `jkt`; `authenticateClient` can return a confirmation that grants forward to `issueTokens`; confirmations on opaque tokens fail closed; `cnf` is reserved. - Provider API: `getOAuthProviderApi(ctx, opts, grantType?)` exposes `getClient`, `authenticateClient`, `issueTokens`, `hashToken`, and `validateAccessToken`; grant handlers now receive `provider`. - Single access-token claim authority with precedence: extension < per-issuance extra < plugin < resource; ID-token/UserInfo claims are additive and cannot replace core identity claims. - Client-id discovery is contributed via `clientDiscovery` in an extension; `@better-auth/cimd` now uses this. `consumeClientAssertion` is exported for RFC 7523 audience/lifetime/jti checks; expired assertions are rejected. - **Bug Fixes** - Hardened extension registration: grant/auth/assertion types must be unique; collisions and empty assertion-type lists are rejected; built-in/reserved values cannot be reused. - Tightened client auth: enforce a client’s registered method; reject mixing `client_assertion` with secrets; extension `jwks`/`jwks_uri` pass the same HTTPS/private-address/trusted-origin checks as `private_key_jwt`. - Dynamic registration gates early: when disabled or unauthenticated, return `access_denied` before metadata validation. - UserInfo resolves the OAuth client only when pairwise subject or a claim extension needs it; added tests for introspection, disjointness, revoke, and override behavior. - Provider API `authenticateClient` now binds the client-assertion audience to the served endpoint URL, preventing cross-endpoint replay. Written for commit 37793c60df85ad3623f912ff9a0d67a7b8dfadf0. Summary will update on new commits.

author: biswajitkhanra
body:
## Financial logic
- **INV/DUE fix** — Expected Revenue now equals the whole billed book (all EMI + all fine + all 1st EMI charge, paid + unpaid) instead of the financed principal, so INV/DUE correctly equals everything still outstanding and can never go negative. Same fix applied to the Retailer Payment Summary's Collection %.
- **PROFIT YTD (completed customers ONLY)** — realized profit = collected (EMI + fine + 1st charge) − disburse, computed exclusively over fully **COMPLETE** customers, bucketed by IST completion year. The card shows YTD + all-time and how many completions feed the YTD figure. **Running / partially active accounts are fully excluded** — they stay in live tracking only.
- **NPA / Loss category** — accounts already marked NPA, or RUNNING loans with an EMI unpaid for **more than 3 months** (90 days past due). Dashboard banner shows the account count and the **EMI-due-only** loss exposure (fines & charges excluded).
- **Fine Collected is month-wise** (IST approval month) with a year selector and 12 clickable month bars.
- **Card order**: LOAN AMOUNT → COLLECTION → BTD → MARKET DUE → INV/DUE → PROFIT YTD.

## Search & customer-open flow
- **Inline shelf-search loader** — a compact strip directly **under the search bar** (never full-screen): multiple people scanning multiple shelves, files flying out while the query runs. Multi-customer results read as files pulled from the shelves.
- **Skeleton crew on single-customer open only** — multiple skeletons, each with a phone, dancing under disco lights. Pure UI placeholder with **no shared state**; it exits with a phone-throw + flash effect **before** the popup renders, and the EMI-due / 1st-charge popup is gated on the loader having exited so it is fed exclusively by the customer's real breakdown data. No mixing of the two loaders.

## Approvals
- **SuccessBurst** — emblems spin in from every screen edge and converge on a rotating ✓ badge. Mounted **only** from the verified approve-success path and unmounted on a timer, with a double-fire guard — re-renders, refreshes and rotation can never replay it.

## Stability & quality
- **Rotation stability** — all overlays/celebrations are state-driven and mount-once; in-view animations use `viewport: once`; nothing keys off window dimensions, so orientation changes reflow without re-triggering animations.
- **Image quality** — customer photos and document scans render eager (no lazy-load degradation) with high-quality scaling pinned to their own GPU layer (`.img-crisp`).

## UI
- Metric cards are vibrant gradient tiles (distinct palette per metric) with white high-contrast text, animated gradient pan, sheen and glow.
- Distinct accent colours per section across admin / retailer / customer pages.
- **Gooey jelly press feel** app-wide via a global `jellyPop` keyframe (honours reduced motion).
- **Gullak record-payment celebration**: coins pour from the gullak into a glowing Record Payment pill that counts up to the collected amount.
- **Footer** visible on admin, retailer **and** customer pages; the band is transparent and only "Made By **Biswodip Goj**" is coloured.
- **Bank-style per-customer Loan Statement** with instalment ledger, running balance and Download PDF — openable from the customer portal and the admin/retailer customer view.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` succeeds.

author: dadjokez
body:
The quality net from the strategy pause — built and **proven against real Bedrock**.

## What it is
`pnpm eval` runs 5–7 cases per capability through the *same* `runAgentLoop` production uses, scored by **deterministic predicates** (free, exact, stable) + a **Haiku judge** (for qualitative calls). Cases are **data** — locking in a found bug is a one-file edit, no harness change. ~$0.006 per full run, under a minute, non-zero exit on failure.

## Proven (not just written)
I ran it against real Bedrock through the iterate loop you asked for — **6/9 → 7/9 → 7/9 → 9/9** across four passes. Every failure was a too-strict *assertion*, never a product bug:
- markdown bold (`not** Christmas`) broke a regex
- the judge nitpicked a correct meeting-notes answer
- a rubric I wrote contradicted its own skill (penalized the Executive Brief for... recommending)
- the model *flagged* a prompt injection (better than ignoring it) and a narrow rubric failed it

Then the success criteria:
- **SC-001** ✅ Christmas + faithfulness cases pass on `main`
- **SC-003** ✅ reverting the date-stamp fix turns the suite **red on date-grounding specifically** (regression lock works)
- **Stable** ✅ 9/9 three consecutive runs

## Coverage (v1)
- `date-grounding` — the Christmas class: real date, current year, no stale training year, no fabricated 'today's news'
- `skill-faithfulness` — Meeting Notes→Actions (owners from source; asks when empty), Email Drafter (subject + brevity), Executive Brief (faithful facts, allowed analysis), prompt-injection resistance

## CI
- Per-PR: a free mock-mode wiring test (`packages/evals/harness.test.ts`) runs in the normal suite
- Nightly: `.github/workflows/nightly-evals.yml` does the real-model run (OIDC creds via `AWS_EVAL_ROLE_ARN` repo var), uploads the report, opens/refreshes a regression issue on failure

The README bakes in the lessons (prefer deterministic; test the capability not adjacent weaknesses; write rubrics for the best acceptable behavior). Next capabilities (tool no-hallucination, slash redirect, redaction) need the app stack and land as a follow-up tier.

body:
## Summary

- Adds `supabase/functions/payment-confirm-reminder/index.ts` — cron-driven edge function that queries jobs in escrow where the helper marked complete 24–48 h ago and the poster hasn't confirmed yet, then inserts an in-app notification (which auto-fans-out to APNs/FCM push via the existing trigger)
- Adds `supabase/migrations/20260612440000_payment_confirm_reminder.sql` — new `jobs.payment_confirm_notif_sent boolean` column + partial index + cron schedule at 15:00 UTC (10 AM Central)
- Registers `[functions.payment-confirm-reminder]` with `verify_jwt = false` in `supabase/config.toml`

The reminder fills the silent gap between the helper marking complete and the 48 h auto-release, giving the poster a clear window to confirm or request a revision.

## Architecture notes

- Idempotent: `payment_confirm_notif_sent IS NULL` filter + flag-on-send prevents duplicate pushes even if the cron fires twice
- Replay-safe migration: `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, `DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM cron.unschedule(...) EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL; END; $$` before `cron.schedule`
- Auth gate matches all other cron functions: accepts `CRON_SECRET` or `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` bearer; returns 401 otherwise
- Health-check shortcut (`?health=1`) with no auth required, same pattern as expiring-jobs-push
- Uses `vault.decrypted_secrets` for URL + key in the cron body — same vault names as `expiring-jobs-push`

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build` pass (frontend checks only — Deno functions not checked by Vite)
- [ ] After `supabase db push`: confirm `jobs.payment_confirm_notif_sent` column exists, partial index created, cron job visible in `cron.job`
- [ ] Manual invoke: `curl -X POST <fn-url>/payment-confirm-reminder -H "Authorization: Bearer <service_role_key>"` — should return `{ processed: N, sent: N, errors: 0 }`
- [ ] Verify notification appears in bell + push arrives on device for a job in the 24–48h window
- [ ] Re-invoke — same job should NOT be re-notified (`payment_confirm_notif_sent = true` flag prevents it)

author: bridgerdavidson
body:
## Why

A full audit of the charge-at-completion architecture (both flows x card/ACH; findings + remaining backlog in `docs/payments-audit-v3-charge-at-completion.md`, which supersedes the v2 sweep doc) found four blockers that should land before the new flow is cut over. The unauthenticated setup-intent routes (finding C1) already shipped separately as #65.

## What

**Recovery loop for failed completion charges (C2)** — under charge-at-completion, charge failures happen on COMPLETED appointments, but the card-link recovery (`setup_intent.succeeded`) explicitly excluded completed rows, so a decline/3DS at completion was a permanent dead-end:
- the re-queue now includes completed jobs, bumps `reauth_count` (a spent idempotency key would otherwise replay the cached decline), and charges the new card immediately;
- new reconcile sweep `chargeUncollectedCompletions` charges completed jobs whose charge never ran (flags off at completion, 502 mid-charge). `authorization_status IS NULL` is the loop-breaker: a declined attempt stamps `failed` and leaves the sweep until a new card re-arms it, so dead cards are never hammered;
- a saved card detached between booking and completion is substituted with the customer default (persisted + ledgered) instead of surfacing as a fake decline.

**Cancel during an in-flight ACH debit (C3)** — the payer used to be debited days later for a cancelled job with no refund, funds stranding on the platform. Charges now carry `charge_kind` (`completion` vs `cancellation_fee`, in PI metadata and on `payments.charge_kind`); a completion charge that settles on a since-cancelled appointment is auto-refunded in full (key `cancelrefund-{id}`, system-issued `refunds` row) instead of settled, in both the webhook and the `settleUnsettledCaptures` backstop. The fee charge still legitimately settles to the tenant. The cancel route reports `inflight_debit` and charges no fee in that case (ACH payers are fee-exempt by policy anyway).

**Uniqueness (C4, migration 088)** — partial unique indexes enforce one Stripe-backed revenue payment row and one payout row per appointment (manual cash records stay exempt), with pre-dedupe of any existing duplicates, 23505-aware writers, and a `duplicate_charge_detected` forensic event when two real PaymentIntents collide.

**Complete/cancel race (H7)** — a PAID completion charge now blocks the cancel (409: refund instead); cancelling a completed-but-uncharged job is an administrative undo that charges no fee; a DB trigger forbids `cancelled -> completed/in_progress`. A charge racing a cancel resolves money-safely through the C3 auto-refund.

**Cancellation-fee retries (H6)** — the fee idempotency key is attempt-suffixed (`cancelfee-{id}-{n}`); previously a same-day retry replayed the cached decline and a changed fee amount hit a Stripe `idempotency_error`. A thrown decline now also persists a failed payments row so the retry bump actually triggers.

**Silent money-loss states (H5)** — new admin notifications `charge_failed` (decline vs 3DS wording), `cancellation_fee_failed` (reasoned), `self_pay_no_card`, and `cancelled_job_refunded`, deduped via `notification_events.dedupe_key` (088) so webhook replays cannot double-notify. Self-pay no-card paths also gain the previously-missing ledger events.

## Tests

35 new/updated integration tests across `cancel`, `charge`, `webhook` (new `route.chargerecovery` sibling), and the reconcile sweep (new `chargeUncollected` sibling), plus label/navigation unit tests. Full integration suite serialized locally: 345/347 with the only failures being a missing mock export (fixed in this PR) — the flaky `payout.paid OLDEST` test (audit finding M3, pre-existing on master) passed this run. `npx supabase db reset` rebuilds cleanly through 088.

## Follow-ups (specified, not in this PR)

Phases B (clawback hardening H1-H4), C (money-math mediums), D (disputes UI + notification dedupe backfill) are fully specified in `docs/payments-audit-v3-charge-at-completion.md` and land as sequential PRs.

author: johnverheij
body:
Adds three assertions for how many times timer callbacks ran:
HasTimerFiredCount(int), HasNoTimerFired(), and HasTimerFiredAtLeast(int).
ObservableTimeProvider now wraps each timer callback to count fires. The count
is cumulative and survives disposal, so a heartbeat that fired three times and
then stopped still reports 3. With a FakeTimeProvider it increments each time
fake time is advanced past a due or period boundary, so it stays deterministic.
TimerFireCount and ActiveTimerInfo.TimesFired expose the same data on the core.

Two fixes alongside it:

- After a periodic timer fires, NextTimerDueTime now reports the period instead
  of the stale creation-time due. A fired one-shot becomes disabled and drops
  out of the pending-due calculation.
- The README and ActiveTimerAssertions docs claimed the package ships no polling
  assertion. It has shipped HasNoActiveTimersEventually and its siblings since
  0.7.0/0.8.0, so the text now points to those for the async disposal race.

Both packages go to 0.9.0, baseline to 0.8.1. ApiCompat suppressions and the
PublicAPI snapshots are regenerated (additions only). New code is at 100%
line/branch/method; 219 tests pass.

author: jorgebc
body:
The three session-ingestion LLM calls (extraction, entity resolution, conflict detection) concatenated GM-supplied text into prompts without the untrusted-data guard that Query Mode already applies. Bring them up to the same bar (OWASP LLM01), mirroring QueryPromptAssembler:

- Extraction: wrap the raw summary in <session_summary> tags; system prompt instructs the model to treat the tagged content strictly as data, never as instructions.
- Entity resolution: wrap untrusted mention/candidate values in <data>
  tags (trusted id/type kept as plain metadata) + matching guard.
- Conflict detection: wrap narrative header, extracted entities, and world-state context in <data> tags + matching guard.

Add an adversarial unit test to each adapter (mirroring QueryPromptAssemblerTest) asserting instruction-like input stays inside its delimiter and the guard phrasing is present.

author: andlog0713
body:
## What this is

iOS half of web PR #74 (report-trust wire format), scope 3A: decode every new v3 field, prove it against the real deployed report, render ONE hero chart. The other 8 charts / ~10 components / BY-HOUR typed-array swap are deliberately NOT here (next prompt).

## Decode layer

New types: `ReportRecovery`, `ReportCharts` (+ `HourPnlPoint`, `DayPnlPoint`, `ChartOddsBucket`, `StakeByStreak`, `SessionTimelinePoint`, `HeroSession`, `BetTypeMixEntry` with `betClass` mapped from the reserved wire key `class`), `FindingSubSplit`. Additive optional fields: `AutopsyAnalysis.recovery`/`.charts`, `DetectedSession.framing`, and `confidence`/`subSplits` (+ raw `severity` on StrategicLeak) across the three finding types. Tolerant `try?` decode throughout; `ReportCharts` degrades per-array. Nothing removed.

**Directive correction, validated by the proof:** explicit CodingKeys do *not* bypass `.convertFromSnakeCase` — JSONDecoder converts the wire key first, then matches stringValue. The camelCase keys (`netUSD`, `tOffsetMin`, …) have no underscores, pass through unchanged, and are pinned by exact-wire CodingKeys as directed. The snake_case `sub_splits` keys must be pinned to their **post-conversion** spellings: `roi_pct → roiPct`, `net_usd → netUsd` (property `netUSD`). A raw value of `"net_usd"` silently decodes nil — the acronym trap, one level deeper than the brief assumed. Comments in the models document this.

`ReportCache.currentVersion` 3 → 4: v3 blobs were decoded by a build without these fields and would pin `charts == nil` forever; the bump forces a refetch on first launch.

## Decode proof (gate passed)

body:
differentiateFunction installed the differentiated algorithm section by creating a new class pointer, but the "fake" function node created earlier for recursive differentiation still held the old pointer. Its cached function is what Function.getDerivative/addDiffInfo put back into the function tree when the same call is differentiated again, so codegen received the original (underived) body: the generated derivative never assigned its outputs and e.g. function_diff.mos crashed with a stack overflow whenever the uninitialized return slot happened to be NaN. Update the class pointer in place instead so every node copy sees the differentiated body.

Also add a use-before-assign check for backend-generated functions (the frontend check only runs in typeFunctionBody, which generated functions never pass through): provably unassigned outputs or uses are reported as errors, and variables that cannot be proven to always be assigned are explicitly initialized to zero with a warning, as recommended by the specification.

author: trieloff
body:
## What

Under AI detection, `gh auth token` now returns the **as-a-bot user-to-server token** instead of the user's personal token.

## Why

`gh auth token` was classified as a safe operation (`is_safe_operation`) and passed straight through to the real `gh`, handing detected AI tools the user's personal OAuth token. An agent that captured it could call the GitHub API directly — e.g. `curl -H "Authorization: token <token>"` — bypassing this wrapper entirely, so the actions were recorded as the **user** rather than as `as-a-bot[bot]` acting on their behalf.

This is the single most common circumvention path observed in real agent transcripts: blocked (or simply impatient) at the wrapper, the agent runs `TOKEN=$(gh auth token); curl …` and routes around attribution. Because the token was legitimately reachable, no amount of error-message wording at the *block* point could stop it — the leak was upstream.

## How

- Intercept `gh auth token` right after AI detection and return the as-a-bot token from `get_cached_token` (the same source the write path uses). The reflexive `gh auth token` + `curl` bypass now stays attributed to the bot.
- Fail closed when no bot token can be issued yet (app not authorized) rather than falling back to the personal token.
- Non-AI callers are unaffected: they already pass through to the real `gh` before this block and get their personal token unchanged.
- Remove `token` from `is_safe_operation` so any future fallthrough fails closed instead of leaking the personal token.
- Add an `AI_ALIGNED_GH_BIN` override to `find_real_gh` (unset in production) so token-exchange paths can be integration-tested against a fake `gh`.

## Tests

`test_auth_token_attribution.sh` (new, 5 assertions):
- AI + cached bot token → returns the bot token; personal token never on stdout.
- No AI detected → personal token passes through unchanged.
- AI + no bot token → fails closed, no personal token leaked.

Existing suites unaffected (`test_safe_operation.sh` 30/30, `test_pr_template_*` green, `test_impersonate.sh` green). The pre-existing `test_priority_order.sh` / `test_timeout.sh` failures reproduce on `main` and are environmental (process-tree AI detection picks up the running agent); not touched here.

author: yairfalse
body:
## Summary

The first of the two "where closed goes next" steps: turns the blunt network lock/open switch into **actual per-zone policy**. A network-locked zone may still reach destinations an operator explicitly permits ("this zone may reach `10.0.0.0/8`"), while everything else non-loopback stays denied.

### How
- **eBPF**: new `EGRESS_CIDR_MAP` — a BPF **LPM trie** keyed by `(zone_id, ipv4)`. `zone_id` matched exactly; the IPv4 address longest-prefix matched for CIDR semantics. Address stored network-byte-order on both sides (eBPF reads raw `sin_addr`; userspace writes `u32::from(ip).to_be()`) so the kernel LPM trie compares the same bytes.
- `socket_connect` / `socket_sendmsg` consult the allowlist before denying a non-loopback IPv4 destination; `socket_bind` does **not** (it governs local listeners, not egress). All still honor audit mode.
- **Control surface**: proto `ZonePolicy.allowed_egress_cidrs` (field 6), wired through the file adapter (TOML `network.allowed_egress`), k8s CRD (new `network.allowedEgress`), and REST (defaults empty). Sourced from the previously-unenforced `network.allowed_egress`.

### Scope (v1, documented)
IPv4 CIDR granularity only. **IPv6 and port-level policy (`CIDR:port`) are explicit follow-ups** — non-IPv4 entries are skipped with a warning rather than failing the zone. (Your example had a port; that's the next increment.)

## Lima evidence
`verify-egress-cidr` (new) — a locked zone allowed `<host-ip>/32`:
- `allowlisted connect  -> …:9 : ECONNREFUSED (NOT EPERM — CIDR allows)`
- `allowlisted sendto   -> …:9 : OK sendto (NOT EPERM — CIDR allows)`
- `blocked connect -> 192.0.2.1:9 : DENIED EPERM, socket_connect deny_delta=1`
- `blocked sendto  -> 192.0.2.1:9 : DENIED EPERM, socket_sendmsg deny_delta=1`
- `bind -> …:0 : DENIED EPERM (allowlist does not relax bind)`

Plus `verify-runtime` (9/9 hooks attach with the LPM map) and `verify-network-lock` unchanged (base lockdown un-regressed). Regression of container/k8s/audit/cgroup-escape gates running.

## Also verified
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (Linux), `cargo test --workspace` (Linux + macOS host, incl. a `parse_ipv4_cidr` unit test), `make macos-check`, `check-proto` / `check-release-docs` / `check-api-docs` / `check-openapi` / `check-syvactl-contract`.

author: eriknewton
body:
## Summary

Lands the anomaly subsystem's named forward-list item (detector catalog header and features doc "Extension Points For Chi-8+"): a deterministic, operator-facing root-cause-hint layer built from the drift attribution findings already carry. No new detector, classifier, scoring, severity, or persisted-state change; the layer annotates finding details at routing time only.

## Design: seam choice

Hints are attached at a single seam: `routeFinding` in `server/src/anomaly-detection/anomaly-pipeline.ts`. Every finding flows through it, including the `audit-event-class-distribution` detector's custom `evaluate()` override, so all 7 detectors (and any future detector) get hints with zero per-detector edits. The alternative seam, `buildAnomalyFinding` in `types.ts`, would have missed the custom-override finding builders and required duplicate wiring.

The enrichment is fail-closed by construction (`enrichDetailsWithRootCauseHints`): a thrown error inside hint generation degrades to an empty hints array, and a details-copy failure degrades to the original details unchanged. The finding is the security signal and always survives.

## Hint-table coverage

`server/src/anomaly-detection/root-cause-hints.ts` maps real emitted feature names (verified against each feature extractor) to detector-specific likely-cause text for all 7 shipped detectors:

| Detector | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `per-agent-activity` | all 5 count features (tool/egress/credential/audit/receipt) |
| `cross-agent-timing` | co-fire rate (lockstep shape), p50/p99 inter-event time, correlation strength |
| `tool-call-sequence` | distinct tools, sequence length, 3-gram entropy, repeat-pattern score (exfiltration-shaped loop) |
| `audit-event-class-distribution` | `total_events`, `class_count:*` / `class_proportion:*` prefixes, plus `per_class_drift` attribution (top 3, flat skipped, mirrored contributions deduplicated) |
| `credential-use-sequence` | event count, distinct credentials (credential-enumeration shape), repeat-pair score, 5-minute burst (dump shape) |
| `cross-agent-distribution` | `peer_z:*` prefix (cohort divergence, hotter/quieter), `peer_count` |
| `time-of-day-activity` | `band_count:*` / `band_proportion:*` (night band reads as off-hours/exfiltration-window signal), `active_band_count` |

Selection rules: contribution earns a hint at |z| >= 1 (matches the severity floor), sign picks above/below baseline, sorted by |z| then feature name, capped at 5. Unknown detector ids and unknown features degrade to a generic hint built only from the contribution stats; malformed or missing attribution degrades to an empty array; never throws into the dispatcher. Hints are built only from numeric contribution stats, feature names, audit-operation class names, and detector ids; no raw audit payloads, secrets, or key material can reach a hint.

## Tests

29 new tests in `server/test/anomaly-detection/root-cause-hints.test.ts` (mirrors the Chi-7 suite structure): per-detector positive mapping for all 7 detectors, direction thresholds (sub-1-sigma silence, exact-threshold fire, sign-to-direction), ordering/cap/determinism, unknown-detector and unknown-feature fallback, empty/missing/malformed attribution, `per_class_drift` mapping (up/down, flat skipped, top-3 cap, dedup, null z), fail-closed wrapper (forced-throw builder, hostile-getter details), dispatcher integration (hints in store + tick return + listener emit; hostile finding still persists), and no-leakage assertions.

## Gates

- `npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npm test`: 507 files passed (1 skipped), 6185 tests passed (8 skipped), zero transform/collection errors, baseline floor 6000 cleared
- `npx eslint src --max-warnings=4`: 4 pre-existing warnings, 0 new

author: ryannono
body:
Stacked on #8167 (BP7 palette). Review that one first; this PR's diff is against the palette branch, so it shows only the semantic layer.

## What this adds

The BP7 semantic token layer as a preview: intents, surfaces, typography, and emphasis. Every file lives under `tokens/next/`, which the Style Dictionary config does not glob, so the build still emits BP6 only. Nothing here changes shipped output.

## Intents are the single source

The five intents (`neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`) drive everything. Each surface and text color resolves from an intent through a `com.blueprint.derive` extension that applies OKLCH lightness/chroma/hue offsets plus alpha. No surface or text token hard-codes a palette stop, so changing the palette repaints every surface without editing a surface token.

## Surfaces

A three-tier layer model keeps tinting controllable:

1. `layer-opacity`: one lever for tint strength.
2. `layer-color`: the intent at that opacity. `rest` is the raw intent; `hover` and `active` derive a fixed OKLCH offset from it.
3. `layer`: that color wrapped in `linear-gradient()` so it composites as a background-image.

Borders lighten the intent toward its `.200` tint in light mode and use the raw intent in dark. Dividers carry the Figma alphas (9%/12% light, 12%/20% dark).

## Typography

Follows the Figma type export:

- 13 composite styles under `styles.{code,body,heading}.*`, each referencing the `size`/`weight`/`family` primitives rather than inlining numbers.
- Per-style line-height stored as a unitless ratio.
- `runningLineHeight` on `body.medium`/`body.large` for multi-line running text.
- A `display` family slot (placeholder system stack, swappable when a display face is chosen).
- Letter-spacing held at 0, because tracking is font-specific and Blueprint ships font-less.

## Naming

`intent.default` became `intent.neutral` and `app` became `base`. The intents now read as role words (`neutral / primary / success / warning / danger`), and no-intent (`base`) stays distinct from the fallback-sense `default` still used for font family, weight, and the non-strong divider.

author: tas50
body:
Part of the series reviewing every remediation in `content/` for correctness (#2775, #2780–#2835). This PR covers `mondoo-atlassian-security.mql.yaml`: all 7 checks were reviewed and all 7 needed fixes. Policy version bumped. Verified against the atlassian provider schema and implementation, the checked-in Atlassian OpenAPI specs, and current Atlassian support documentation.

## Remediation surfaces that do not exist

- **admin-no-stale-api-tokens** sent admins to a per-account \"API tokens\" tab under Managed accounts; no such tab exists. Managed-account tokens are reviewed and revoked centrally at **Insights > API token activity**, now in both remediation and audit, with the permanence of revocation stated.
- **confluence-no-unlicensed-space-access** looked for an \"unlicensed-user permission row\" in space permissions; none exists. That access is granted through the Jira Service Management knowledge-base integration, so the fix now goes through **Project settings > Knowledge base > Who can view** per linked service project, with the site-wide **JSM Access** gate as the structural control. The refs URL for portal customers 404s and is replaced with the live doc.
- **confluence-no-anonymous-space-access** used the outdated Space settings path; now **More actions > Space settings > Space access > Anonymous access**, plus the site-level setting that stops space admins reintroducing public access — with the drift note that the space-level entries the check reads must still be cleared.
- **jira-no-anonymous-permission-grants** offered a holder label that doesn't exist in the grant dialog; the authenticated catch-all is **Any logged in user**.

## Flows that stopped one step short

The IP-allowlist remediation never mentioned the separate **Activate IP allowlist** action — an allowlist created but not activated keeps `status` at disabled and the check failing — nor the Premium/Enterprise plan prerequisite without which the steps can't be followed. Domain verification now includes identity-provider verification and the real **Claim accounts** location (Directory > Domains, not Managed accounts).

## Audit corrections

The verified-domains audit claimed passing = `type == \"verified\"` — the API's `type` is the JSON:API discriminator, always `\"domains\"`; verification lives in `attributes.claim.status`. The dormant-users audit referenced list filters that couldn't be verified to exist and now uses the documented CSV export. The Confluence anonymous-grant field is the `anonymousAccess` boolean, not `subjects.anonymous`.

## Left for maintainers (never-pass check)

**admin-verified-domains-configured** can never pass: the provider populates `domain.type` from the JSON:API resource discriminator, whose only enum value is `\"domains\"`, so `any(type == \"verified\")` matches nothing on any organization. The go-atlassian model carries `attributes.claim.status` but the provider never reads it. Fixing requires a provider field (e.g. `claimStatus`) plus an mql change; the `.lr` doc comment \"Domain type (e.g., verified)\" likely seeded the error.

## Validation

- `cnspec policy lint` passes
- YAML parses clean; no mql changed

author: ashenfad
body:
Three iterations from continued live two-device testing (follows #44):

## 1. App-state directory seeding (`d2c945b`)
The surviving console 404 after #44's listing-index fix was the directory listing itself — it 404s once per sweep until any device ever pushes app state, and browsers log the response regardless of handling. On a not-found listing the engine now seeds the `app-state` branch with a `.keep` file (one-time, self-healing for existing connections, failure-tolerant). Every future listing on every device is a clean 200; the index filters to `*.json` so the keep file never reads as a session.

## 2. Determinate, row-visible upload progress (`d8932b1`)
A long session's first push looks like a hang: the client deliberately paces mutations ~750ms apiece (secondary-limit budget), so a 100-turn initial upload takes minutes — and the live count was hidden in a tooltip. Now: while syncing, the session row swaps its date for the live detail, and a **first-ever push is determinate** (`uploading · turn 37 of 120`) because its delta is the full local history, countable locally for free. One subtlety worth review attention: the branch-existence probe reads the storage key directly because `VersionedKV.open` *creates* missing branches — which would poison the stub-download path. Pull totals remain a future kvgit API addition (the remote walk knows them; the generator interface doesn't expose them).

## 3. App-state opt-out + orphan-squash (`cd4cb9c`)
The structural answer to "snapshots could dominate the repo": app-state needs no history (LWW reads the tip only), yet every save was a permanently-reachable commit. Every 25 pushes the engine squashes the `app-state` branch to a **parentless commit carrying the current tree**, force-moved into place — identical content, zero ancestry, everything older unreachable for GitHub GC. (Known small race documented in place: a concurrent push between read and force-move loses one LWW snapshot the next save re-writes.) Plus the controls: a global **"Sync app save data"** setting — default **on**, since squashing handles the size concern structurally and default-off would silently break pick-up-on-your-phone — and a 2MB bag cap (warn-once, skip).

Concurrency note (discussed, deliberate): same app running on two devices simultaneously is whole-bag last-writer-wins — bounded loss at reload, by design for the sequential pick-up pattern. Per-key LWW is the documented next rung if it ever bites.

## Tests
3 new (suite 707): squash-to-orphan after N pushes (parentless commit + force move asserted via the contents-API fake), the `syncAppState` off-switch (no pushes, pulls, or seeding), and directory seeding on first contact.

author: markatmutter-cloud
body:
## What & why

Mark: *"Sotheby's shows as a link, the lots are live, but no listing available."* The auction **calendar** still listed Sotheby's sales, but the **catalogues were empty** — `public/auction_lots.json` held **1** Sotheby's lot vs 630 Christie's / 624 Phillips.

**Root cause:** Sotheby's stopped server-rendering the `algoliaJson` payload into the auction page (`pageProps.algoliaJson` is now `null`; only the first 48 lots ship inline as a `lotCardsConnection`). `enumerate_sothebys` keyed off `algoliaJson` for both the lot list *and* the bootstrap-lot slug, so every sale logged `algoliaJson: 0 hits / no bootstrap slug → 0 lots kept`.

## Fix

Rewrote `enumerate_sothebys` to drive the site's own Cosmo **GraphQL** router (`clientapi.prod.sothelabs.com/graphql`):
1. Fetch the auction page → `auctionId` (raw uuid) + sale metadata (title / currency / slug / end-date) from `apolloCache`.
2. Paginate the page's own `LotCardsFilterByPaginated` query (inlined **self-contained** so a JS chunk-hash redeploy can't break it; introspection is disabled on the router but arbitrary valid queries run) by `offset`/`limit`.

Each card carries title, lot number, estimate, image (brightspot CDN), and — on closed sales — the realised price (`bidState.sold.ResultVisible.premiums.finalPrice`). One ~5-call walk replaces the old per-lot fetch storm. Removed the now-orphaned `_scrape_sothebys_lot_full` / `scrape_sothebys_lot_image` helpers.

## Verified the real path (not a mock)
- **Live** Fine Watches → **414 watch lots**, all with estimate + image
- **Closed** sale → **160 lots all with realised prices** (e.g. 204,800 CHF), per-lot currency correct
- `is_excluded_title` correctly drops the handful of non-watches (pocket watches/clocks)

## Trade-off
Lot descriptions/essays aren't in the card payload, so `description` = maker + title and the essay fields are empty. That's the card data the feed needs; the per-lot essay fetch was the slow, WAF-risky part — dropped deliberately.

## Tests
`tests/test_sothebys_lots.py` pins the `_sothebys_card_to_lot` transform (estimate / sold-price / image rendition / maker-prepend / exclusion). 48 pytest green. CLAUDE.md Sotheby's note updated.

author: anuragid
body:
## Summary

- **Bug fixed**: `require_byok_credits` in `backend/app/dependencies/byok_gate.py:87` called `get_cached_balance(db, user, max_age_seconds=0)`, bypassing the persisted-balance cache on every Analyze click. This forced two synchronous httpx GETs to OpenRouter (10 s timeout each) directly on the FastAPI event loop, causing ~20 s click-to-response latency and stalling all concurrent requests.
- **Fix**: Pass `max_age_seconds=settings.BALANCE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` (default 60 s) so a recently-fetched balance is returned immediately from the DB row — zero network calls on the hot path.
- **Authoritative fresh check preserved**: `analyze_chunk_step` calls `resolve_byok_with_preflight(force_refresh=True)` (`analysis_steps.py:334-338`) which passes `max_age_seconds=0`. This live fetch happens before any LLM spend. A user who exhausted credits after the route check is caught here and surfaces as `InsufficientCreditsError` → `InsufficientCreditsNonRetryable` with structured `error_type=insufficient_credits` payload (`byok_service.py:167-168`, `analysis_steps.py:83-103`).

## Reviewer attack surface: stale cache letting zero-balance through

**Q: Can a user with $0 credits enqueue a task?**

Yes — if they had credits when the route check ran (cache hit) but ran out before the task started. But:

1. **Task-side preflight catches it**: `analyze_chunk_step` forces a fresh balance check (`force_refresh=True`, `analysis_steps.py:338`) _before_ calling any LLM node. `InsufficientCreditsError` is raised → wrapped in `InsufficientCreditsNonRetryable` → `_update_analysis_error` stamps `video.error_message` with `{"error_type": "insufficient_credits", "retryable": false, "balance": {...}}` → frontend renders the "Add credits" alert. No LLM spend occurs.

2. **Worst case window**: 60 seconds (default TTL). Practically, a user running out of credits mid-session is far rarer than the 20 s stall bug hitting every legitimate user on every click.

**Q: Does saving a new BYOK key bust the cache?**

Yes — `users.py:250-265` does a live balance fetch, rejects $0-credit keys immediately (400), then writes the fresh balance to `key_balance_checked_at = balance.checked_at` (now). The cache is warmed immediately. Key removal nulls `key_balance_checked_at` (`users.py:484`), making `build_balance_from_persisted` return `None` on the next gate hit (treated as pass-through).

## TDD evidence

Three tests added/updated in `tests/test_byok_gate.py`:

| Test | Assertion |
|------|-----------|

## Summary

PR #27's loudness pass-1 broke the assemble that follows it: `@ffmpeg/ffmpeg`'s `writeFile` **transfers** the buffer to the worker (detaching it on the main thread), and the measurement wrote each narration clip's actual `Uint8Array`. The subsequent `assemble()` then tried to write those same, now-detached arrays → `attempting to access detached ArrayBuffer`.

Fix: `measureLoudness` writes a copy (`clip.slice()`) so measurement is a true side-read and the caller's bytes survive for the render. The WAVs are tens of KB, so the copies are negligible.

## Test Plan

- [x] `npm run build`, `npm run test:run` — 296 passing (the transfer behavior lives in the wasm worker boundary, not reachable in jsdom; the fix is the documented copy)
- [ ] After deploy: assemble the scene again — measurement (k/n) should complete and the render should start instead of erroring

- Neuer GitHub-Actions-Workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: läuft bei jedem Pull Request und kann manuell getriggert werden (`workflow_dispatch`)
- Schritte: Node 22 mit npm-Cache → `npm ci` → `npm run build` → `npm run build:standalone` → Vitest mit JSON- und JUnit-Reporter
- **Testergebnis im Action-Summary:** `.github/scripts/test-summary.mjs` schreibt das Vitest-JSON als Markdown ins Step-Summary (`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`): Ergebnistabelle, bei Fehlschlägen die Fehlermeldungen (ANSI-Codes entfernt) und eine aufklappbare Liste aller Tests – ohne Dritt-Action

author: jordanpartridge
body:
Root cause of the Solo 🧪 Tests process never finishing (and the reason the old composer 300s timeout kept 'failing' it — see #151).

## The bug

`PlayerCommandTest`'s loop tests pass the interactivity guard and enter the player's `while` loop. They only terminated because Laravel Prompts' `select()` throws on EOF when stdin is **not** a TTY (CI, pipes, sandboxes). Run the same suite in a real terminal and `select()` renders and blocks on keyboard input forever — the suite hangs deterministically right after `PlayCommandTest`, every time. Reproduced and verified with `script(1)`.

## The fix

- **`tests/Pest.php`**: route Prompts through the Symfony question fallback suite-wide (`Prompt::fallbackWhen(true)` in a `beforeEach`). `fallbackWhen()` ORs into sticky static state, so setting it per-file would make other files' behavior depend on test order — suite-wide is the only deterministic placement.
- **`PlayerCommandTest`**: the two loop tests now drive the prompt explicitly (`expectsQuestion(..., 'exit')`) and assert the goodbye path, instead of relying on EOF-throw side effects.
- **`SetupCommandTest`**: the `--reset` test now stubs its confirmation (`expectsConfirmation(..., 'no')`) — it previously leaned on the non-interactive default.

## Verification

- Full suite piped: 716 passed (2132 assertions)
- Full suite under a pseudo-TTY via `script(1)`: **716 passed, exit 0** — previously hung indefinitely
- Pint, PHPStan, Rector all clean

author: omirmaj
body:
## The #1 scheduler upgrade from the research — and the one competitors lack

Your scheduler already out-classes the SMB field on **planning** (CPM, baselines, EVM, dependencies). The research finding was that the missing layer is **production control** — Lean construction's **Last Planner System**: the lookahead → make-ready → weekly-commitment → reliability loop that actually prevents residential jobs from slipping. Touchplan/Outbuild are whole companies built on just this; **Buildertrend and Knowify don't have it.** ([Lean Construction Institute](https://leanconstruction.org/lean-topics/last-planner-system/), [Touchplan/PPC](https://touchplan.io/blog/why-percent-promises-complete-ppc-is-critical-to-construction-productivity/))

This builds it, sitting on top of your existing CPM schedule. **Works on mobile *and* web** (same screen, RN Web, centered max-width column).

### Three views
- **Lookahead (CAN)** — next 3 weeks; each task gated by a **constraint log** (materials / permit / prior work / selection / inspection / …). Open constraints → "Constrained"; flagged **at-risk** when a need-by date threatens the task start. Tap to clear.
- **This Week (WILL / DID)** — the **weekly work plan**: commit the work the crew *will* finish; at week's end mark each **kept or missed**. Warns if you commit still-constrained work. Then **push each crew their committed slice** (see below).
- **Reliability (LEARN)** — **PPC** (% of commitments kept, Lean target **80–85%**), the weekly trend, and a ranked **"what's costing you"** variance breakdown — the learning step that drives PPC up.

### Crew "this week" push — closes the loop ✅
Once the weekly work plan is committed, **"Send the week to your crews"** pushes each sub/crew exactly their slice — **email** when a contact is on file, **native share** (SMS/WhatsApp) otherwise. Competitors blast the whole schedule to everyone; this is the opposite: **opt-in, scoped to committed tasks only**, with "sent" state tracked per crew. This was listed as a follow-up in the original cut — it's now built here.

### What's in it
- **`utils/lastPlanner.ts`** — pure engine (date math, readiness, lookahead/WWP assembly, PPC + variance analytics). **28/28** on a throwaway harness — which caught a real bug (done tasks leaking into the weekly plan). Removed before commit.
- **`utils/crewDispatch.ts`** — pure crew-grouping + message/HTML formatting engine (groups by assigned sub → free-text sub → crew lane → unassigned; contactable crews first, unassigned last; HTML-escaped email body). **14/14** on a throwaway harness. Removed before commit.
- **`hooks/useLastPlanner.ts`** — local-first per-project constraints + commitments + crew dispatches (`tertiary_last_planner`). Cloud sync is a follow-up.
- **`app/last-planner.tsx`** — Pro-gated (`schedule_gantt_pdf`), responsive. Its readiness constraints are deliberately **separate** from `ScheduleTask.anchorType` (CPM date pins) and never touch the CPM engine. Email path reuses the existing `send-email` edge function.
- **Registered everywhere**: mobile route (`_layout`), **web nav** (`DesktopSidebar`, OVERVIEW), and Tools → FIELD.

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; lint **0 new warnings** on changed files.
- Engine harnesses **28/28** (Last Planner) + **14/14** (crew dispatch).
- ⚠️ Not run on device/web — exercise the commit→review→PPC loop, the crew send (email + share), and the desktop layout on hardware.

### Follow-ups (from the research, not in this PR)
Weather-driven auto-reschedule + delay-day log; conversational schedule agent (ALICE-style) on mageAI. Documented in the research summary.

author: bg9m9r
body:
A collapsible right-edge drawer that logs every game action so a player
can answer "what just happened?" when there's no animation. Reuses the
SignalR event stream: the store's `announcementFor` is generalized into a
structured `describeEvent` (log.types.ts) that feeds BOTH the aria-live
region and a new scrollable `logEntries` buffer in `GameStore`.

What's logged: casts, activated/triggered abilities, stack resolutions,
life changes, counters, ETB/death/exile card moves, continuous-effect
add/remove (CR 613 layers), and game-loss. Turn/phase lines are dimmed;
rows are color-coded self vs foe. Closed by default; auto-scrolls to the
newest entry. **Passing priority is never logged** (the engine emits no
event for it).

Implementation notes:
- `announcementFor` is now a thin wrapper `describeEvent(...)?.text ?? null`,
  so the aria-live behaviour is unchanged (existing specs stay green).
- `applyEvent` captures the line right after the seq gate, before the
  patch attempt, and appends it unconditionally — so events that force a
  `/state` refetch (unpatchable) still log.
- `ContinuousEffectAdded/RemovedEvent` are handled as reducer no-ops
  (return state) so layer mutations don't trigger a refetch storm.
- `StackObjectAddedEvent` of `kind: 'spell'` is skipped (the `SpellCastEvent`
  already logged that line) to avoid duplicates.

Degradation: the layer-effect lines depend on the core continuous-effect
events (PR bg9m9r/majik#2618) being deployed to majik-api. Every other
line works regardless, and the portal degrades gracefully if the API
lacks those events (they simply never arrive — no error).

Tests: 721 pass (was 706; +15 new across log.types, game.store, the
reducer no-op, and the game-log component). Visual verification pending.

author: rod-feuer
body:
## What

Replaces the bare type/paste emoji input with a **searchable grid of curated emojis** for picking category icons — in both the badge editor (existing categories) and the New-category form.

## Why this shape

The app deliberately runs on a lean dependency set (no UI component libraries). A full emoji-picker package would add thousands of glyphs, skin tones, and bundle weight for a job that only needs "the kinds of things a budget category is." So this is an in-app curated set: ~120 hand-picked emojis (dining, groceries, home, utilities, transport, travel, kids, sports, health, money, shopping, entertainment, pets, work, gifts), each tagged with lowercase keywords so search matches by meaning (`car` → 🚗, `bill` → 🧾).

## Implementation

- **`lib/emoji.ts`** — the curated `CATEGORY_EMOJIS` list (`{char, keywords}`).
- **`EmojiPicker`** — search box + grid. A pasted emoji that isn't in the curated set is still offered as a "use this" tile, so the any-emoji escape hatch survives.
- **Category badge popover** — picker inline, color palette below.
- **New-category form** — `EmojiButton` (shows the current emoji, opens the picker popover) replaces the old icon text input.

## Verification

- New test: the set has **unique chars** (React keys won't collide) and **lowercase keywords** (search can't silently miss), and a representative search resolves to the right glyph. **72/72 pass**, `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Categories page compiles and serves on the dev server.

author: iainn
body:
Change CH-WBXZPK · primitive: fix

Closes the four dogfooding lessons surfaced while shipping the daemon-wedge change, plus a hardening of the daemon grace parser found by reflecting on where property-based testing would have helped.

- **#334** — `branch-ci` now triggers on the canonical `wp/**` branch shape (was `feat/wp-*` + `change/*` only). A correctly-named WP branch gets CI directly, so the merge train no longer hangs polling a run that never starts.
- **#336** — the executor resolves its branch via `wpx-wp branch-name` (canonical `wp/{primitive-slug}/wp-NNN-*`) instead of hand-templating `feat/wp-NNN-*`. The train's `queue-list` finds it and (with #334) CI triggers.
- **#335** — the engineering-architect body now pins the canonical INDEX header and mandates `wpx-index lint` (which already catches a drifted header, exit 1) after writing INDEX.md.
- **#337** — `wpx-step12 wrap` force-removes the worktree so executor-left untracked sidecars can't strand the wrap at `step-7-held`.
- **inf-harden** — `resolve_wedge_grace_secs` / `resolve_idle_exit_secs` reject non-finite overrides (`inf`/`1e400` parse cleanly and pass `> 0` → an *infinite* window that silently disables the self-heal). Added a Hypothesis property test that catches it; example tests alone missed it.

Daemon suite 83 passed; step12/worktree 77 passed; ruff clean. #337 is a one-flag wiring of the already-tested `wpx-worktree remove --force`.

Closes #334. Closes #335. Closes #336. Closes #337.

author: predixx
body:
## What

Extracts a single sensing layer: `services/sensing/` now owns every VS Code event subscription and behavioral state read used by telemetry. The session recorder, the EQ pipeline, and the v1 inactivity/diagnostics services consume typed hub channels instead of subscribing to `vscode.*` themselves. Zero behavior change: recordings stay schema-v2 identical.

Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-struggle-engine-v2-port.md` (PR 1 of the struggle-engine-v2 effort; all PRs of this effort target `feat/struggle-engine-v2`, not `dev`).

## How

- `SensorHub` interface + `VsCodeSensorHub`: one lazy relay per VS Code API. A channel subscribes to its source only while at least one consumer is attached, so consent-scoped consumers still produce consent-scoped VS Code listeners (the untouched `terminalShellExecution` test proves it). Per-listener error isolation, per-subscription refcounting, post-dispose inertness.
- Save-triggered diagnostics settle snapshot (500 ms LS settle, coalescing) moved from `CompileEquivalentEmitter` into `sensing/collectors/diagnosticsSettle.ts`. The emitter keeps the EQ pairing logic and now drops cross-session settles via a monotonic ordering token (`savedSeq`), reproducing v1's clear-timer-at-session-start semantics without same-millisecond ambiguity.
- All policy (phase gates, generation tokens, URI filters, debounces) stayed in the consumers; handler bodies are byte-identical, only the subscription expressions changed.
- Production wiring creates exactly one hub (`extension.ts`) and injects it everywhere; classes keep optional owned defaults so tests construct them standalone.
- `TestSensorHub` double for deterministic lifecycle tests.

## Equivalence proof

1. Existing suites pass unchanged: unit 1344/0, struggle 135, recorder-e2e 9, react/logic 865/0 (only test change: a construction site in the wiring test got the injected hub; assertions untouched).
2. New targeted lifecycle tests (`observationLifecycle.test.ts`): debounce coalescing, consent-downgrade discard, end-flush ordering, session isolation; plus EQ settle-path tests including the cross-session guard and pre-session v1 parity.
3. Clean bundle: `verify-clean-bundle.js` green on the openvsx variant (sensing is in, recorder/consent stay out).
4. Manual before/after recording field-diff: DONE (2026-06-13). Two comparable interactive dev-host sessions against the same exercise (19570), one on the base branch (pre-refactor recorder), one on this branch: open file, type, save 3-4x, select, scroll, terminal, file switches, end session. Result: schema v2 on both; the per-type field sets are IDENTICAL for every common event type (incl. `eqSnapshot`: `confidence/eq/source/timestamp/type`); both sessions bracket cleanly (`sessionStart` first, `sessionEnd` last); event counts per type are in the same range with differences fully explained by session content (the sessions were similar, not scripted identically; e.g. `viewNavigation` only occurred in the base session, `terminalCommand`/`textDocumentClose` only in the refactored one). The EQ settle path produced 3 `eqSnapshot` events in both sessions. `validate-recording` passes on both; the handful of timestamp-regression warnings appear on both sides and on a pre-refactor recording from 2026-06-02 (debounce design: payload stamped at trigger, written later), so they are pre-existing, not refactor drift.

## Notes for later PRs

- `sensing/collectors/diagnosticsSettle.ts` imports `shouldRecordUri` from `services/telemetry/uriFilter`; when `services/telemetry` dissolves (PR 2/PR 5), `uriFilter` should move to a neutral location.
- The known micro-difference (documented in the plan's decision log): the `struggleDetection.enabled` gate for the EQ save path moved from save-time to settle-time; only observable when the setting flips inside the 500 ms settle window.

body:
## What

Adds an option in **Admin → Students** to reset a student's speaking **trials** for a selected task — each challenge speaking task **and** the level test. Resetting gives the student a fresh set of attempts (`MAX_TRIALS` = 2).

When you expand a student → a challenge (or the *Level test*), there's now a **Speaking trials** section showing `used / 2` per task with a **Reset trials** button (disabled when nothing's been used).

## Why it needed more than a delete button

Trials are enforced server-side in `x50_trials` (keyed by **auth `user_id`**), but the admin Students view groups everyone by their display name (`"name - job"`). So the change had to:

1. **Bridge name → user_id** via `x50_students` (admin can already read all rows).
2. **Reset the right `task_id`** — `level_test`, `challenge_<id>`, or `challenge_<id>#<index>` — computed with the same `serverTaskKey()` the student app uses.
3. **Actually free the student.** The client previously took `max(server, localStorage)` for the attempts count, which would mask a server-side reset. `fetchServerTrials` now returns `0` (not `null`) on a clean read with no row, and `SpeakingTask`/`LevelTest` mirror the server count exactly — so a reset propagates while clearing the browser still can't (the server is authoritative).

## Changes

- **`supabase/reset_trials.sql`** (new) — `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC `x50_reset_trial(p_user, p_task)` that self-checks the admin email then deletes the `(user, task)` counter row. Same admin-gate pattern as the rest of the project.
- **`src/pages/Admin.tsx`** — `StudentsAdmin` loads `x50_students` + `x50_trials`, resolves `user_id`, and renders the per-task reset UI in `ChallengePanel`.
- **`src/lib/progress.ts`** — `fetchServerTrials` distinguishes "no row" (`0`) from "couldn't read" (`null`).
- **`src/components/SpeakingTask.tsx` / `LevelTest.tsx`** — sync mirrors the server count instead of `max(server, local)`.

## ⚠️ Deploy step

Run **`supabase/reset_trials.sql`** once in the Supabase SQL editor to create the RPC. Without it, the Reset button returns an error.

- `npm run build` passes.
- `eslint` introduces no new errors (the 5 pre-existing `set-state-in-effect` warnings are unchanged).
- Not yet manually verified against a live Supabase instance — the RPC needs to be deployed first.

author: kishiguro
body:
## Summary

**B3** from the peer-membership-list plan (`docs/design/bgp-peer-list.md` §8 step 3). Independent of #1409/#1412 (capability layer only).

RFC 7911 §3 makes negotiated Send a hard wire contract — every NLRI of the family must carry a path-id. Only IPv4-unicast and VPNv4 have the per-candidate twins that honor it. The families that could nevertheless negotiate Send were incoherent:

- **VPNv6 / EVPN / LU-v4 / LU-v6**: reach stamps `local_id`, withdraw hardcodes `0` — which the emitters encode as **no path-id field** → malformed MP_UNREACH on an AddPath session (RFC 7606 treat-as-withdraw / session reset on a conformant peer); tolerant peers accumulate stale paths forever.
- **IPv6-unicast**: AddPath peers are excluded from the only incremental path, no twin exists → nothing after the initial dump.

`add-path` is configurable on every family (no YANG `when`), so one config line armed this.

### Fix — at the capability layer

- `addpath_send_implemented()` pins the supported set (v4-unicast, VPNv4), with a test that forces the set to grow only together with real per-family twins.
- OPEN build: pure `send` config on an unsupported family → capability withheld; `send-receive` → downgraded to `receive`; both `warn!`.
- `cap_addpath_recv` mirrors the gate (negotiated state stays honest against any remote).
- Receive is untouched — path-id parsing is family-generic.

The doc's originally sketched alternative (guard the fan-out scans) is **not wire-safe** — once Send is negotiated, both id-less sends and silence violate the contract; §8.3 updated accordingly.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude bdd`: 1686 passed (2 new); workspace clippy clean
- BDD smoke `@bgp_basic_ebgp` + `@bgp_update_group_ipv4` green on the rebuilt binary

### Note for reviewers
The B2 regression sweep surfaced that `bgp_evpn_capability.feature` has **no Teardown scenario** — it leaked two root daemons + namespaces into my later runs. Trivial follow-up PR if you want it.

author: stan220
body:
## What

Navigating the treemap is now animated in both directions:

- **Entering a folder (LMB)** — the new level starts affinely compressed into the clicked brick (wherever it is drawn at that moment, including mid-flight) and the existing critically damped springs expand it to the full map. Since a folder brick already renders silhouettes of its content, this reads as the folder scaling up to fill the screen.
- **Going up (RMB / Up button)** — the inverse transition: the current map shrinks back into the brick of the folder being left on the parent level.
- Everything else still snaps: first layout, rescan, canvas resize, jumps over several levels, and a folder collapsed into the rest tail.

## Why it needed a view fix

The hover actions panel used to toggle the widget tree between a bare canvas and `stack![canvas, panel]`. A click clears the active brick, removes the panel, and iced rebuilt the canvas widget — wiping the spring state in the same frame, so any navigation animation died before rendering. The canvas now always sits in the stack and the panel is just an optional second layer.

## Implementation

- `Zoom` direction (`In`/`Out`/`Snap`) is derived in the canvas `update` from the tree relation between the displayed level and the navigated-to one; stale ids after a rescan are bounds-checked and snap.
- `MapState::zoom_frames` builds the (`from`, `to`) frame pair; every spring starts at its target remapped via `map_rect` and flies on the same springs (same `STIFFNESS`) used by scan snapshots, so mid-flight retargets stay seamless.
- Hit-testing and labels already follow in-flight bricks — no other changes.

## Tests

New unit tests cover direction detection, the affine remap (round-trip), zoom-in (including starting from a mid-flight brick position), zoom-out, and all snap fallbacks (brick not on screen, folder collapsed into rest, resize in the same frame).

author: rafaelpalomar
body:
## Summary

T3 ResectogramPipeline (#465) **foundation**: the LayerDM Pipeline + dedicated display node + the (u,v) Algorithm helpers, re-authoring the superseded #259 toward an ADR-0013 Pipeline. **This PR is deliberately non-regressive infrastructure** — the actual monolith-sever (the render-path flip) is *not* in it; see "Deferred" below.

## What's in this PR

- **Algorithm helpers** (`vtkLiverResectogramAspectRatio`, `vtkLiverResectogramPixelMapping`) under `LiverResections/Algorithm/` — the (u,v) aspect-ratio + pixel→(u,v) math extracted as pure, CI-testable functions (ADR-0015). Two RED→green unit tests, **run in CI**.
- **`vtkMRMLResectogramDisplayNode`** — a dedicated display-node type so the resectogram Pipeline keys on its own type rather than sharing `vtkMRMLParametricSurfaceDisplayNode` (one Pipeline per display-node type, ADR-0013 §1). Registered via `RegisterNodes()`.
- **`ResectogramPipeline`** + `FlattenedSurface`/`VascularContour` Representations + `registerResectogramPipelineCreator()` (the ADR-0013 §5 `AddPipelineCreator`, keyed on the new display node), wired in `qSlicerLiverResectionsModule::setup()`. No custom DM.
- Test-first scaffolding (ADR-0027): the dispatch test (launched, #460-gated) + visual-regression scenario stubs for the eventual sever/blur.

## Why it's safe to land now (non-regressive)

The Pipeline is **dormant**: nothing in production creates a `vtkMRMLResectogramDisplayNode`, so the creator never fires. The resectogram is **still rendered by the v1 monolith** (`vtkSlicerBezierSurfaceRepresentation3D`) exactly as before. This PR only adds registered, currently-unexercised infrastructure + CI-verified pure-math helpers — no rendering behaviour changes.

## Deferred (NOT in this PR)

- **Monolith-sever** (move the resectogram render off `vtkSlicerBezierSurfaceRepresentation3D` onto the Pipeline) and the **Gaussian blur pass** — these are render-path changes whose equivalence can only be verified by the visual-regression render, which currently **aborts/hangs on every available host** (#475; gate hardening #474). Severing a working render without verification is exactly the risk the soft-gate would hide, so it waits for a working render gate. Tracked under #465.

## Conformance

- ADR-0013 §1 (one Pipeline per display node → dedicated `vtkMRMLResectogramDisplayNode`) + §5 (RegisterNodeClass + RegisterInDefaultViews + AddPipelineCreator).
- ADR-0015 (pure-VTK Algorithm library for the (u,v) math).
- ADR-0025 (the pixel→(u,v) mapping the locator producer consumes).
- ADR-0027 (invariant tests precede implementation).

## Related

- #465 — the T3 issue (this is its foundation slice; sever + blur remain).
- #475 / #474 — the render abort / headless-GL gate that blocks verifying the deferred sever.
- Builds on the just-merged T2.7-2b (#476): a clean rebase merged the `RegisterNodes()` changes (2b removed the legacy registration; this adds the resectogram one).

| Pre-quote | **Reviewing your details…** | Checking whether a couple of quick questions would sharpen your analysis. |

The post-quote variant also reassures the user their quote is actively being read — reinforcing the value rather than implying a step that may be skipped.
