body:
## What

Bumps `tsx` `4.21.0 → 4.22.4` (within the existing `^4.21.0` range) to clear a newly-published **high** advisory on transitive `esbuild`.

## Why

[GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr): `esbuild >=0.17.0 <0.28.1` ships the Deno install module without binary integrity verification, enabling RCE via a malicious `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`. CCSC pulled `esbuild@0.27.7` transitively through the `tsx` devDependency (`tsx@4.21.0` pins `esbuild ~0.27.0`).

This **failed the CI `bun audit --audit-level=high` gate on every PR repo-wide** — a blocking gate in unmodified code, surfaced while working `ccsc-175`. Filed + fixed on its own trail per the readable-bd rule.

`tsx@4.22.4` pins `esbuild ~0.28.0` → resolves the fixed `0.28.1`.

## Risk

Minimal. `tsx`/`esbuild` are **build-time only** (the `npx tsx server.ts` Node fallback path); CCSC never invokes esbuild's Deno installer, so runtime exposure was nil. A compatible minor bump of a devDependency.

## Verification

- `bun audit --audit-level=high --ignore=GHSA-j3q9-mxjg-w52f` → **0 vulnerabilities**
- `bun run typecheck` → clean
- `bun test` → **1156 pass / 0 fail**

Closes `ccsc-dqu`.

- Jeremy Longshore

author: anuragid
body:
## Summary

- **Bug**: All 8 analysis nodes were missing `error_type` on the post-retry validation failure return path (after BOTH the initial call and the in-node retry throw `OutputValidationError`). `_raise_for_node_error` defaults missing `error_type` to `"unknown"`; `is_retryable("unknown")` → `False`; Celery routes through `NonRetryableAnalysisError` → **terminal failure**. A transient LLM truncation/malformed-JSON error became a permanent pipeline failure requiring manual user retry.
- **Fix**: Stamp `error_type="llm_error"` on the post-retry failure `return` in each of the 8 affected nodes: `chunk`, `infer`, `relate`, `explain`, `activate`, `cross_relate`, `cross_explain`, `cross_activate`. `"llm_error"` is classified retryable, so Celery autoretry engages.
- **Scope**: Only the post-retry path is changed. The earlier guard-returns in the same nodes (`validation_error` for empty utterances, all chunks filtered, etc.) remain non-retryable and are untouched.

## Reviewer attack surfaces

**Q: Does this make permanently bad LLM output retry infinitely?**

No. Retry is bounded by the Celery task decorator on each step task in `analysis_steps.py` and `project_analysis_steps.py`:

```python
max_retries=3,
retry_backoff=True,
retry_backoff_max=600,
retry_jitter=True,
```

Worst case: 3 Celery retries × 2 internal node validation attempts = **6 LLM calls**, then Celery exhausts retries and the task fails terminally. This is intentional and correct behavior for a genuinely bad model.

**Q: Did you miss a node?**

No. All 8 nodes were audited with `grep -rn "Output validation failed after retry"`. The 24 new parametrized tests (8 nodes × 3 assertions) cover every node. Each test failed before the fix and passes after.

**Q: Do existing non-retryable tests still pass?**

Yes. The earlier guard-returns (e.g. `"validation_error"` for empty transcripts, filtered-empty chunks) are unchanged and non-retryable. `test_chunk_step_validation_error_is_non_retryable` and all existing tests in `test_analysis_step_non_retryable.py` pass. Full suite: **747 passed, 12 skipped**.

**Q: Why `llm_error` and not a new type?**

`"llm_error"` is the existing canonical category for "the LLM API call succeeded but the output was unusable" — it accurately describes what happened here (LLM returned JSON that passed parsing but failed schema validation twice). No new category is needed.

## Test evidence

```
tests/test_node_post_retry_validation_error_type.py::test_post_retry_validation_failure_sets_error_type[chunk] PASSED
tests/test_node_post_retry_validation_error_type.py::test_post_retry_validation_failure_sets_error_type[infer] PASSED
```

Two upgrades: completes the user-control contract on action cards, and makes installing Olympus a one-liner with a plain-English first run — the Hermes-style experience.

## 1 · One-line install + first-run wizard

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maadjiba24-afk/Olympus-/main/install.sh | sh
```

Then type `olympus`. First run asks one question — which API key you're bringing (Anthropic / OpenAI / any compatible provider) — saves it to `~/.olympus/config.env` (owner-only, chmod 600), and drops straight into plain-English chat. No bash, no pip, no environment variables, ever again.

body:
## Summary
**Stacked on #18 (W7)** — merge that first; this branch includes it. The gate uses W7's `resolved_name` for URL identity matching.

- Adds `RDI_DUP_RUN_GATE=off|on` (default **off**) + `RDI_DUP_RUN_GATE_WINDOW_DAYS` (default 30) + `AnalyzeRequest.force_reanalyze` (default false, bypasses). When a company's evidence fingerprint matches a recent non-failed `company_runs` row, the prior result is copied into a new row for this job instead of re-running the pipeline.
- **Migration**: `ALTER TABLE company_runs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS evidence_fingerprint TEXT` + index on `(company_lookup_key, run_created_at DESC)` (run_created_at, NOT created_at — the upsert never writes created_at) + a partial index on `evidence_fingerprint` for document-mode lookups. Rollback file included.
- **Fingerprints** (shared `src/agent/dup_fingerprint.py`, versioned): pitchdeck `doc-v1` over the file sha256 (multi-file: sorted join); Specter CSV `specter-csv-v1` over the full descriptor JSON (false-negative-biased = safe); URL/LeadGen `identity-v1` over `company_lookup_key + input_mode` — requires W7's `resolved_name`, otherwise the gate safely misses.
- **Reuse** = `persist_reused_company_run`: copies the prior `result_payload`, injects `{reused, reused_from_job_id_legacy, reused_run_created_at}` (also into `summary_rows[0]`), upserts a row for the NEW job with `run_created_at=now`. `_compose_results_payload_from_company_runs` surfaces it with zero results-pipeline changes (test-pinned). Failed prior runs never match.
- **Gate placement**: worker-backed Specter queue (URL hits removed from the task list; CSV hits persisted and skipped by the worker's existing db-backed resume logic, so N/N math holds with `_final_job_outcome` untouched); chunked in-process Specter (reused rows persisted before the resume-key load); document single-company and per-file batch paths (reused payloads merged into the live in-memory results; DB compose ranks them properly on reload).
- Fresh runs persist their fingerprints: document results carry them directly; Specter children receive `--evidence-fingerprint` computed at dispatch (CSV: raw descriptor; URL: resolved identity).
- **UI**: amber "Reused from run <date>" badge on reused rank cards with a force-re-analyze hint.
- Known v1 gaps (called out deliberately): the non-chunked in-memory Specter path doesn't persist fingerprints (its rows just never match); reused rows in live batch results are appended unranked (ranked properly on reload from DB).

## Tests
- New `tests/test_dup_run_gate.py` (18 tests): fingerprint determinism/order-insensitivity per scheme; `find_recent_company_run` filter assembly + failed-row exclusion (fake-client capture); `persist_reused_company_run` marker injection + column set + new-job keys; lookup-key helper parity; compose-path badge fields; `AnalyzeRequest.force_reanalyze`; flag default-off + warn-once window fallback; gate off → zero db lookups; force bypass; hit → persist + progress message; URL-item fingerprint requires resolved_name; reused-payload merge; URL/CSV task fingerprint plumbing.
- Full suite: 592 passed / 15 skipped, with `SUPABASE_URL` unset **and** set. Ruff `F,E9` clean.

- [ ] (pre-merge) apply migration on staging + `scripts/supabase_rls_preflight.py`
- [ ] (post-merge, staging) same deck twice → second instant + badge; `force_reanalyze` re-runs; URL repeat batch skips resolved companies

body:
## Summary

- sex-gate the prostate cancer PRS so it only runs when the caller provides a confident `XY` biological-sex context
- wire `infer_biological_sex()` into both `/api/analysis/cancer/run` and the full `run_all` cancer path before storing cancer PRS findings
- add regressions for `XY`, `XX`, `unknown`, and `manual_review` contexts, including a rerun case that clears a previously stored prostate PRS when the later run is non-`XY`

Closes #153

## Evidence

The bundled prostate score is based on Schumacher et al. 2018, which meta-analyzed prostate-cancer GWAS data in more than 140,000 men and reported prostate PRS risk strata in men [1]. Later prostate PRS validation and screening studies likewise frame the model as prostate-cancer risk stratification in men/prostate-screening cohorts [2], [3]. That supports suppressing the prostate-specific numeric PRS when sex inference is `XX`, `unknown`, or `manual_review`.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/backend/test_cancer_prs.py tests/backend/test_prs_ancestry_mismatch.py -q` -> 66 passed
- `python -m ruff check backend/analysis/cancer_prs.py backend/analysis/run_all.py backend/api/routes/cancer.py tests/backend/test_cancer_prs.py tests/backend/test_prs_ancestry_mismatch.py`
- `python -m ruff format --check backend/analysis/cancer_prs.py backend/analysis/run_all.py backend/api/routes/cancer.py tests/backend/test_cancer_prs.py tests/backend/test_prs_ancestry_mismatch.py`

Local integration note: `tests/backend/test_cross_module_integration.py::TestCrossModuleIntegration::test_cancer_module_processes_panel` first failed during local setup with Huey SQLite unable to open the default DB path; rerunning with `YELIZTLI_DATA_DIR=/tmp/yeliztli-issue-153 YELIZTLI_HUEY_IMMEDIATE=1` hung without output after roughly two minutes and was stopped. Focused backend coverage above passed; CI should exercise the standard backend suite.

## References

author: mike-north
body:
Adds the approved design spec for **expression explanations**: a deterministic, template-based, human-readable rendering of celscript zones aimed at non-technical reviewers (authz approval being the anchor use case). Example target output for `["admin", "super-admin"].includes(user.role)`:

> `user.role` is either `"admin"` or `"super-admin"`

Key decisions recorded in the spec:

- **Standalone explain pass** in a new `@mike-north/celscript-explain` package that walks the zone's TS AST, reusing the existing `ts.Program`/`TypeChecker` — zero added cost on the compile path (alternatives considered and rejected: building on chip-ast; emitting explanations inside the compile walk).
- **Two-level clause/phrase grammar** so templates compose instead of exploding, with bail-out at both levels (opaque clause / code phrase) — explanations can be quieter, never wrong.
- **Gloss-with-markers precision policy**: prose may simplify (e.g. collapsing nullish fallback seams), but every simplification is recorded in the tree — required because reviewers may approve authz policies based on these explanations.
- **Outline as the artifact**, flat-sentence collapse as a renderer policy using scope words ("either / both / any of") as precedence markers.
- **v1 template catalog** mapped row-by-row to `spec/20-lowering.md`, plus drift-control via a conformance corpus and recognizer predicates shared with the emitter.

Docs only — no code changes.

body:
## What

This season's prize code is a **redemption URL** rather than a short code. The winner's results email previously rendered the code in a big **letter-spaced** box styled for short codes — which mangles a long URL visually and leaves it non-clickable.

Now `emailResults` (`src/common/queries.py`) checks the code: an **`http(s)` URL** renders as a tappable `<a>` link (`word-break:break-all` so it wraps, no letter-spacing) under *"redeem here:"*; a **plain code** keeps the existing letter-spaced box under *"redeem with this code:"*. Only `http(s)` is linkified, so any non-web scheme (e.g. a stray `javascript:`) falls back to plain text. The value is HTML-escaped, so query-string `&` is safe (`&`).

Generalizes the single rendering into the two real cases rather than special-casing this year's URL — next year's short code still works unchanged.

## Testing

- **68 unit tests pass** (1 new): `test_email_results_renders_url_code_as_link` asserts the winner's email has an escaped `href`, says "redeem here:", and that the loser gets no link; the existing one-winner test now also pins that a short code stays a non-link letter-spaced box.
- Docs: `api.env.example` + README note that `GIFT_CARD_CODE` may be a code or a URL.

## Context

Follow-up to #14 (the gift-card prize). After this merges + deploys, the prize gets armed on the Pi with the real `$20 Amazon Gift Card` URL for `GIFT_CARD_YEAR=2026`.

author: cmgrote
body:
## Summary

- Completes the P001–P018 error-recovery rule catalog and implements fully-deterministic AST-based checks for all 18 rules — migrating the read-only detection from the LLM-driven `/signal-over-noise surface` mode into the conformance suite
- Adds inline suppression via `# conformance: ignore[Pxxx] <reason>` (trailing or line-above); suppressed findings emit as SARIF `inSource` suppressions for an audit trail and never fail the gate
- Enables the P-series alongside C-series in the conformance CI gate (`--series C,P`); the gate will go red on this repo's own BLOCK violations by design — dogfooding the tool before triage

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `conformance/suite/rules/error_recovery.py` | Added P011, P014–P018 `RuleDefinition` entries |
| `conformance/suite/checks/error_recovery.py` | **New** — `Checker` AST visitor for all 18 rules + suppression directive parsing |
| `conformance/suite/schema/findings.py` | Extended `Finding` with `suppressed` / `suppression_justification`; `findings_to_report()` passes `Suppression` to builder |
| `conformance/suite/runner.py` | Registered P-series; suppression-aware summary and annotations |
| `conformance/tests/test_error_recovery.py` | **New** — 125 tests (positive, negative, carve-out, suppression) for every rule |
| `conformance/tests/test_catalog.py` | Extended P-series presence set to include P011, P014–P018 |
| `conformance/docs/schema-contract.md` | Added §5b with P001–P018 anchor sections |
| `.github/workflows/conformance-ci.yaml` | `--series C` → `--series C,P`; paths-filter extended to `**/*.py` |
| `.claude/skills/signal-over-noise/SKILL.md` | Noted that detection is now delegated to `suite.runner --series P` |

## Determinism guarantee

Every rule's acceptable conditions are baked into the AST predicates. Rules with irreducible contextual residue (P008, P010, P011, P018) are handled by the suppression directive — never by hidden heuristics. Same source text always produces the same findings.

## CI will go red — intentionally

Enabling `--series P` while BLOCK violations exist in `application_sdk/` is the desired first result. The self-scan surfaces ~36 BLOCK findings (P002, P013) in live source — these are real violations to triage, not false positives. The gate can be manually overridden while the follow-up triage/fix pass happens.

## Test plan

- [x] `PYTHONPATH=conformance uv run pytest conformance/tests/ -q` — 194 passed
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=conformance uv run python -m suite.runner --repo . --series P` — human summary lists real violations with correct rule IDs and line numbers
- [x] Conformance CI job runs `--series C,P` and surfaces P-series findings as annotations

body:
## What

Documents the metrics changes from [agentmail-api#358](https://github.com/agentmail-to/agentmail-api/pull/358) (the Fern follow-up it called out):

- **`GET /metrics/usage`** (+ `/pods/{pod_id}/…`, `/inboxes/{inbox_id}/…`): cumulative usage series per usage type (`storage_bytes`, `message_count`, `thread_count`, `inbox_count`, `domain_count`, `pod_count`). New `UsageType`/`UsagePoint`/`QueryUsageResponse` types; `value` is a `long` since storage bytes can exceed int32. Docs cover the cumulative semantics (running totals, not per-bucket deltas), per-scope field carve-outs, the 90-day retention floor, future-`end` clamping, and the 1000-bucket cap.
- **`GET /metrics/events`** (+ scoped variants): the canonical event-count path, same parameters and response as the old query endpoint. `period` is integer-typed (the API rejects fractional values).
- **Bare `GET /metrics` removed from the spec.** The API keeps the alias responding, so existing clients and SDKs keep working, but the next SDK release drops `client.metrics.query()` in favor of `client.metrics.queryEvents()`. Redirects added from the old `/api-reference/*/metrics/query` pages (and one pre-existing stale redirect destination fixed).
- **Endpoint names are `queryEvents`/`queryUsage`** to match the verb convention used across the spec (list, get, search, query) — SDK methods come out as `query_events`/`query_usage` in Python, `queryEvents`/`queryUsage` in TypeScript.
- **`MetricEventType` synced with the API's `EventTypeSchema`**: adds `message.received.spam`, `message.received.blocked`, `message.received.unauthenticated`, and `domain.verified`; removes `message.delayed`, which the API rejects — it never worked, so SDK code referencing it gets a compile error instead of a runtime 400.
- Changelog entry for 2026-06-12 with Python/TypeScript examples.

Deliberately not documented: the default usage bucket size (requested as a server-side change on [agentmail-api#367](https://github.com/agentmail-to/agentmail-api/pull/367)) — the docs say "defaults to the last 24 hours," which holds before and after that PR.

author: jozanek
body:
Closes #1211 

## Summary

When two `/wallet/payment/send` or `/wallet/transaction/send` requests arrive faster than the mempool acceptance roundtrip, both calls see identical unspent boxes and generate conflicting transactions. This PR closes the race atomically using the wallet actor's existing message-serialization guarantee.

**Root cause:** `GenerateTransaction` selected boxes from the current actor state but never updated it. The state update only came later via the async `ScanOffChain` message, leaving a window where any queued `GenerateTransaction` could pick the same boxes.

**Fix:** On send endpoints, after a successful generation the actor stamps the selected inputs as *reserved* (`ErgoWalletState.reservedInputs`) and calls `context.become` before replying. Because the actor processes one message at a time, the next `GenerateTransaction` already sees the reservation in `walletFilter.notReserved` — no locks, no extra synchronization.

**Reservation lifecycle** (all paths covered):
- `ScanOffChain` (mempool accepted) — converts reservation to normal off-chain state
- `FailedTransaction` / `DeclinedTransaction` events — releases reservation immediately
- Route verify/broadcast failure — explicit `releaseReservedInputs` call before returning the error
- TTL prune on `ScanOnChain` (block scan) — releases any leaked reservation older than 2 blocks

**Scope:** only `/wallet/payment/send` and `/wallet/transaction/send` reserve inputs. `/wallet/transaction/generate` and `/wallet/transaction/generateUnsigned` remain side-effect-free — clients that broadcast externally own their own sequencing.

**Limitations:**
- Two concurrent sends that both supply the **same explicit `inputsRaw`** can still conflict; explicit-input callers are responsible for their own sequencing.
- Reservations are in-memory only — a node restart drops them; the mempool `spentInputs` check resumes protecting against double-spends once readers reconnect.
- A reservation created just before a node crash or pipeline hang will block those inputs for up to 2 blocks (~4 min) before the TTL prune recovers them.

Two new properties in `ErgoWalletSpec`:
1. Second `generateTransactionForSend` fails while first is reserved; `FailedTransaction` event and explicit `releaseReservedInputs` both restore selectability.
2. Reservation survives a block boundary (protecting in-flight sends) and is pruned after `ReservedInputsTtlBlocks = 2` blocks (recovering from crashed pipelines).

author: jeanbaptisterenard
body:
## Summary

- **Problem**: `search_fts` was a plain fts5 table with no `content=` option, causing fts5 to store a full trigram-amplified copy of every transcript body — 172 MB of index for ~13 MB of raw text (13.9x amplification) → 193 MB total DB.
- **Fix**: Convert `search_fts` to an **external-content** fts5 table (`content='search_content'`). A new `search_content` table stores one copy of truncated plaintext (title + body capped at 32 KB). The fts5 shadow tables hold only the trigram index and read columns from `search_content` at query time.
- **`snippet()` is unchanged**: fts5 reads the body for snippet generation directly from `search_content` — no API change, no JS-side snippet building needed.

## Before / after DDL

**Before** (stores full copy inside fts5 shadow tables):
```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE search_fts USING fts5(
  title, body, tokenize='trigram case_sensitive 0'
)
```

**After** (fts5 holds only the trigram index):
```sql
CREATE TABLE search_content (
  rowid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', body TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE search_fts USING fts5(
  title, body, content='search_content', tokenize='trigram case_sensitive 0'
);
```

## `snippet()` rework decision

**Chosen approach: external-content table (`content='search_content'`)**

- `snippet(search_fts, 1, '<mark>', '</mark>', '...', 40)` continues to work unchanged — fts5 reads body from `search_content` on demand, so the query in `searchByType()` needs no modification.
- The alternative (contentless + JS-side snippet extraction from stored body) would require rewriting the query, extracting match offsets, and building previews in application code. Higher complexity, same correctness.
- Body is truncated to `FTS_BODY_MAX_CHARS = 32768` (32 KB) before insertion into `search_content`. This bounds the content table size and is more than enough for meaningful snippets; the most relevant content of a transcript (first prompt, key tool calls) appears early.

## Migration / recreate flag

Migration **v6** (the 6th entry in the `migrations` array in `db.js`):
1. `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS search_fts` — removes the old fat table
2. `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS search_content` — clean slate for existing installs that may have an old/partial version
3. `DELETE FROM search_map` — clears orphaned rowid references
4. `searchFtsRecreated = true` — tells `main.js` (line ~2010) to call `populateCacheViaWorker()`, which triggers a full JSONL re-scan and re-populates both `search_content` and `search_fts` via `upsertSearchEntries`.

The re-index runs in a Worker thread and is non-blocking. For a 193 MB DB (~13 MB raw text, ~1000+ sessions), this takes a few seconds in the background on first launch after update.

## Storage math

| Component | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Raw text in transcripts | ~13 MB | ~13 MB |
| `search_fts` (trigram, 13.9x) | ~172 MB | ~5–8 MB (index only) |
| `search_content` (truncated plaintext) | — | ~13 MB (≤ raw text, body capped at 32 KB) |
| Other tables | ~8 MB | ~8 MB |
| **Total** | **~193 MB** | **~26–29 MB** |

Expected ~6-7x reduction. (Audit estimated ~5x; exact ratio depends on how many transcripts exceed the 32 KB body cap.)

## Tests

14 new static-analysis tests in `test/db-fts-contentless.test.js` (native-module-free, same pattern as `db-daily-activity.test.js`):
- Schema: `search_fts` carries `content='search_content'`; `search_content` has `title` and `body`
- Body truncation constant exists and is applied via `.slice(0, FTS_BODY_MAX_CHARS)`
- Migration v6 drops both tables and sets `searchFtsRecreated = true` (≥ 2 occurrences)
- Delete-by-session / delete-by-folder / delete-by-type all purge `search_content` rows
- `searchUpdateTitle` targets `search_content` (not `search_fts`)
- `snippet(search_fts, 1, ...)` is present in `searchQuery`
- `searchInsertContent` call precedes `searchInsertFts` in `upsertSearchEntriesBatch`
- All public FTS exports are still present in `module.exports`

Full suite: 230/230 pass, 0 fail.

## Needs before merge

**This PR changes search-result semantics and cannot be fully validated without the live 193 MB DB.** It requires:

1. **Human review**: verify the external-content fts5 protocol (insert order, delete order, title update patch) is correct.
2. **Live-DB verification**: the orchestrator / user should apply this to the real `~/.switchboard/switchboard.db`, confirm the DB shrinks as expected, and run a few searches to validate `snippet()` output is correct.

The migration is one-way: after v6 runs, the old fat `search_fts` is gone. A full re-index is required (handled automatically by `searchFtsRecreated = true`). Rolling back would require resetting `db_version` in the `settings` table and manually re-running the old DDL — not recommended without a DB backup.

author: codyborn
body:
## Context

[SWAP-2839](https://linear.app/uniswap/issue/SWAP-2839/uniswapx-order-timeouts-can-still-create-filled-orders): `POST /v1/order` callers intermittently see `400 InputValidationError` / `timeout of 2000ms exceeded` while the order is actually accepted and later filled.

Root cause (confirmed via Datadog trace `2119114652437636364`): the 2s timeout lives in **uniswapx-parameterization-api**'s order-post client (`ORDER_SERVICE_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000`). When this service's post path exceeds 2s, the caller hangs up, but the Lambda (29s budget) finishes — persists the order, notifies fillers — and the order fills. The hard-quote handler then rewrites the timeout into a 400, which TAPI surfaces as `InputValidationError`. Companion fixes: parameterization-api (reconcile-on-timeout, status mapping) and TAPI (timeout headroom, error mapping).

## Changes in this service

1. **Never return an error after the order is persisted.** `logOrderCreatedEvent` / `startOrderTracker` failures now log + emit `PostOrderPostPersistFailure` (alarmable) and still return `201 { hash }` — the signed order is already live and fillable, so erroring just misinforms the caller.
2. **Reuse the `SFNClient`** across invocations in `kickoffOrderTrackingSfn` (was a new client + TLS handshake per order, awaited after persist).
3. **Run the open-order count concurrently with validation** (was a serial DynamoDB query after the on-chain `eth_call`).
4. **Bound RPC calls at 5s** (`RPC_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS`) so a hung provider fails the request *before* the order is accepted, instead of the ethers default of 120s.

## Testing

- `yarn test`: 513/513 pass, including new tests:
  - post-persist SFN kickoff failure still returns the order hash (and logs/alarms)
  - open-order limit still rejects before persist

Request-side half of subset LB + locality preference.

- **Provider-defined subsets**: selectors derived per service from `metadata.endpoint.aether.io/<key>`; the node's vocabulary union travels to consumers as **one shared `header_to_metadata` config over ECDS** (`config_discovery` + non-blocking default) — no consumer declaration, no LDS churn on vocabulary changes. `x-aether-subset-<key>` headers select; strict NO_FALLBACK per selector; headerless traffic unchanged (cluster-level ANY_ENDPOINT).

Not Envoy `zone_aware_lb_config` — that requires O(all-nodes) local-cluster membership, which 004 just retired.

author: leafaar
body:
#### Problem

Durable nonces let a transaction stay valid forever by replacing blockhash expiry with an on chain nonce account. Supporting that means special cases all over the place: a fallback path in the bank's age check, a separate validation and rollback path in the SVM (including the fee payer being the nonce account), five system program instructions, a dedicated retry policy in the send transaction service, and a pile of tests for all of the above. Usage on mainnet is tiny compared to the complexity it carries, and the unbounded replay window is also a recurring source of fee theft style footguns.

#### Summary of Changes

Opening this as a draft to size the change and see what CI thinks of it. Obviously an actual removal would need a SIMD and a feature gate, this is the "what would it look like" half of that conversation.

* bank: a transaction whose blockhash is not in the queue now always fails with `BlockhashNotFound`. No nonce fallback in `check_age`, and `get_fee_for_message` no longer reads nonce data.
* svm: nonce validation and nonce rollback are gone. `CheckedTransactionDetails` loses `nonce_address`, `RollbackAccounts` collapses from a three variant enum to a plain fee payer struct, and `nonce_info.rs` is deleted.
* system program: `AdvanceNonceAccount`, `InitializeNonceAccount`, `AuthorizeNonceAccount` and `UpgradeNonceAccount` now fail with `InvalidInstructionData`. `WithdrawNonceAccount` is kept on purpose so lamports in existing nonce accounts stay recoverable, and the rent floor for nonce shaped system accounts (fee payer validation, `Bank::withdraw`) is kept for the same reason.
* rpc and send transaction service: the durable nonce retry path is removed, nonce transactions no longer get the special last_valid_block_height fallback or the retry until advanced behavior, and the `nonced-tx` stat is gone.

Not touched here, would be follow ups if this ever goes anywhere: the cli nonce commands and offline signing flows, `rpc-client-nonce-utils`, docs, the `blockhash_lamports_per_signature` plumbing (still used by the withdraw path), and the published SDK crates (`solana-nonce`, `solana-nonce-account`, `solana-system-interface`), which this PR only de-uses.

Net: 22 files changed, ~220 insertions, ~4600 deletions.

author: starlein
body:
This pull request introduces important reliability and timeout safeguards to the GitHub Actions security check scripts, ensuring that workflows cannot be stalled by slow or unresponsive GitHub API calls. It also adds a comprehensive skill documentation for managing and verifying Paperclip development workspace services. The most significant changes are grouped below.

**Reliability and Timeout Safeguards in Security Scripts:**

* Added a wall-clock watchdog timer (`startScriptWatchdog`) to `.github/scripts/check-pr-security.mjs` that forces the script to exit with code 0 if it exceeds a 90-second budget, preventing workflow hangs due to stuck API calls. The watchdog is started at script entry and cleared on normal exit. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9e0f636cc7fd3763c0915d23ae5c6f89af6c333726e2ccd5a2e9c787c05f68ddR309-R331) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9e0f636cc7fd3763c0915d23ae5c6f89af6c333726e2ccd5a2e9c787c05f68ddR387)
* Implemented a per-call timeout (`GH_FETCH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 15s) in `ghFetch` (in `.github/scripts/get-bot-token.mjs`), so any slow or hung GitHub API endpoint cannot consume the entire workflow budget. The timeout is customizable per call.
* Capped pagination for searching draft advisories to 20 pages in `findExistingDraftAdvisory`, with a warning if the cap is hit, to prevent large backlogs from stalling the workflow. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9e0f636cc7fd3763c0915d23ae5c6f89af6c333726e2ccd5a2e9c787c05f68ddR246-R253) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9e0f636cc7fd3763c0915d23ae5c6f89af6c333726e2ccd5a2e9c787c05f68ddR268-R273)

**Testing Enhancements:**

* Added tests for the new watchdog timer and per-call timeout logic in `.github/scripts/tests/check-pr-security.test.mjs`, ensuring that the watchdog triggers as expected and that `ghFetch` aborts requests within the specified timeout. Also added a test to verify the draft advisory pagination cap. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-93d540743582673050cdc621635a66c791008abb2b82aaf6d407fea33421b773R148-R160) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-93d540743582673050cdc621635a66c791008abb2b82aaf6d407fea33421b773R336-R380)

**Documentation:**

* Added a detailed skill documentation file `.agents/skills/paperclip-dev-workspace-run-verify-fix/SKILL.md` describing the process, rules, and verification steps for running, verifying, and repairing a Paperclip dev workspace service.

author: eyalz111
body:
## What & why

`link_meeting_to_topics` runs at **extraction (pre-approval)** and blind-inserted mentions + did `meeting_count = meeting_count + 1` with no `(topic_id, meeting_id)` uniqueness; the reject cascade deleted the mention but never decremented the count nor dropped now-empty threads. Two **fabrications** resulted:

- **(a) orphan threads** — a meeting that first-mentions a topic, then is rejected, leaves a thread with `meeting_count=1` and zero mentions, shown in `list_active_threads`.
- **(b) inflated frequency** — reprocessing a meeting inflated the count → "discussed in 6 meetings" when it was 3, surfaced as fact in briefs.

## Fix
- `_create_mention` is **idempotent** on `(topic_id, meeting_id)` — drops any prior mention for the pair before inserting, so a re-extraction *replaces* rather than duplicates.
- `meeting_count` is recomputed from **COUNT(DISTINCT meeting_id)** over the actual mentions (`_distinct_mention_count`) instead of a blind +1; the link flow is reordered to create the mention *before* the recompute.
- `delete_meeting_cascade` captures the affected threads *before* the mentions are deleted, then recomputes each thread's `meeting_count` and **drops any thread left with zero mentions** (both the tombstone and hard-delete paths).

## Tests
- New `tests/test_topic_thread_integrity.py` (3): distinct-count dedup, recompute-not-blind-increment, mention idempotency.
- 406 affected-suite tests green (incl. the existing cascade + topic-state suites).

## Risk
Pure code, no migration. The cascade change is additive (a new cleanup pass after the existing deletes) and clears of the supabase_client regions touched by the other open PRs — clean 3-way merge.

## What this does

Brings the companion sample code in line with the current version of the CircleCI blog tutorial *"Automated testing for Electron applications with continuous integration."* The article was rewritten to use **Playwright** for Electron E2E testing, but this repo still used **Spectron + Jest** (discontinued) on Electron 9 with a legacy CI image. This PR migrates the code to match the article so a reader can follow it end-to-end against this repo with zero contradictions.

## Changes

- **Test framework: Spectron + Jest → Playwright** (`@playwright/test`). Replaces `src/__tests__/AppTest.js` with `src/__tests__/app.spec.js` (the spec from the article).
- **Electron 9.4.0 → 42.4.0**, **Electron Forge 6.0.0-beta.52 → 7.11.2** (adds `forge.config.js` and `preload.js`, the current template layout).
- **`.circleci/config.yml` fixed** — the previous config had three defects that prevented it from running:
  1. `circleci/node:11-browsers` is a legacy image (EOL 2021-12-31) → **`cimg/node:lts-browsers`**.
  2. Added an explicit dependency install and kept caching simple via `npm install`.
  3. The test now runs under **`xvfb-run`** — Electron needs a display to launch in headless CI, which the old config never provided.
- **Tooling: yarn → npm** (drops `yarn.lock`, regenerates `package-lock.json`).
- Left untouched: `README.md` and the unrelated `.github/workflows/main.yml` (project-board automation, not tests).

## Validation

Validated end-to-end in a fresh `cimg/node:lts-browsers` container (Node 24.16, `linux/amd64`):

- `npm install` from the committed lockfile — clean.
- `xvfb-run npm run test` — **1 passed** (the `<h1>` "💖 Hello World!" assertion against the launched Electron app).
- `circleci config validate` + `circleci config process` on the new config — valid.

Tier: **executed in Docker** (not just statically reviewed). The matching CircleCI pipeline run is being triggered separately on this branch.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The accompanying **article update ships separately** (it's edited in the CMS, not in this repo), so prose/screenshot references are handled there. This PR is code-only.
- The new devDependency tree still surfaces some transitive `npm audit` advisories (Electron Forge maker toolchain); these are present in any fresh Forge 7 scaffold and are unrelated to the tutorial's runtime.

author: dzejrou
body:
Closes #155.

## Summary

- `OmniSprite` gains opt-in exported configuration for conventional/lazy animation-resource lookup: `UseConventionalAnimationLookup` (default `false`, so existing actors keep their explicit-resource behavior) and `AssetKey` (e.g. `demon`). When enabled, it derives `res://resources/animations/<asset-key>_spriteframes.tres` and assigns it to the existing `AnimatedSprite2D` when the resource exists.
- A missing conventional resource is treated as an expected development state: the existing pink placeholder shows with no resource-load errors or repeated warnings. Failed lookups are not permanently cached — `TryPlay` retries while frames are still null, the next scene instantiation re-attempts at `_Ready`, and the new public `RefreshConventionalSpriteFrames()` supports an explicit runtime refresh. Invalid non-empty configuration (blank/malformed `AssetKey`, wrong resource type) emits one warning per instance.
- Requesting an unavailable animation no longer leaves the previous valid animation visible: `TryPlay(missingName)` returns `false`, stops the stale animation, and the visual falls back to the static texture (if intentionally configured) or the pink placeholder. A later successful `TryPlay` clears the missing-request state and restores the animated visual. Works for arbitrary animation names; base/status modulation continues to apply to whichever visual is active.
- `AnimatedCharacter.TryPlayDirectionalAnimation` now forwards unresolvable names to `OmniSprite.TryPlay` instead of short-circuiting, so missing attack/cast animations register the placeholder and trigger the lazy lookup retry. `PlayIdleIfAvailable`/`SetAnimationSafe` remain guarded and quiet.
- Purely a visual/resource fallback: no synthesized durations, no action delays; controllers still receive `false` and keep their authored timing.

## Verification

- [x] `dotnet build --verbosity quiet` — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [x] `/Applications/Godot_mono.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --headless --path /Users/jjindrak/Projects/Dotai --quit-after 1` — clean run
- [x] `./run.sh --import` not needed: no new files or UID/import metadata (only edits to existing `.cs` files)

## Manual Test Plan

- [x] Existing actors with explicitly assigned SpriteFrames still animate normally.
- [ ] An `OmniSprite` using lazy lookup with a nonexistent asset key shows the pink placeholder without resource-load errors or repeated warnings.
- [ ] Requesting a missing animation while another valid animation exists switches to the placeholder.
- [ ] Requesting an available animation afterward restores the animated visual.
- [x] Base/status modulation still affects the active animation, static sprite, and placeholder.
- [ ] After a conventional SpriteFrames resource is created/imported for the same asset key, the unchanged lazy `OmniSprite` discovers and plays its available animations on re-instantiation or refresh.
- [ ] Missing animations do not add artificial action delays.

author: mujahidabbas
body:
Adds `shipfastlabs/toolkit-firecrawl`, a new tool package wrapping the [Firecrawl](https://firecrawl.dev) v2 API.

## Tools

| Tool | Endpoint | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `FirecrawlScrape` | `POST /v2/scrape` | Scrape a single URL to clean markdown (also html, rawHtml, links, summary) |
| `FirecrawlMap` | `POST /v2/map` | Discover a site's URLs, with an optional search filter |
| `FirecrawlSearch` | `POST /v2/search` | Web/news/image search, optionally scraping each result into markdown |
| `FirecrawlCrawl` | `POST /v2/crawl` | Start an asynchronous crawl; returns a crawl id |
| `FirecrawlCrawlStatus` | `GET /v2/crawl/{id}` | Poll a crawl and collect its pages |

Firecrawl's crawl is asynchronous, so it's split into a start tool + a status tool (mirroring Firecrawl's own MCP server) rather than blocking inside a single tool call.

## Conventions followed

- `Firecrawl::all()` helper returning `Collection<int, Tool>`, plus a shared `InteractsWithFirecrawl` concern (same pattern as the Exa package)
- `#[Strict]` tools, fluent schema, typed `Request` accessors, errors returned to the model as strings
- Config read from `services.firecrawl.key` (API key) and `ai.toolkit.firecrawl.*` (optional defaults) — no config file or service provider shipped
- Allow-listed `formats`/`sources`, clamped numeric inputs, and a crawl-id format guard so an id can never be used to reach another endpoint
- Root `composer.json` autoload + `replace` wired; README generated with `tools/docgen.sh Firecrawl`

## Quality gates

`composer test` passes locally — Pint, Rector, PHPStan (max), 100% type coverage, 100% code coverage (374 tests, 750 assertions).

Also validated end-to-end in a fresh Laravel app installing the package as a real dependency: every tool exercised against the live Firecrawl v2 API (scrape, map, search, async crawl + status) plus the guardrails, all green.

Happy to adjust scope (e.g. drop crawl/crawl-status for a tighter surface) if you'd prefer.

author: engao2011-coder
body:
## Overview

Three related improvements to the stocks feature and web admin, all driven by real issues observed on-device.

## 1. Stock fetch-status reporting (so the user knows when *they* must fix something)

Previously a symbol that failed to fetch showed an indefinite `...`, indistinguishable from one still loading. Diagnosing two stuck symbols (`SGLH.DE`, `ISWD.DE`) showed Yahoo returns `Not Found / delisted` for them — i.e. invalid symbols the user needs to correct, not a network problem.

- `Quote` now carries a `FetchStatus` (`PENDING` / `OK` / `TEMP_ERROR` / `BAD_SYMBOL`) and a consecutive `failCount`.
- `fetchOne()` classifies each failure: `404` / provider `chart.error` / null result → **BAD_SYMBOL**; network / parse / `price==0` → **TEMP_ERROR**, escalating to BAD_SYMBOL only after repeated misses (avoids flapping on a brief pre-market gap).
- **Backoff fix:** a bad symbol no longer trips the global 60s network backoff, so one bad ticker stops slowing the healthy ones sharing the round-robin.
- **On-screen:** bad symbols render `CHECK SYMBOL` in the alert colour instead of `...`.
- **Web UI:** each symbol input shows a live badge — green `ok`, grey `loading`, red `not found — check symbol` — right where the user edits it.

## 2. System-wide change-metric toggle

The summary page showed daily change while the stocks page showed change vs the 52-week high — inconsistent. New `Settings::stockFromPeak` makes both pages agree, via a shared `Stocks::metricPct()` helper (also used for the "top mover" ranking and the stocks-page sort). Falls back to daily change when a symbol has no 52-week data. Exposed as a checkbox in the web settings.

## 3. Changeable admin password

`Settings::adminPassword` overrides the default MAC-derived device password for **web/OTA Basic Auth only** — the AP (hotspot) join password shown on the setup screen is unaffected. New "Admin Password" section in the settings page with New + Confirm fields and a reset-to-default option. Input is validated (≥ 8 chars, matching confirmation, fits buffer) **before** anything is saved; on failure a new `settingsErrorPage()` explains why and nothing is persisted.

## Reviewer notes

- Firmware builds clean for the `cyd` env (Flash ~91%).
- `IUSE.DE` is intentionally **not** flagged: it returns a valid price, but Yahoo reports its 52-week high equal to the current price, so its from-peak % is a real-but-flat 0%. That's a data quirk, not a fetch error.
- The admin password is stored in plaintext NVS and Basic Auth is sent over plain HTTP — consistent with how saved Wi-Fi passwords already work. Hashing / HTTPS would be a sensible follow-up if stronger protection is wanted.

body:
## Summary

Fixes all findings from a full code review of `main`:

- **Backup/restore data loss (high)** — ZIP and ODS backups now round-trip stock `assetType`, `lastKnownConsensus`, `trailingStopPct`, `trailingStopHighWater`, `manualYieldPct`, and dividend `source`/`confirmed`. Previously a restore reset every ETF/bond to `stock`, erased trailing stop-loss configs and manual yield overrides, and marked unconfirmed auto-fetched dividends as confirmed. Old backups still import (safe defaults, no format-version bump).
- **Quote parse crashes (medium)** — `MarketDataService` uses `Decimal.tryParse` for Yahoo quote and historical close values; non-finite values (NaN/Infinity) no longer throw a `FormatException` past the `DioException`-only catch blocks.
- **WebDAV paths (medium)** — `NextcloudService` routes every method through a single `_davPath()` helper that percent-encodes the username (supports `@`/spaces) and normalises bare paths against the DAV root; PROPFIND hrefs pass through unchanged so existing callers are unaffected.
- **README secret names (medium)** — corrected to match the workflows (`ANDROID_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_B64`, `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`); the wrong names caused the release-signing step to be silently skipped.
- **CI supply-chain hardening (medium)** — all third-party actions in `ci.yml` and `release.yml` pinned to commit SHAs (with `# vN` comments), guarding against tag re-pointing.
- **Dio reuse (low)** — Claude/Groq/Gemini services hold one constructor-injected `Dio` instead of allocating a new client per streaming request.
- **Parser naming (low)** — `skippedFractional`/`_isFractional` renamed to `skippedNoUnit`/`_hasNoUnit` (the check matches empty-unit rows, not fractional shares).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` and `flutter test` pass
- [ ] Export ZIP backup → restore → asset types, trailing stops, manual yield %, and dividend confirmed/source flags survive
- [ ] Restore a backup created before this change → succeeds with defaults

author: matthewsuttles
body:
## Summary

Fixes **finding #3** from the 2026-06-12 performance audit (codebase index: unbounded duplicate edges + full-repo scan per edit — HIGH).

### (a) Duplicate `tests` edges
- `extract_rails_edges` now rebuilds `tests` edges from scratch (`@edges.reject!` on the relationship first), so repeated `update!`/`update_file!` calls stay idempotent instead of appending another full copy of all spec→source edges each time.
- One-time cleanup: `load` now dedupes edges (`uniq`), so index files bloated by older versions self-heal on next load and the cleanup is persisted by the next save.

### (b) Full-tree rescan per file edit
- New `CodebaseIndex#update_file!(path)` re-indexes a single known-changed file: removes its nodes/edges, re-parses it (or just removes if deleted), rebuilds tests edges from in-memory mtimes, and saves. No `Dir.glob`/mtime sweep.
- `Tools::Executor#maybe_update_codebase_index` now calls `update_file!(path)` — the executor already knows exactly which path changed. The full-scan `update!` remains for session start.
- Bonus from the finding: `ruby_files` now prefers `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- '*.rb'` in git repos, so ignored dirs (`tmp/`, `log/`, `coverage/`, `db/`) are no longer indexed; falls back to the glob outside git repos or on error.

## Testing

- New specs: no duplicate tests edges after repeated `update!` and repeated `update_file!`; `update_file!` only touches the changed file's nodes/edges (other files' nodes/edges preserved, deletions handled, persisted to disk, paths outside project root ignored); `load` dedupes bloated index files; git-aware discovery skips gitignored files.
- `bundle exec rspec spec/rubyn_code/index/codebase_index_spec.rb spec/rubyn_code/tools/executor_spec.rb` — 62 examples, 0 failures.
- Full suite: 554 examples, 2 failures — both in `spec/rubyn_code/llm/adapters/integration_spec.rb` and pre-existing on a clean checkout of origin/main (local machine config points the Anthropic adapter at a proxy URL, so WebMock stubs miss). Unrelated to this change.
- `bundle exec rubocop` on touched lib files: no offenses.

author: rickylabs
body:
## Incident

All six Wave 5d PLAN-phase runs (PRs #34–#39, model `openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code`) ended with **zero artifact files on their branches** — only the `chore(openhands): record run trace` commits landed. Investigation (committed trace tails on each branch):

1. The SDK `Conversation` default `max_iteration_per_run=500` was hit mid-exploration in at least 5d3/5d4/5d5/5d6 (`Agent reached maximum iterations limit (500)` in each `agent.log`, ~16–17M input tokens each, never reached the writing phase). 5d1/5d2 "finished" but their final messages admit the artifacts were still pending.
2. The SDK only logs the limit and sets ERROR status — it doesn't raise — and `agent_runner.py` returned 0 unconditionally, so the workflow verdict was `completed`.
3. `ensure_summary()` then asked the cut-off agent to "write the summary now". With its working context condensed, the model **described intended work as delivered** (files "created and committed", `Commit hash: TBD`), producing convincing but false `READY FOR PLAN-EVAL` comments.
4. `git add -A` in *Commit changes back to PR branch* found an empty workspace (nothing was ever written), and the step is skipped entirely when the agent step fails — so even partial work from a future failed run would be discarded.

## Fix

**`.openhands/agent_runner.py`**
- `max_iteration_per_run` now comes from `OPENHANDS_MAX_ITERATIONS` (default 500, clamped 50–3000).
- After `run()`, detect `MaxIterationsReached` (event code, with execution-status fallback) → write a synthesized, truthful "INCOMPLETE (iteration limit)" summary (including the last agent message) and **exit 3** so the workflow verdict is `agent-failed`. The cut-off agent is never asked to summarize — that's the fabrication vector.
- Hardened `SUMMARY_RETRY_PROMPT`: describe only work actually performed; state incompleteness explicitly.

**`.github/workflows/openhands-agent.yml`**
- New trigger token `iterations=<n>` (parsed like `model=`/`output=`) + `iterations` dispatch input → exported as `OPENHANDS_MAX_ITERATIONS`.
- *Commit changes back to PR branch* now runs on `always()` (bootstrap-gated) with an honest `apply partial agent changes (agent outcome: …)` message and push rebase-retry — partial deliverables survive a cut-off run instead of dying with the runner.
- Operational contract now tells agents: create deliverable files EARLY and grow them incrementally; uncommitted workspace files are committed back automatically.

**`.agents/skills/openhands-handoff/SKILL.md`**
- Documents the `iterations=` knob and the "oversized single-run task" pitfall.

## Validation

- `ast.parse` on `agent_runner.py` — OK.
- `@std/yaml` parse of the workflow — OK.
- Behavior change is exercised by the planned re-trigger of the 5d PLAN runs once this merges (workflow + runner are hydrated from the default branch at trigger time, so this must land on `main` first).

author: jeffmhopkins
body:
## What

PR 3 (final Lists slice): a list now renders as a **tappable checklist** in chat instead of plain text. `read_list` surfaces a `list_card` view alongside its text, and the frontend renders it.

## How

- **The loop's `tool_view` emit seam** (new, additive): `ToolOutput` gains an optional `view: ViewPayload` slot, threaded through `_Dispatched`, and `run_stream` yields a `ToolViewEvent` right after the `ToolResultEvent` it belongs to. Every existing tool passes `view=None`, so nothing else changes. (This is the seam the research flagged as missing — the loop surfaced sources/proposals/entities but never a view.)
- **`read_list`** returns `ToolOutput(text, view=list_card(info))` — data-only slots (`{list_id, title, domain, items: [{id, body, checked}]}`), never model-authored markup.
- **Frontend `ListCard`** registered in the view registry: full-bleed rows, theme-drawn checkbox, struck-through done items. An unknown view still renders nothing (the invariant holds).

Read-only for now (it shows state; a tappable checkbox that mutates server state is a follow-up — the model can already re-`read_list` after a change).

## Tests

- Backend: `run_stream` emits a `ToolViewEvent` immediately after its result (and none when the tool has no view); `read_list` carries the `list_card` data.
- Frontend: the registry renders the checklist with checked state and survives an empty/missing payload; the unknown-view invariant still holds.
- Full gate green: **598 backend unit + 282 frontend tests**, ruff/format/pyright/biome/tsc, build.

That completes the Lists feature (schema #114 → tools #115 → this view). Stacked on the now-merged #115.

body:
Fixes #47.

## What
Bump the `/open-review` Revue version floor `REQUIRED_REVUE` from `0.1.1` → `0.2.0` in `skills/open-review/SKILL.md`, and refresh the rationale + both prose mentions.

## Why
Below 0.2.0, opening an **esr/non-main worktree** (a branch tracking e.g. `origin/esr115`) failed with `Error loading diff: spawnSync /bin/sh ENOBUFS` — revue diffed the branch against `origin/main` (mozilla-central), so `base..HEAD` spanned tens of thousands of commits and overflowed git's output buffer. Those worktrees would not open at all. 0.2.0 makes the diff base upstream-aware (prefers the branch's `@{u}`, nearest non-empty merge-base), so esr/beta uplift worktrees show only their own patches.

Source: revue `v0.2.0` (commit `200bbfe2f0cb3c7a8c3f70986180edf74cc555d3`).

author: matthewsuttles
body:
Fixes finding #5 from the 2026-06-12 performance audit: **Synchronous network calls at REPL start — HIGH (bad networks) / MED**.

## Problem

- `AutoSuggest#check` hit `https://rubyn.ai` synchronously on every session start — the `suggested.json` state file only filtered what was *displayed*, not whether the request fired. With the registry client's 10s timeouts, a slow or blackholed network blocked the first prompt for up to ~10–20s. No response caching.
- `VersionCheck#notify` joined its background thread for up to 2s before the prompt on cache miss.

## Fix

- **AutoSuggest** now mirrors the VersionCheck pattern: `start` spawns a background thread, and the new non-blocking `pending_message` is polled between prompts. Its registry client uses a 3s timeout (via a new `timeout:` option on `RegistryClient`; other callers keep 10s).
- **Registry responses are cached** for 24h in `.rubyn-code/suggestions_cache.json`, keyed by a hash of the Gemfile's gem list — so even the background request fires at most once a day per gem set.
- **VersionCheck#notify** defaults to a non-blocking `join(0)`, notifies at most once, and keeps polling until the thread finishes instead of blocking startup.
- **REPL** starts both checks in the background and flushes their results in `flush_startup_notices!` before each prompt read — notices still surface, just never mid-input and never blocking the first prompt.

## Tests

- New specs: AutoSuggest cache write/read, TTL expiry, gem-list invalidation, corrupted-cache fallback; `start`/`pending_message` background contract; VersionCheck notify-once and non-blocking behavior; REPL spec stubbing a registry client that sleeps 10s and asserting `run` returns in under 2s.
- `bundle exec rspec` for the touched specs: 124 examples, 0 failures. Full suite has 23 pre-existing failures in `llm/client_spec` and `tools/spawn_teammate_spec` that also fail on the base commit (unrelated).
- `bundle exec rubocop` on changed files: no new offenses (7 pre-existing in `repl_spec.rb`, also on base).

Closes the biggest PRD gap from the coverage analysis: the Messaging Agent's **highest-value behaviors** — chasing the sales that already leaked — didn't exist. There was no order/payment entity and no quiet-thread state for them to stand on.

## Data layer
- **`Order` model** — DM-pipeline lifecycle `QUOTED → INVOICED → PAID → FULFILLED → CANCELLED`, `Decimal` amounts, `is_unpaid` / `is_overdue(now)` / `hours_overdue(now)`. Money leaks at `INVOICED` — sent but never chased.
- **`Conversation` quiet helpers** — `last_message_at`, `last_direction`, `is_open`, `hours_quiet(now)`.

## Detection (deterministic, not LLM)
`tools/followups.py` decides *which* threads and invoices need attention — the LLM never invents who owes what:
- `find_quiet_threads(quiet_after_hours)` — open threads gone quiet, sorted most-quiet-first, with a `customer_waiting` flag (last message inbound = seller dropped it vs. outbound = customer went silent).
- `find_unpaid_invoices(grace_hours)` — overdue unpaid invoices with **exact** amounts, most-overdue-first.
- Pure `detect_*` functions take an explicit `now` → fully deterministic tests.

## Agent behavior
The Messaging Agent gets both tools (in-process in **both** modes — they read orders/threads, not the catalog, same as `compute_bundle_price`) plus prompt behaviors to draft warm re-engagements and polite payment reminders **grounded in the tools' output** (exact amount/customer, never guessed; "nothing to chase" when empty). Like every specialist, it **cannot send** — drafts stop at the approval gate.

## Surfaced
- `GET /api/followups` and `GET /api/invoices/unpaid` — the seller's work queues, judge-inspectable.
- Seeded at startup with demo quiet threads + an overdue invoice, **plus negative controls** (a fresh thread and a paid order that must NOT surface — proving detection is real).

## Gates (local)
- `ruff` clean · `ruff format --check` clean · `mypy src` clean (37 files)
- **210 passed, 2 skipped** — new `test_tools_followups.py` (thresholds, closed-thread exclusion, customer-waiting flag, sort order, grace window, no-due-date, paid/quoted exclusion, demo seed + controls) and two API-endpoint tests.

## Remaining increment (documented, not silently skipped)
The order/thread store is in-process today (mirroring the decision log + eval-runs). Grounding orders/threads through MongoDB Atlas is the next write-path increment — called out in ARCHITECTURE.md implementation-status.

## Problem
`get_dap_binary` passed raw binary names (`"flutter"`, `"dart"`, `"fvm"`) 
as commands without resolving them against the host's PATH. WASM extensions 
cannot read `$PATH` directly, so the debug adapter failed to launch on remote

## Fix

local and remote worktrees. This is consistent with how `language_server_binary` 
already resolves the `dart` binary.

author: cbspire
body:
Turns the TipTap editor into a Notion/Confluence-style writing experience, replacing the button-heavy classic toolbar UX.

![Editor overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cbspire/tiptap-wp-editor/claude/tiptap-notion-editor-q1v9cj/docs/screenshots/editor-overview.png)

## What's new

### `/` slash commands
Typing `/` opens a filterable block palette: Text, Heading 1–3, bulleted/numbered list, quote, code block, divider, Image (Media Library), **Upload image**, read-more, shortcode, raw HTML. Arrow keys + Enter to pick; keep typing to filter (`/im` → image blocks). Built on the official `@tiptap/suggestion` utility with a dependency-free DOM menu (no tippy/popper).

![Slash menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cbspire/tiptap-wp-editor/claude/tiptap-notion-editor-q1v9cj/docs/screenshots/slash-menu.png)

### Floating formatting bar
Selecting text shows a bubble menu: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inline code, H2/H3, quote, and an inline link editor (replaces the old `window.prompt`).

![Bubble menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cbspire/tiptap-wp-editor/claude/tiptap-notion-editor-q1v9cj/docs/screenshots/bubble-menu.png)

### Image upload
Drag & drop or paste images into the editor — they upload to the Media Library via `POST /wp/v2/media` (REST nonce), show a pulsing placeholder while uploading, then become a standard `wp-image-{id}` image. On failure the placeholder is removed and an error notice shown; content is never saved pointing at a blob URL. Gated on the `upload_files` capability.

### Block drag handles
Hovering a block shows the Notion ⠿ grip (drag to reorder via ProseMirror's native move + dropcursor, click to select) and a `+` button that inserts a block below and opens the slash menu. Hidden on touch devices.

### Placeholder + slim toolbar
Empty blocks hint *"Type "/" for commands…"*. The top toolbar is slimmed to essentials (B/I/U, image, read-more, undo/redo) and kept mainly for mobile, where hover/selection UX is limited. The AI menu (WP 7.0+) now mounts in the toolbar row.

## Why custom extensions instead of TipTap's Notion template
TipTap's official Notion-like template depends on **TipTap Pro** packages (drag handle, slash UI) served from their private npm registry under a non-GPL license — a WordPress.org plugin can't ship those. This PR uses the official open-source building blocks (`@tiptap/suggestion`, `@tiptap/extension-placeholder`, StarterKit's dropcursor) with thin custom glue, plus the WP-specific pieces (Media Library REST upload, shortcode/read-more blocks) that no template provides.

## Tests & tooling
- Vitest + jsdom setup (`vitest.config.ts`, ProseMirror DOM shims); **24 tests** covering slash item filtering/commands, the upload helper (nonce header, error paths), and the upload placeholder lifecycle (patch on success, remove on failure, no transient attrs in saved HTML).
- `demo/` — standalone build of the real editor on a plain HTML page (no WordPress), used for UI work and to generate the README screenshots in `docs/screenshots/`.
- Bundle: `editor.js` is **105 KB gzipped** (target < 150 KB). New deps are all MIT TipTap packages already in the family: `@tiptap/suggestion`, `@tiptap/extension-placeholder`, `@tiptap/pm`.

## Verification
- `npm test` — 24/24 passing
- `npm run build` — clean
- Screenshots above were captured from the real built editor running in Chromium (slash menu, filtering, bubble menu, drag handle, placeholder all verified live)

author: evanve5420
body:
## Summary

Scheduled CronAgents runs each get a fresh, isolated `COPILOT_HOME` whose `mcp-config.json` was always written empty (`{"mcpServers": {}}`), so agents' declared MCP tools (teams, mail, etc.) never loaded unattended. Only `ado-mcp` worked, via the separately authenticated `az` CLI fallback.

This adds a per-agent **`mcpServers`** registration field that selects which MCP servers a run receives from the user's `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:

| Value | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `null` / omitted | All servers (copied verbatim, after JSON validation) |
| `[]` | None — built-in tools only (prior behavior) |
| `["a","b"]` | Only the named servers (plus the file''s `inputs`) |

## Implementation

- **`Resolve-RunMcpConfig`** (new, in `CopilotHome.ps1`) builds the per-run config; **`Initialize-RunCopilotHome`** writes it.
- **`ConfigLoader.ps1`** parses the field; **`Invoke-ScheduledAgent.ps1`** wires it through to the run.
- Empty arrays are preserved via explicit `[string[]]` variables so the "no servers" opt-out cannot silently collapse to "all servers" (the classic `@()` → `$null` if-expression collapse).
- Malformed, empty, or missing source configs degrade gracefully to built-in tools only, with a warning.

## Docs & schema

Updates `cronagents-agent.schema.json`, `guide/configuration.md`, and the `creating-agents` skill (`SKILL.md` + `REGISTRATION-FIELDS.md`) to stay in sync, including a security note that the user MCP config (which may contain secrets/inputs) is duplicated into retained run directories.

## Testing

- `CopilotHome.Tests.ps1` — 25 passed (new coverage for null/`[]`/subset + graceful degradation).
- `ConfigLoader.Tests.ps1` — 68 passed (field parsing through the full config path).

## Reviewer note

The effective default for agents that **omit** `mcpServers` changes from "no servers" to "all servers" (a least-privilege → most-privilege shift). This is intentional per the design and documented with a security note, but pre-existing scheduled agents will start receiving all of the user''s MCP servers on their next run.

author: dakejahl
body:
## Summary
USB gadget mode for the `justapi-cm5` target: the USB-C flashing port doubles as a USB Ethernet adapter, so `ssh pi@192.168.55.1` (or `just-a-pi.local`) works over a single cable with no host-side drivers on Linux, macOS, or Windows 11. A baked `ark-usb-mode` toggle flips the port back to USB2 host mode (reboot to apply) when that's needed instead.

## Problem
A headless Just-A-Pi with no Ethernet or Wi-Fi configured is unreachable out of the box, and stock Trixie pins the CM5 dwc2 controller to `dr_mode=host`, so the USB-C port can't act as a device while Linux runs. The image already ships Raspberry Pi's `rpi-usb-gadget`, but it is g_ether-based (RNDIS needs a manual driver install on Windows), randomizes MACs every boot, uses 10.12.194.1, and can only be enabled on a booted system via cloud-init plus an extra reboot — not bakeable in the build chroot.

## Solution
New `TARGET_USB_GADGET=1` target key installs `files/usb-gadget/`: a configfs CDC NCM gadget script with stable per-unit MACs derived from the SoC serial, a oneshot systemd unit, a NetworkManager shared-mode profile (192.168.55.1/24 — the Jetson-style address ARK users know — DHCP for the host, NAT to the Pi's uplink), and the `ark-usb-mode {gadget|host|status}` operator toggle at `/usr/local/bin`. `justapi-cm5` opts in and swaps the stock `[cm5]` dwc2 overlay to `dr_mode=peripheral`; everything the gadget needs (dwc2/libcomposite/NCM modules, dnsmasq-base, nftables) is already in the base image, so nothing is installed.

Tradeoff: while Linux runs, the USB-C's USB 2.0 pins serve one role at a time — gadget by default, host via `sudo ark-usb-mode host` + reboot (rpiboot flashing, the JST-GH USB2 host port, and the RP1 SuperSpeed lanes are unaffected either way). The carrier's USB-C has no CC resistors, so only A-to-C cables work — documented in the README. Pending bench validation that the carrier's USB-C works in device mode at all (same electrical topology as the documented rpiboot eMMC flashing path).

author: talchain
body:
## Row

**V5-LANE-B-STRUCTURAL-01** — improve canonical J1 explain experience with the hybrid validation beat. Decision approved: **Option 3 (Hybrid)** — keep the rich J1 LLM narrative, deterministically append the contract-safe validation beat.

⚠️ **Do NOT merge without Paul.** Full external **Codex review required** before merge (user-facing composition change). Pause for Paul/ChatGPT-led review.

## Why

#256 (`11ee0bcd`) landed the "what to validate" beat on the deterministic advice-gate path, but live smoke showed it only reaches **J1b** ("Explain the results."). Canonical **J1** ("Why?") matches no deterministic pattern, routes via the LLM `explain_results` handler, and uses Sonnet's `answer_text` verbatim — so J1 users got the rich narrative but never the validation beat.

## What

Hard constraints honoured: **no router change, no prompt/PMS change, no route swap for bare "Why?"**, J1b advice-gate output **byte-for-byte preserved** (253/253 pins green, helper extraction only), precondition/stale/missing/degraded copy untouched.

1. **`coaching/validation-priority.ts` (new, shared SSOT)** — #256's `describeValidationPriority` + `VALIDATE_LINK_EVIDENCE` moved verbatim; the advice gate re-imports. Adds the shared renderability predicate and a **standalone variant** that names both link endpoints (`the link from 'X' to 'Y'`) because the in-flow copy's "that link" would dangle after free LLM prose. Ladder unchanged: named fragile link → top driver → **omit** (never filler). ID-shaped/blank labels are never rendered.
2. **Dedup guard** (`decideValidationBeat`) — documented **coarse heuristic**: skip the link variant ONLY when the answer contains **both endpoint labels AND validation/evidence/checking vocabulary**; labels alone never skip. If skipped, the driver rung fires only when it adds a distinct priority; if that would also duplicate → `dedup_skipped`. Bias: under-suppression over over-suppression (a duplicated beat is mildly templated; a wrongly suppressed beat silently deletes the feature). **Codex: please review this heuristic against captured real outputs.**
3. **`AnalysisProjectionSummary.fragile_edges`** (optional, additive) — label pass-through from `ContextPackAnalysis`, pre-filtered renderable (F.6, no derivation). The chip-click intermediate already supplied the field; the builder was dropping it.
4. **`explain_results` handler** — execute-verdict path only. Sonnet-valid → standalone beat appended as a final paragraph (post-dedup). Fallback → same beat placed before the closing nudge (no dedup needed: the deterministic fallback never states a validation priority).
5. **Mechanism observability** — `HandlerOutcome.__validation_beat` (internal channel, `__plot_timings` pattern) mirrored by the turn-executor to the new `v5.explanation.validation_beat` event: `appended` / `dedup_skipped` / `omitted` + matched evidence (link endpoints / driver label / omission reason), so smoke asserts the **mechanism**, not just surface text.

### Schema hard rule (addendum) — follow-up declared

`ExplainResultsResultSchema` is `.strict()` in the **generated `@talchain/schemas` package** (vendored `0.13.0` tarball). A persisted `result.validation_beat_appended` field would fail fact validation without a package release — **blocked behind V5-CI-01** (GitHub Packages auth). Per the addendum, that sub-task stopped; telemetry (above) is the approved path. **Follow-up:** add the field to `@talchain/schemas` once V5-CI-01 lands.

## External Codex review prompt addendum

Review PR #267 with these additional focus points:

1. **Human-read acceptance risk**
   - Do not treat telemetry saying `appended` as sufficient proof of user-facing success.
   - The real risk is that Sonnet's rich narrative and the deterministic validation beat both state similar advice in different words, making the answer feel repetitive or bolted on.
   - Review whether the combined J1 output is likely to read as coherent coaching, not a pasted-on mechanism.

2. **Egress-strip proof for `__validation_beat`**
   - Do not accept the `__` prefix naming convention as proof.
   - Verify the actual egress/response-building mechanism strips or excludes `HandlerOutcome.__validation_beat` from the user-visible response, wire response, persisted handler facts, and public blocks/chips/suggested actions.
   - Compare to how `__plot_timings` is handled.
   - If the strip/exclusion mechanism is not explicit and covered by tests, flag it.

3. **Schema path and V5-CI-01**
   - Confirm PR #267 correctly avoided adding `validation_beat_appended` to `ExplainResultsHandlerFact.result`.
   - Confirm the schema follow-up is correctly gated on V5-CI-01 because `@talchain/schemas` package/auth must be reliable before generated schema work resumes.
   - Do not ask this PR to mutate generated schemas.

4. **Post-merge acceptance**
   - Confirm the smoke plan must include telemetry mechanism check: `appended`, `dedup_skipped`, or `omitted` with matched evidence.
   - Include at least one engineered append-fires case.
   - Human-read the actual combined J1 answer against V5-COMP-01 for coherence and non-redundancy.
   - Confirm J1b no regression.
   - Confirm J3 no false-stale deflection.
   - Confirm nine-journey no-regression versus `11ee0bc`.

5. **Cross-lane overlap with D1-SHAPE**
   - PR #267 touches `turn-executor.ts` for telemetry forwarding.
   - D1-SHAPE will also touch `turn-executor.ts` around STEP 7.
   - Confirm PR #267's edit is semantically independent from the D1 commit-graph merge-back.
   - Require whichever PR lands second to rebase and rerun relevant turn-executor suites.

## Verification

- Touched suites **357/357**: advice gate **253/253** (incl. #256 pins — byte-stability proof), handler 35 (link append / dedup skip / distinct-driver / omit / ID-guard / fallback parity / strict-schema round-trip / no-beat-on-precondition), fallback, projection, new helper 21.
- Full `src/orchestrator-v5` scope: **same 11 pre-existing failures as clean base `11ee0bcd`** (verified by stash-rerun) — net zero.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` clean; full `tsc` error count **461 == base**; eslint clean on touched files.

## Post-merge smoke plan (mechanism-level, per addendum)

On staging `/orchestrate/v2/turn` with a fresh-analysis scenario:
- **J1** "Why?" → narrative preserved + beat; read `v5.explanation.validation_beat` for `appended` + evidence (engineer at least one case where Sonnet does not pre-empt the priority so the append branch fires live).
- **J1b** "Explain the results." → advice-gate output byte-comparable to `11ee0bc`.
- **J3** freshness follow-up → no false-stale deflection.
- Nine-journey no-regression vs `11ee0bc` (J2/J5/J5c/J6; J4/J9 stay Track-S-gated; J7 stays V5-GROUND-01).

author: mfittko
body:
## Summary
- reopen the Copilot loop at round cap when the PR head changed since the last submitted Copilot review, all prior threads are resolved, and loop-state CI is green or credibly green
- fail closed for older/incomplete snapshots that omit the current-head review signal instead of inferring a head advance
- let `request-copilot-review.mjs` auto re-request from live PR facts without forcing operators onto `--force-rerequest-review`, while still honoring refinement config like low-signal suppression
- add regression coverage for loop-state interpretation, detector auto-detect/input modes, request flow, and handoff routing; update script docs to match

## Scope and context
Issue #746 found that clean PRs could still dead-end at the review round cap after follow-up fixes landed on a new head SHA. This change keeps the hard cap for same-head or still-unresolved review states, re-opens the loop when new commits land after all prior Copilot feedback is resolved and the updated head is clean again, and avoids reopening from incomplete legacy snapshots that do not prove the head changed.

## Changes
- `packages/core/src/loop/copilot-loop-state.mjs`
  - route round-cap + clean-thread + green/credibly-green + new-head cases back to `ready_to_rerequest_review`
  - require an explicit `copilotReviewOnCurrentHead` signal before treating round-cap cleanup as a head-advanced rerequest case
  - keep same-head or incomplete clean cases on `round_cap_clean_fallback`
- `scripts/github/request-copilot-review.mjs`
  - detect round-cap auto-rerequest eligibility from live PR facts and review threads before returning `round_cap_reached`
  - reuse the full refinement config for that eligibility check, so low-signal suppression still applies at round cap
  - preserve `--force-rerequest-review` as override for other new-commit round-cap cases
- tests
  - `packages/core/test/copilot-loop-state.test.mjs`
  - `test/loop/detect-copilot-loop-state-auto-detect.test.mjs`
  - `test/loop/detect-copilot-loop-state-input-modes.test.mjs`
  - `test/github/request-copilot-review.test.mjs`
  - `test/loop/copilot-pr-handoff.test.mjs`
- docs
  - `scripts/README.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `detect-copilot-loop-state.mjs` recognizes the resolved-comments + new-commits pattern at round cap as a non-terminal re-request eligible state.
- [x] The new state transitions naturally to `waiting_for_copilot_review` when `request-copilot-review.mjs` is called without `--force-rerequest-review`.
- [x] `run-watch-cycle.mjs` and `copilot-pr-handoff.mjs` handle the new state correctly by continuing into watch instead of stopping.
- [x] The change is covered by unit/integration tests in the loop-state test suite.
- [x] `maxCopilotRounds` still blocks same-head or unresolved-thread cases.

## Definition of done
- round-cap re-request behavior is deterministic and test-backed
- current same-head and unresolved-thread guardrails remain enforced
- incomplete legacy snapshots fail closed instead of inferring a head advance
- low-signal refinement still suppresses re-requests where configured
- CLI docs match the implemented request behavior
- validation passes on the PR head

## Non-goals
- changing the default `maxCopilotRounds` setting
- allowing unlimited Copilot rerequests
- relaxing unresolved-thread or CI requirements for rerequesting Copilot
- changing unrelated PR follow-up or merge-gate behavior

- npm run verify

body:
@
## Loop B — Helix gap #3: signal supports/contradicts stance

### Why
`scenario_calibration` only moved probability **up** — every signal corroborated, clamped to `>= prior` — so a contradicting development could never refute a scenario. The module documented this as the intended follow-up: *"Downward calibration needs scenario-relative stance detection — an explicit follow-up."* Per the Helix CI/wargaming analysis (`raw_notes.md` / COORDINATION §7.1 H-g), this is the keystone for *"contradictions are often the insight."*

### What (reuse-first, grounded, zero-regression)
Grounded in the existing **`signals.direction`** column (DB-checked `positive`/`negative`/`neutral`) — not guessed:
- A **negative** signal about a **rival** now **contradicts** a `Competitive pressure: <rival>` scenario → pulls probability toward the floor (0.05).
- Positive/neutral/unknown still **support** (toward 0.95). Focal-asset scenarios (no polarity model yet) treat every signal as corroboration → **no regression**.
- `signal_stance()` pure classifier; `calibrate_scenario_prob` reads `s[stance]`, defaulting to `supports` so old callers are unchanged; bounded `[0.05, 0.95]`; the note reports the corroborating/contradicting mix + raised/lowered.

No new tables, no new machinery — extends the PB-H14 loop and a column that already exists.

### Tests / evidence
- **11 new** stance tests + **38 existing** calibration tests green.
- Prod (read-only probe): `signals.direction` populated — **408 positive / 108 negative / 109 neutral / 66 null** — so refutation is grounded and activates when a rival gets a post-derivation negative signal. 0 of the 3 current competitive scenarios have one yet → capability is **live but not yet fired** (honest; no fabricated downward move).

### Follow-ups (tracked, separate)
COORDINATION §7.1 H-b (persist a `scenario_probability_history` time-series — calibration still only stores a `note`) and focal-asset scenario polarity.

body:
## Problem

With `render_mode = direct-to-documenso`, clicking **Originate Mandate** lands on `/app/m/<draft-id>` and the page is **blank** — the shell appears to vanish. Under `through-docraptor` the full Engagement Proposal renders. Root cause: [Mandate.tsx](apps/platform-app/src/routes/app/Mandate.tsx) hard-returned `<div aria-hidden className="min-h-[60vh]" />` for the direct-to-documenso branch (PR #118, "display TBD").

## Fix

Replace the blank body with a new `MandateDraftShell` that renders the **engagement-proposal structure** with blank data slots:

- Reuses the shared `DocumentFrame` chrome — utility bar (`Catalyst-Driven Origination` / `Strategic Origination Mandate`), the `Engagement Proposal` letterhead header, the trust-strip footer.
- Mirrors the `MandateEditor` body scaffold — **Prepared for**, the **Strategic Origination Mandate** term rows (Infrastructure Fee · Term · Billing · Total), **Execution** / **Sign the mandate**, **Confirm & originate**.
- Every data slot is blank (`—`); the Sign / Confirm actions are inert (`disabled`).
- Static + dataless: takes no `shell`, fetches nothing, so it can never 404 or flash.

The draft's concrete values (pricing, prepared-for, success-fee tiers) and the sign/confirm wiring are a deliberate separate step — this change is purely the structural shell so the page is no longer empty.

## Scope

- `apps/platform-app/src/proposals/MandateDraftShell.tsx` (new)
- `apps/platform-app/src/routes/app/Mandate.tsx` — swap the blank div for `<MandateDraftShell housing="cockpit" />`
